author: ACG
title: The General Strike in Spain on November 11th
content:
The 24-hour general strike that took place on Wednesday, November 11

th

, involving around 4 million people, had its origins in the big protests in October against the housing policies of the Socialist Party (PSOE) government, led by Pedro Sanchez, in alliance with the left Movimiento Sumar, especially against the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal which eventually led to her death.  Rents have risen by 45% and house prices by 68%. Between 2008 and 2015 there were 500,000 evictions. These protests themselves involved millions turning out in many parts of Spain.


Sanchez responded by dissolving his government and calling for snap elections on November 29

th

. He hoped to blackmail the movement by offering a false alternative of supporting the PSOE government, or opening the way to a government of the Popular Party-PP (with its roots in Francoism) and the fascist Vox party.


A movement towards organising a general strike began with the housing movement, especially around the Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos (Tenants Union) of Madrid, spreading to Catalonia. It coordinated with the syndicalist and anarcho-syndicalist unions CGT and CNT (100,000 members and 15,000 members respectively. These jointly organised neighbourhood strike committees, which ensured massive strike pickets on the day.


The leadership of the union centrals UGT, controlled by the PSOE, and in alliance with Sumar, and the CCOO, controlled by the Stalinists, then were forced to swing in behind the strike call, hoping to gain control of the movement.


This is in the context not just of the housing crisis, but of wages remaining stagnant, and rising inflation. The cost of living has shot up considerably, by at least 45%, with big food, and energy increases. In the meantime, corporate profits have risen 40%.


Sanchez used the vote in Congress (Parliament), where a Housing Decree, reforms announced to head off the housing movement, was blocked by the PP, Vox, and the Catalan right-wing party Junts. The PSOE was re-elected in 2023, on a promise to halt the housing crisis. A huge building boom led to a slump, but instead of socialising the huge number of empty houses, the PSOE government sold them cheaply to investment bankers. Promised rent controls and increases in social housing were not enacted, whilst tax breaks were given to the big landlords.


The Sanchez government and its allies in the UGT and CCOO leadership hoped to use the mobilisation to stay in power. However, the four million who turned out on the day, are acting against the policies of the PSOE-Sumar government, disgusted by both the crises in housing and the cost of living. On the day, the various unions influenced by anarchism and anarcho-syndicalism mobilised their members, as did the many neighbourhood housing action committees, which have a membership of 10,000.


Despite the bad weather in some regions, there were massive demonstrations and large blockades in many towns and cities. The biggest was in Madrid, despite teeming rain, followed by that in Barcelona. The strike began at midnight. Blockades were put up on major highways, and large workplaces were picketed. Strikes heavily impacted industries in Madrid, Catalonia, Valencia, and the Basque country, and less so in other cities and provinces.


The railways were completely closed down, with a strike beginning the day before. Big chain stores were picketed and shut down, including supermarkets like Mercadona, Adidas, Benetton, El Cortes Ingles and Zara.


Of course, the forces of the State intervened, with the cops attacking demonstrations and making at least 115 arrests.


On the day after the mobilisation, Sanchez introduced another two decrees that were almost identical to the rejected ones. They were presented to a smaller parliamentary council on Thursday, giving the government a better chance of passing the laws. The first decree passed narrowly and includes a measure extending protections against evictions for tenants deemed by social services to be in a precarious financial or social position, as long as regional authorities cannot offer them an alternative residence. Another measure attempted to reduce real estate speculation by stopping any company involved in the real estate market from buying properties for less than 70 percent of their value.


However, it was rejected. again narrowly, after the centre-right Basque party voted with the right-wing bloc after having supported the other decree. The PP …

author: anred
title: MetroGAS: una distribuidora, un negocio y responsabilidades que no se tercerizan
content:
La responsabilidad de la muerte de un obrero y una treiuntena de heridos con gravedad en la explosión tras la fuga de gas en Remedios de Escalada no puede reducirse a la empresa Exgadet que operaba la tuneladora. MetroGAS es la distribuidora que tiene a su cargo la red y el servicio en buena parte del Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires. La contratación de una firma externa no la exime de garantizar que las obras se realicen bajo condiciones adecuadas ni de supervisar los procedimientos de seguridad. Los trabajadores venían advirtiendo de las malas condiciones de trabajo. ¿Como operó el lobby Vila Manzano en la justicia? . Por ANRed


La propia empresa cuenta con un Programa de Prevención de Daños que establece responsabilidades compartidas entre quienes ejecutan excavaciones y la distribuidora. MetroGAS debe garantizar la integridad de la red y brindar asistencia técnica durante las obras. Por eso, la investigación debe establecer qué controles realizó sobre Exgadet, qué instrucciones había impartido y cómo respondió cuando recibió el aviso de la rotura.


La actuación de la distribuidora quedó especialmente comprometida por lo sucedido después de las 9.44. Según la reconstrucción municipal, recibió el aviso de la fuga, envió una cuadrilla y no activó el sistema local de emergencias. La decisión de mantener el episodio bajo control de la propia empresa, sin alertar a los organismos municipales, dejó expuesta a toda la población de la zona.


Mientras tanto, el Gobierno nacional avanza con un esquema de desregulación y reorganización del mercado energético que favorece la concentración empresarial y la rentabilidad privada. En agosto de 2026, YPF acordó vender el 70% de MetroGAS a Edenor por 780 millones de dólares. La operación fue impulsada por el grupo empresario integrado por José Luis Manzano, Daniel Vila y Mauricio Filiberti, y quedó sujeta a las autorizaciones correspondientes.


La operación se inscribe en un proceso más amplio de concentración de empresas de servicios públicos. Edenor, que ya controla la distribución eléctrica en una extensa zona del AMBA, busca incorporar a su estructura una de las principales distribuidoras de gas del país. Al mismo tiempo, el nuevo marco regulatorio energético contempla revisiones tarifarias y una eventual extensión de la concesión de MetroGAS hasta 2047.


En este escenario, la pregunta por los controles adquiere una dimensión política. ¿Qué lugar ocupa la seguridad de los usuarios y trabajadores en un modelo donde los servicios esenciales se organizan alrededor de grandes negocios privados? ¿Quién garantiza que la búsqueda de eficiencia y rentabilidad no termine descargando los costos sobre quienes trabajan y viven en los territorios?


La desregulación no significa solamente modificar normas o reducir la intervención estatal. También implica discutir qué controles se mantienen, quién los ejecuta y qué capacidad tienen los organismos públicos para fiscalizar a empresas que manejan infraestructuras fundamentales para la vida cotidiana.


Dos directivos de MetroGAS y una investigación que debe avanzar


La gravedad de lo ocurrido llevó a la fiscal Yanina Estévez, de la UFI N.º 6 de Lanús, a disponer inicialmente la detención de dos responsables jerárquicos de MetroGAS que se encontraban en el lugar. La medida fue informada por el director de Defensa Civil municipal y estuvo vinculada al presunto incumplimiento de los protocolos de emergencia.


Posteriormente, fuentes judiciales informaron que los dos directivos habían sido trasladados para su identificación y puestos preventivamente a resguardo, y aclararon que no estaban formalmente detenidos ni aprehendidos. La diferencia entre ambas versiones deberá quedar esclarecida en el expediente.


La investigación debe determinar qué hicieron los responsables de la distribuidora durante la hora que transcurrió entre la detección de la fuga y la explosión. También deberá establecer quién decidió que la situación estaba controlada, por qué no se dio intervención inmediata a los servicios municipales y qué responsabilidad tuvieron los directivos en la cadena de decisiones.


No se trata solamente de establecer quién rompió el caño. La responsabilidad empresarial incluye la prevención, la supervisión de las contratistas y la respuesta ante una emergencia. Son obligaciones que no desaparecen cuando una empresa decide tercerizar sus trabajos.


El lobby de Vila-Manzano para liberar a los directivos

author: Nathalie Levey
title: Even When Domestic Workers Have Labor Protections, Claiming Them Isn’t Easy
content:
For immigrant domestic workers, asserting their rights can lead to dangerous forms of retaliation.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

For seven years, Teresa tended to another family’s children inside a Manhattan home. She now calls it the worst job of her life. They kept meticulous logbooks of the hours she put in, an unwitting manifestation of a household that tallied everything and answered for none of it.

Teresa first began working in Mexico when she was 13 years old, yet in all those years, no employer wore on her like this one. It was the family’s rule that she could not even speak to the other nannies at the playground. So through long afternoons she was mostly mute, laughing without a word and saving what she wanted to say for when she was out of sight. And beneath this stranglehold, the family wasn’t even paying her what she was owed.

Help arrived when a friend mentioned that the National Domestic Workers Alliance (NDWA) ran free training sessions for nannies. There, she learned a worker holds incontestable rights no matter their immigration status. And she realized the family’s ongoing pattern of underpayment was wage theft. Organizers told her she could fight back, but a claim lives or dies on proof through documentation of hours worked, cash receipts saved, and money exchanged as it passed from their hands to hers.

Then she remembered the logbooks.

“It occurred to me to grab the books without permission, knowing that they trusted me,” she said. “I took them home, took copies for the years I was there, 2017 until 2024. Then I returned the books to their place and didn’t touch anything else.”

“That’s been my most powerful weapon now to confront them,” she said.

Teresa, who is using a pseudonym for fear of retribution, moved to New York in 2003 and has made her living through housecleaning and childcare, which enabled her to put her own children through private school in the U.S. She knew the wealthy family whose logbooks she copied could destroy her, and she dreaded going to court, but she persevered with her claim “to show that it can be done.” Her former employer even agreed to an early settlement until the family’s lawyer went silent, forcing Teresa’s attorney to bring the case before a judge.

Teresa is one worker living through a pivotal moment for American domestic work, a national reckoning about whether existing protections translate into substantive security. Over the past 15 years in cities and states across the East Coast, nannies, house cleaners, and home care workers have secured once-impossible protections that promise minimum wage, written contracts, and safeguards against retaliation. But while these rights have been codified, exercising them safely is a fraught prospect for those whose livelihoods are jeopardized once they speak out.

Marrisa Senteno, director of NDWA’s New York chapter, has spent a decade building New York’s enforcement program, and recognizes that a statute does not guarantee instantaneous progress. “A law being passed isn’t a magic wand. You pass it, and things don’t just appear,” she said.

For immigrant workers, a household withholding wages can resort to more dangerous forms of retaliation, weaponizing their legal status to sidestep accountability. Nicole Kligerman, who founded the Pennsylvania chapter of NDWA in 2018, has witnessed a single reprisal hush an entire workforce. “That happens to one person, and everybody knows about it immediately,” she said. And when the city is sluggish in its investigation and a claim stalls, Kligerman added, “that’s a real chilling effect.”

When New York passed the country’s first Domestic Workers’ Bill of Rights in 2010, the measure was billed as a national model for bringing labor law into the private home. The state’s domestic workforce — roughly 328,000 people in 2021, 63% of them immigrants and 92% women — gained overtime pay, a weekly day of rest, and protection from harassment. But six years later, Senteno could count the claims filed under the law on one hand, and she recalled state officials concluding, “Well, there must not be cases.”

Enforcement at the state labor department is complaint-driven, Senteno said, meaning an investigation typically begins only when a worker comes forward. Isolated inside their employers’ homes, domestic workers rarely have someone who can help them recognize a violation as it happens, and many have “zero knowledge” of how …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Pauny no se presentó a la audiencia y crece la incertidumbre sobre la continuidad de los 450 empleados de su planta de Córdoba
content:
Pauny, la fábrica de tractores, debía presentar un plan para afrontar la deuda salarial y reactivar la producción en la fábrica de Las Varillas. Lucas Sarmiento, titular de la UOM San Francisco, aseguró que adeuda dos meses de sueldos.


La crisis de Pauny sumó un nuevo capítulo este jueves, luego de que la empresa no se presentara a la audiencia convocada por la Secretaría de Trabajo de Córdoba para abordar la deuda salarial con sus empleados y la paralización de la actividad productiva en la planta de Las Varillas.


En diálogo con Cadena 3, Lucas Sarmiento, secretario general de la Unión Obrera Metalúrgica (UOM) de San Francisco, cuestionó la decisión de la firma y rechazó los argumentos expuestos en un comunicado empresarial, en el que se responsabilizó a los trabajadores por las dificultades para retomar la actividad.


La audiencia tenía como objetivo que la empresa presentara un plan para afrontar las obligaciones salariales pendientes y una propuesta productiva que permitiera reactivar la fábrica, prácticamente paralizada desde hace entre tres y cinco meses.


“Los trabajadores están acá en planta esperando justamente una propuesta de la patronal para reactivar rápidamente la empresa. Eso no sucede”, sostuvo Sarmiento.


Sarmiento precisó que Pauny tiene alrededor de 450 trabajadores directos y que la deuda con el personal no se limita a los últimos dos meses de salarios impagos: “Están adeudando los últimos dos meses completos, pero no es solamente eso. Los trabajadores fueron tomando deuda a lo largo de este año y del año pasado porque la empresa fue pagando a destiempo”, explicó.


Uno de los puntos más cuestionamientos del sindicato es la intención de la empresa de desprenderse de 150 trabajadores mediante un plan de retiros voluntarios o desvinculaciones, con el pago de parte de las indemnizaciones en 12 cuotas.


“Es ilógico que la empresa plantee un plan de retiro voluntario cuando ni siquiera junta la plata para pagar la deuda que tiene con los trabajadores”, afirmó Sarmiento.


El dirigente también puso en duda la capacidad de la firma para afrontar esos compromisos y mencionó la situación financiera de Pauny. Según los datos que dijo haber consultado en la Central de Deudores del Banco Central, la compañía registra obligaciones con distintas entidades bancarias por más de 50 millones de dólares y 206 cheques rechazados en los últimos 15 días, por un monto superior a los $1.500 millones.


“¿Con qué van a pagar? ¿Con cheques? ¿Quién va a aceptar cheques de Pauny? Es una locura lo que está haciendo la empresa”, cuestionó.

author: AusDemWeg
title: Neue Broschüre: Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs
content:
Auf unserer Website

www.ausdemweg.net/downloads/

 ist ab sofort unsere erste Broschüre „Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs“ zum Download bereit. Die Broschüre umfasst unsere drei bereits veröffentlichten Texte zum Thema, sowie eine Einleitung und einen Prolog, der auf die Rolle der Sozialpolitik im historischen Nationalsozialismus im Zuge der Machtergreifung eingeht. Falls ihr die Texte auf unserer Website verpasst habt oder nochmal alles in hübschem Design nachlesen wollt ist das jetzt die perfekte Gelegenheit.


Es stellt sich die berechtigte Frage, warum so viel Arbeit und Energie in eine Auseinandersetzung mit der Ideologie einer kleinen faschistischen Partei gesteckt werden sollte. Schließlich hat die antifaschistische Bewegung in der Vergangenheit oft sehr erfolgreich Treffpunkte und Kader solcher Gruppen oder Parteien unter Druck gesetzt. Doch einerseits funktionieren diese Vorgehensweisen bei wirklich großen Organisationen wie der AFD nicht mehr und andererseits bilden sich insbesondere in den letzten Jahren an vielen Orten wo faschistische Strukturen zerschlagen wurden wieder neue Zusammenhänge. Es reicht offenbar nicht die feindliche Bewegung zu zerstören, da sich nach einigen Jahren einfach eine neue bildet.


Der III. Weg ist eine Partei, die bundesweit viele erfahrene und gut organisierte Nazis in einer Partei vereinen konnte. Auch wenn die Partei immer wieder Rückschläge erlitten hat, ist ein stetiges Wachstum der Strukturen erkennbar. Ein Teil dieses Wachstums ist eine immer größere Zahl von Broschüren und Büchern im parteieigenen Onlineshop. Aktuell sind dort zehn Bücher und vier Broschüren erhältlich, wobei auch einige Schriften fehlen. Es wäre demnach ein Fehler der Partei wie der lokalen Kameradschaft eine mangelnde theoretische Grundlage zu unterstellen. Auch in den Reden und den Beiträgen in den sozialen Medien zeigt sich, dass diese theoretische Grundlage durchaus Anwendung findet.


Die Auseinandersetzung mit den Schriften der Nazis zeigt wenig überraschend eine Vielzahl an Schwächen, die ausgenutzt werden könnten. Dabei geht es sowohl um die innere Logik in ihrer Ideologie, als auch um Grundannahmen und sich daraus ergebende Theorien. Es wäre daher wünschenswert, wenn die antifaschistische Bewegung in Zukunft neben dem Kampf gegen faschistische Infrastruktur und die Aktivisten auch die inhaltliche Auseinandersetzung vorantreibt. Abgesehen davon hilft eine solche Auseinandersetzung mit den Positionen des Gegners auch bei der Schärfung der eignen politischen Vorstellungen. All das kann der antifaschistischen Bewegung nur gut tun.

author: CNT Galiza
title: 20 de noviembre. Combatir el fascismo desde su raíz
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Galego


Castellano

Combatir el fascismo desde su raíz. Cuatro paradigmas de opresión.


Desde CEAG consideramos necesario organizar este evento, donde contaremos con cuatro expertos en diferentes áreas para descifrar algunas claves del discurso fascista. Ofreciendo una perspectiva multidisciplinaria, abordaremos los aspectos más importantes para enfrentarlo desde una posición crítica y de clase. Hablaremos sobre los problemas que atraviesa la clase trabajadora desde una perspectiva laboral-legal, feminista y comprometida con la causa palestina.


En las ponencias, cuatro personas de diferentes ámbitos de la militancia explicarán, desde su experiencia y conocimiento en sus respectivas áreas de lucha, un aspecto muy concreto de la expansión de nuevas formas de autoritarismo dentro del capitalismo: cómo las ideas de los opresores han permeado la lógica de pensamiento de los pueblos oprimidos y sus organizaciones.


Este es un primer acercamiento desde ámbitos específicos de la militancia: la lucha contra el genocidio palestino, la lucha de clases, la lucha feminista y la lucha LGTBI+.


No se pretende agotar el análisis de estas manifestaciones de resistencia, ni ofrecer en esta primera conferencia un enfoque global y abstracto: buscamos realizar una primera aproximación, desde la perspectiva de estas luchas concretas, al cambio de mentalidad que se observa en las personas y en las propias organizaciones de izquierda, a la existencia o no de permeabilidad de las ideas del opresor en la mente de los oprimidos.


Queremos que sea una primera línea de un análisis más amplio y global, pero partiendo de las impresiones de la experiencia, con cuatro ejemplos para un diagnóstico.


Hace 90 años, la clase trabajadora inició una lucha contra la reacción fascista que aún continúa. Para combatirla, comprender los cambios que se están produciendo debe ser, y es, una misión prioritaria para todos nosotros.


Situados en un momento histórico, tenemos la oportunidad de cambiar el rumbo de la situación.


Por lo tanto, les invitamos a participar en la charla en la que habrá espacio para el debate el próximo viernes 20 de noviembre en la Casa do taberneiro (Rúa de San Pedro, 15, Santiago de Compostela) a las 19:00 horas. ¡Asiste y difunde!


Galego

Combater o fascismo de raiz. Catro paradigmas da opresión


Desde o CEAG cremos necesario orgnanizar este acto onde contaremos con 4 expertos en diferentes áreas para poder descifrar algunhas claves do discurso fascista. Ofrecendo unha perspectiva multidisplinar cubriremos os aspectos máis importantes para facerlle fronte desde unha postura crítica e de clase. Falaremos sobre as problemáticas que atravesa a clase traballadora desde un punto de vista xurídico-laboral, feminista e comprometido coa causa palestina.


Nas palestras, catro persoas de diferentes ámbitos de militancia explicarán, dende a súa experiencia e coñecemento no respectivo ámbito de loita, un aspecto moi concreto da expansión das novas formas de autoritarismo dentro da capitalismo: como as ideas dos opresores permearon na lóxica de pensamento das persoas oprimidas e das súas organizacións.

Trátase dunha primeira aproximación dende ámbitos concretos de militancia: A loita contra o xenocidio palestino, a loita de clases, a loita feminista e a loita LGTBI+.

Non pretende agotar a análise nestas parcelas de resistencia, nin aportar nesta primeira palestra un enfoque global e abstracto: queremos facer unha primeira aproximación, dende a óptica de esas concretas loitas, do cambio de mentalidade que se observa nas persoas e nas propias organización de esquerdas, da existencia ou non de permeablidade das ideas do opresor na mente das persoas oprimidas.

Queremos que sexa unha primeira liña dunha análise máis ampla e global, pero comenzando coas impresións da experiencia, con catro mostras para unha diagnose.

Ha 90 anos a clase traballadora comezou unha batalla contra a reacción fascista que aínda continúa hoxe en día. Para poder combatela, entender os cambios que se están a producir debe ser e é unha misión prioritaria para todas nós.

Situadas num momento histórico, temos a oportunidade de darlle a volta á situación. 


Por iso, invitámosvos a participar da charla na que haberá espazo para o debate o vindeiro venres 20 de novembro na Casa do taberneiro (Rúa de San Pedro, 15, Santiago de Compostela) ás 19.00. Asiste e difunde!

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Minneapolis Activists Demand Resignations and Investigations Over Further Surveillance Revelations
content:
Minneapolis, MN – Activists and community members gathered the morning of Nov. 11 just steps from the Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC) in downtown Minneapolis to demand third-party investigations into Hennepin County and the resignation of two high-ranking employees who have been involved with and directed the

surveillance of activists

 calling for the plant’s closure.


Coinciding with the announcement, the Minnesota Environmental Justice Table published an open letter – “initiated by frontline community leaders impacted directly by the HERC trash burner” – for community members to

sign a petition

 pressing the county to meet them.


The two county employees named are Department of Environment and Energy Assistant Director David McNary and the department’s strategic initiative manager Angie Timmons.


“I find it deeply concerning that county resources have been used to monitor environmental justice organizers,” Jordan Area Community Council Executive Director Audua Pugh said during the announcement. “We are calling for the termination of two county employees and an independent third party investigation into these activities. David McNary and Angie Timmons both bear responsibility for allowing such conduct to take place.”


Watch the press conference below.


In a

report

 released by the Zero Burn Coalition in October, public data obtained through information requests revealed that McNary had been sharing private communications between environmental justice advocates with industry representatives to tank a legislative bill that would have given the city the option to shut down HERC.


Hennepin County Surveilled Anti-HERC Activists Since 2023


McNary’s surveillance of activists began in February 2023 with the kickoff of MNEJT’s campaign to close the trash burner. After the event, Hennepin County Environmental Engagement Coordinator Joe Vital, who attended the event, included McNary in an email with notes that included the campaign’s goals.


In a recently uncovered email from March 2023, Department of Environment and Energy Operations and Compliance Manager Randy Kiser referred to Vital as “our spy on the opposition.”


Vital, who was a community activist prior to landing his role with the county, would continue to monitor the campaign and share notes with McNary and other county employees.


According to the October report, Vital also attempted to learn the identity of a Hennepin County whistleblower through MNEJT co-founder Nazir Khan.


Timmons, whose resignation is also demanded by community members and activists, regularly shared information obtained by Vital and through other channels with McNary and Department of Energy and Environment Director Rosemary Lavin.


According to MNEJT Campaign Manager Isuru Herath, part of the county’s surveillance included photographing organizers and community members at events.


“As your constituent, I am very concerned,” Hennepin County resident and organizer Susan Delattre said during the announcement. “It’s already troubling to know that burning my trash harms other people. But now I learned that my own county government has been monitoring my friends and neighbors, including Black and brown community members, who are simply fighting for the right to breathe clean air.”


Also at the announcement was

Alec “Mac” Stewart

, one of

15 Minnesota organizers indicted

 by the U.S. Department of Justice on charges of conspiring to “impede or injure” federal immigration enforcement officers earlier this year during

Operation Metro Surge

.


Stewart drew direct parallels between the surveillance of anti-HERC activists and the indictments against the Minnesota 15 as well as the long history of the U.S. government targeting and disrupting community organizers.


“Instead of defending their constituents, they seek to surveil, disrupt, and dismantle a community-led effort to protect themselves,” Stewart said. “I say that we learned a thing or two about taking back our agency in Metro Surge.”


HERC was included as one of the 20 worst offending trash burning plants in a report published Oct. 13 by the international environmental advocacy group Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives (GAIA).


According to the report, the facility produces roughly 350,000 million tons of carbon dioxide and 72,000 million tons of incinerator ashes annually. The effect of that pollution on the community is roughly $16 million in health damages and one to two deaths annually.

author: Michael_1973
title: South Africa’s ANC Is Collapsing. The Far Right Is Rising.
content:
The African National Congress is losing its working-class base. The beneficiaries: parties of the Right. South Africa’s local elections expose the fallout of three decades of economic failure — and the need to rebuild working-class power.

In this article, Zwelinzima Vavi, the General Secretary of the South Africa Federation of Trade Unions, reflects on the rout of the ANC in the local government elections on 4 November 2026.

While the global left celebrates the recent successes of the Workers’ Party in Brazil and the Democratic Socialists of America in the United States, the African National Congress (ANC) has suffered a historic collapse in South Africa’s November 4 local government elections. After three decades of mass unemployment, deepening inequality, corruption, and economic policies that have failed the working class, the former liberation movement is losing its political authority. The principal beneficiaries of the ANC’s electoral rout are parties of the Right, including an increasingly powerful far right that has built its project around aggressive and often violent xenophobia.

With more than 70 percent of votes counted, the ANC’s national share of the vote fell to around 32 percent. The ANC is not expected to retain an outright majority in any major city, and the center-right Democratic Alliance (DA), historically the principal party of the white liberal establishment, is making substantial gains and is projected to become the largest party in most of South Africa’s big cities. Former President Jacob Zuma’s Zulu nationalist uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) is on track to be the largest party in Durban. The far-right ActionSA has made a strong showing in Johannesburg and Pretoria and is likely to be the second-largest party in Pretoria, with the ANC in third place.

The central question is not only why the ANC has lost so much support. It is why the suffering and anger of the working class have failed to produce a powerful democratic socialist alternative, and why the Right has been so successful in presenting itself as the answer to a crisis created by the existing economic and political order.

The defeat of apartheid was an extraordinary achievement. We won universal suffrage, democratic institutions, constitutional rights, and legal protections for workers. Those victories were won through generations of sacrifice and collective struggle, and they must be defended. But political apartheid was defeated while the economic structures inherited from apartheid remained largely intact.

The liberation movement historically brought together different classes and social groups united against racial oppression. That unity was indispensable to apartheid’s defeat. But national identity does not abolish class contradictions. Instead of using democracy to transform the ownership and control of the economy in the interests of the majority, the ANC increasingly became an instrument through which a new elite could enter and benefit from the existing economic order.

The ownership and control of the commanding heights of the economy were never fundamentally transformed. Land ownership remained extraordinarily unequal. The former Bantustans, created as reservoirs of cheap African labor, were never provided with the productive economic foundations needed to overcome their inherited poverty.

Over time, the ANC came to treat the advancement of an emerging black capitalist class as evidence of economic transformation. A narrow layer of businesspeople accumulated wealth, in some cases extraordinary wealth, through access to political power, state contracts, and opportunities created by the Black Economic Empowerment policy, while the overwhelming majority remained excluded from meaningful economic power.

The ANC’s adoption of neoliberal economic policies in the 1990s deepened this problem. The language of economic liberation gave way to investor confidence, competitiveness, and market reform. Brutal austerity, liberalization, and dependence on private investment displaced the redistributive ambitions of the liberation struggle.

We were repeatedly told that economic growth would eventually deliver employment and redistribution. We were also told that redistribution must wait for economic growth and the development of the productive forces. But if redistribution had to wait while productive capacity developed, why did South Africa simultaneously deindustrialize?

We have become what I have described as a “warehouse economy …

content:
Karp, who gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. in 2024, said after the midterms that he’s been a Democrat his “whole life.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As Democrats prepare for their sweeping campaign to investigate corporate abuses during the upcoming Congress, Palantir CEO Alex Karp claimed this week that he and his company — a massive Trump administration collaborator — are actually “progressive” now.

Karp, who gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. in 2024 and another million for Donald Trump’s inauguration, told Politico Playbook on Wednesday that he’s always been a Democrat.

“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir — all of our products are essentially progressive,” he told Politico, speaking of his company that has a $30 million contract with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to aid Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

Far from being progressive, Karp and his company have helped to accelerate the Trump administration’s descent into fascism while wooing Trump in order to gain favor with the government.

The tech CEO has been on the record many times branding himself and Palantir as undertaking a far right effort, with Karp calling his company “anti-woke” and praising the Trump administration’s anti-immigration measures.

But in the Politico interview, Karp claimed that he was happy that Trump acknowledged that “we kinda went too far” on immigration — a misrepresentation of Trump’s words earlier this week. Karp used the word “progressive” eight times to describe his political philosophy, despite the fact that progressivism is typically known for being antiwar, pro-immigrant, and opposed to tech companies like Palantir.

title: ABC-Belarus lost its hoster Autistici/Inventati because of American fascists
content:
Back in 2010, at the height of the repression, one of our comrades contacted us and proposed setting up a website for our group. At the time, Italian activists from Autistici became our hosters. For a small annual donation, they handled the technical infrastructure, allowing us to focus on our work. Sixteen years later, we find ourselves in a situation where Donald Trump’s fascist politics affect not only collectives in the US or Europe, but also our own struggle.

Even before ABC-Belarus came into existence, the Autistici collective had been a target of the Italian government: they were persecuted for supporting the local Anarchist Black Cross group. At the time, the Italian authorities hacked activists’ servers as part of a criminal investigation. After we began working with Autistici, we learned that unknown hackers from Belarus had also tried to hack the service, but failed. In 2015, through our collaboration with the group, we learned about the hacking of the Italian company Hacking Team’s servers and its possible cooperation with the Belarusian regime.

In August 2026, the Trump administration added the Autistici/Inventati collective to its list of terrorist organizations for providing infrastructure to antifascist and anarchist groups and organizations. This led to the organization’s bank accounts being frozen and further repression against them. In early August, hackers linked to the far-right movement in the US hacked one of the group’s services. Unfortunately, as a result of all the attacks, the collective decided to cease its work, and we completely understand that decision. Today, fascists in the US are using international agreements between various states in an attempt to destroy antifascist and anarchist movements around the world. In this situation, surviving online is becoming increasingly difficult. It is also noteworthy that the collective was shut down not by the Italian fascists from Giorgia Meloni’s party, but by trumpists who gained access to the resources of one of the most aggressive and powerful empires of our time.

With this short message, we want to thank all the members of the Autistici/Inventati collective for their work and for supporting the struggle against Lukashenko’s dictatorship!

title: Nesrin Akgül: Women are not spectators but architects of peace
content:
Women's direct participation in decision-making mechanisms and their role as founding actors are crucial to achieving a lasting and democratic solution through the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Women emphasise that peace must not be limited to the silencing of weapons or negotiations between political actors. They argue that women must participate in decision-making mechanisms through their own political will if the process is to become rooted in society and achieve lasting results. Questions remain over the extent to which women's demands are reflected in negotiations and political processes, how much representation they have in decision-making mechanisms and whether they are being excluded from the process. Women stress that they must not merely serve as a supporting force but must be actors who make decisions and determine the direction of the process. Equal representation, the establishment of independent women's mechanisms and guarantees for women's participation in concrete decision-making bodies are among the key demands. Women's involvement in the process on the basis of their own demands is considered essential to strengthening the social struggle and establishing peace throughout society.


Free Women's Movement (TJA) activist Nesrin Akgül spoke to ANF about the issue.


'Peace is not merely the silencing of weapons'


Nesrin Akgül said that peace cannot be defined solely as the silencing of weapons and that the conditions which gave rise to the war must be eliminated to build lasting peace. Akgül said: "How do we define the process we call peace? If the forces involved in the war cannot establish common ground, even at a minimal level, the question of how peace can be built becomes a matter of debate. Peace is not an achievement that can be secured simply by silencing weapons. Of course, the greatest devastation caused by war is the loss of human life, and ending that loss is the most valuable achievement. However, this war did not take place between two hegemonic powers. It began when a sovereign state denied the existence of a people and an oppressed people rose up against that denial. A people began a war of self-defence in pursuit of their right to self-determination. This was a war entered into out of necessity, but also by choice. It became a struggle to regain dignity. What gained acceptance was that a people reclaimed their dignity through this struggle. For 52 years, this war continued on the basis of that reality.


It is impossible to envisage how peace can be established without identifying the causes of this war. Abdullah Öcalan has repeatedly stressed this point to the state throughout the process. The issue is not disarmament. The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) may cease to exist today, but another organisation could emerge tomorrow. The real issue is eliminating the conditions that gave rise to the war. This is the framework within which the peace process must be defined. In other words, we must move from a negative peace process that begins with the silencing of weapons to a positive process of construction that consolidates the elimination of armed conflict. This process can sustain itself through the socialisation of peace and the social reconstruction conceptualised within the Peace and Democratic Society Process. It will acquire a comprehensive character when the state, as a party to peace, becomes responsive to democracy, consolidates peace legislation and moves towards democratic integration."


'Women cannot be defined by their victimhood'


Nesrin Akgül emphasised that women's responsibilities and role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process are decisive. She continued: "It cannot be a coincidence that women are regarded as the most effective force responsible for both silencing weapons and achieving social reconstruction in discussions surrounding the Peace and Democratic Society Process. In every conflict-resolution process, how women will participate has been one of the central questions and challenges. We must ask: Why are women the first to come to mind when peace is mentioned? Let me take that question further: Why are women primarily defined as those who have suffered the most and whose rights have been violated most severely? For women like us, who have waged a struggle for liberation, the identity and historical position from which women's presence in the peace process is defined are even more important.

Unter anderem, um den deutschen Wirtschaftsstandort und seine global relevante Rolle aufrechtzuerhalten. Das kapitalistische System ist mal wieder in der Krise. Statt alternative Wirtschaftssysteme zu etablieren, die weniger Raubbau an Natur und Menschheit verursachen, wird ein autoritärer Staatsumbau legitimiert, der jegliche erkämpfte Errungenschaften wie Arbeitsrechte und Arbeitslosengeld, freie Bildung, den Klimaschutz,etc. über die Klinge springen lässt.


Gleichzeitig fließen massiv viele Ressourcen in den Ausbau eines Überwachungsapparats, der die Bevölkerung mittels KI ausspioniert, soziale und antifaschistische Proteste kriminalisiert, während eine faschistische Partei auf dem Vormarsch ist.


Junge Menschen haben keinen Bock ihr Leben und ihre Karriere aufs Spiel zu setzen, um Deutschland den Arsch zu retten. Sie wollen keinen Staat und kein Wirtschaftssystem, was ihnen eine positive Zukunftsperspektive verwehrt.


Wir grüßen an dieser Stelle die Gen Z- Proteste!


Faschismus ist die Herrschaftsform des Kapitalismus in der Krise.


In dem was „Zeitenwende“ genannt wird, geht es um die Erneuerung des Kapitalismus in einer Phase wirtschaftlichen Niedergangs. Diese Phase soll einmal mehr durch Aufrüstung, Krieg und die militärische Sicherstellung der Zugänge zu Ressourcen, auf die es vermeintlichen Anspruch gibt, überwunden werden.


Um die Militarisierung voranzubringen, wird vor allem Angst und Unsicherheit in den Köpfen verursacht. Bedrohungsszenarien und teils angestaubte Feindbilder sollen die breite Präsenz und Einflussnahme des Militärs in den zivilen Bereich legitimieren. Schulen und Ausbildungsstätten werden als Rekrutierungszentralen benutzt. Medizinisches Personal für Kriegszeiten mit vielen Verwundeten geschult. Soldat*innen in Uniform in der Öffentlichkeit und großflächige Werbung gewöhnen uns an einen militarisierten Alltag.


Militarisierung und Sozialabbau gehen Hand in Hand mit der zunehmend autoritären Formierung des Staates. Diese wird von bürgerlichen Parteien vorangetrieben und die faschistische Partei AfD als Teil der Neuen Rechten kann die Lorbeeren ernten, wenn es um eine Übernahme des ausufernden Überwachungsstaats, restriktive Aufenthaltsgesetze oder den Umgang mit Protest geht. Rechte und faschistische Kräfte nehmen dann ihre klassische, vom System zugedachte Rolle ein: das Aufbegehren von Teilen der Bevölkerung und den Zusammenhalt untereinander anzugreifen und zu zerschlagen.


Moderner Faschismus und Autoritarismus


Der moderne Faschismus in Deutschland greift natürlich auf Kontinuitäten zurück, die an den Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts zurückreichen. Die Neue Rechte besteht aus intellektuellen rechtsradikalen Projekten, nationalkonservativen, neoliberalen Ansätzen, gepaart mit völkischen Schlägertrupps und Parteirechten. Rechtsradikale von heute sind gut vernetzt. Hier werden Beziehungen zu den US-amerikanischen Tech-Oligarchen ebenso gepflegt wie jene zu europäischen rechten Parteien oder Gruppierungen. Einen zunehmenden Autoritarismus können wir global feststellen. Nicht verwunderlich, wenn die vorherrschende Wirtschaftsform der kapitalistischen und neoliberalen Ordnung folgt.


Autoritäre Einstellungsmuster, die u.a. auf rassistischer sowie sexistischer Diskriminierung und reaktionären Geschlechterrollen aufbauen, entstehen aus der kapitalistischen Ordnung selbst, werden aber durch Militarisierung sowie dezidiert rechte Propaganda und Gesetzgebungen verschärft. Diese Muster sind in der Gesellschaft bereits angelegte Ideologien und „Lösungsstrategien“ für die Krisen des Kapitalismus. title: Karaköy'den Eminönü'ne kadın zinciri: “Erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulsun”
content:
İstanbul – Karaköy’de iskele önünde zincir oluşturan kadınlar Eminönü’ne yürüyüş gerçekleştirdi. Eminönü’nde iskeleye gelen kadınlar burada, ölümü aydınlatılmamış kadınların hikayelerinden aktarımlarda bulunduktan sonra basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. Açıklamada, “Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

25 Kasım Kadın Platformu öncülüğünde Karaköy'de zincir oluşturuldu, Eminönü'ne bir yürüyüş düzenlendi. Eylemde, 2026-2035 yıllarının iktidar tarafından ‘Aile ve Nüfus On Yılı’ ilan edilmesinin ardından 2026'nın ilk 10 ayında 245 kadının erkekler tarafından katledildiği ve 274 kadının şüpheli şekilde yaşamanı yitirdiğine dikkat çekildi, iktidarın mevcut politikalarına tepki gösterildi.

Eminönü'nde yapılan açıklamada “Kadın cinayetlerinin karşısında yalnızca yas tutmayacağız. Kadınların yaşam hakkını tehdit eden bütün mekanizmaları teşhir edeceğiz. Koruma kararlarının kağıt üzerinde kalmasına, şiddet başvurularının görmezden gelinmesine, faillerin iyi hal ve haksız tahrik indirimleriyle ödüllendirilmesine, şüpheli kadın ölümlerinin karanlıkta bırakılmasına izin vermeyeceğiz. Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

Eylemde son yıllarda hayatını kaybeden kadınlara yönelik bazı saldırılar hakkında da şu bilgiler verildi:

“Fatmanur Çelik, 30 yaşında genç bir kadındı. Kuran'a Hizmet Vakfı'nda sohbetlere katıldığı sırada vakıf çalışanı Ayhan Şengüler tarafından tecavüze uğradı. Ailesi tarafından Ayhan Şengüler ile evlenmeye zorlandı ve evliliği boyunca cinsel şiddete maruz kaldı. Ayhan Şengüler'in kızı Hifa İkra'yı istismar ettiği için yargılandığı davada savcının beraat istemesinin ardından 13 Ocak'ta Anadolu Adliyesi önünde adalet nöbetine başladı. Fatmanur Çelik ve kızı Hifa İkra'nın cansız bedenleri 3 Mart'ta Zeytinburnu Sahili'nde bulundu.

Arya 19 yaşında, TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi İngiliz Dili Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisiydi. 13 Nisan 2026’da kaldığı üniversite yurdunda intihara sürüklendi. Ailesi Arya’ya trans kadın olduğu için şiddet uyguladı, onu onarım terapisine götürdüler. Arya kaldığı yurtta hem yurt yönetimi hem öğrenciler tarafından baskı, dışlanma ve tehditlere maruz kaldı. Arya’nın ölümüne intihar deniyor ama Arya’yı intihara sürükleyen koşulların üstünün örtüldüğünü biliyoruz.

İlayda Zorlu 19 yaşında, Karadeniz Teknik Üniversitesi’nde Uluslararası İlişkiler bölümü öğrencisiydi. Polis, İlayda Zorlu'nun ailesini arayarak 'Kızınız 8 Mart eylemlerine katılıyor, çocuğunuz örgüte katılmış' dedi. Ailesinin baskısına maruz kalan, evde alıkonulduğunu, okutulmayacağını ve evden kaçmak istediğini arkadaşlarına anlatan İlayda, 17 Nisan 2026'da Hatay'ın Kırıkhan ilçesindeki aile evinde, polis olan babasının silahından çıkan kurşunla hayatını kaybetti.

Ayşe Tokyaz, 22 yaşında bir üniversite öğrencisiydi. 2025 yılının temmuz ayında, ihraç polis Cemil Koç tarafından Küçükçekmece’de öldürüldü. Cansız bedeni bir valize konularak katil Cemil Koç’la suç ortaklığı yapan erkekler tarafından yol kenarına bırakıldı. Ayşe’nin ikizi Esra, kardeşini kurtarmak için tek başına mücadele etti. Ayşe yalnızca Cemil Koç tarafından değil, katilin işlerini yapan, cinayetten sonra evi temizleten, Esra’yı oyalayan, sosyal medyadan taciz eden, ifadesini katile sızdıran ve cinayetten sonra çevirmelere takılmaması için katile eşlik eden polis memurunun da aralarında olduğu erkekler tarafından el birliğiyle katledildi.

as someone who has severe sensory issues re: my own hair but who also KNOWS THINGS ABOUT MISOGYNY, I always want to respond to “I shave/wax for sensory reasons” with “me too, but I was encouraged to do that with the hair on my legs, whereas when I removed the hair on my eyelids, eyebrows, and scalp, it got me institutionalized. can you think of any reasons why that might be, bc I have a hypothesis”

people do not like when you say things such as this. i think its a conversation which needs to be had, though!!! like what hair is it considered appropriate and desirable for women to remove? what hair is it considered inappropriate and pathological for women to remove? WE HAVE SOME VERY OBVIOUSLY ANSWERS HERE we just choose not to look at them

“I do it for sensory reasons” is, CHARITABLY, not the end of a conversation. i say charitably because it often is not even fucking relevant. but assuming that it is, ok. and how did those around you react when you began doing this. were you encouraged or discouraged? what would the reaction be if you stopped? what if you removed hair from other areas? what if a man removed his hair for sensory reasons? what would the reaction be? what social pressures might he need to overcome in order to take that action that don’t exist for those of us for whom this is expected?

LET’S GO ON A THOUGHT JOURNEY TOGETHER.

less generously and more straightforwardly because I think many people are missing my point here

“I do it for sensory reasons” is almost never fucking relevant to an existing conversation about the expected removal of body hair in women and is 100% never a relevant response to an existing conversation about SOCIETAL MISOGYNY.

and I would like for those who deploy it as such to do some serious reflecting on why they think it is a reasonable counterpoint in said discussions, rather than a segue into another related discussion about what behaviors are rewarded and encouraged in what people and whether those same behaviors are discouraged and punished in other people. and what someone’s experiences seeing reflected in the world around them might prime them to see certain things as normal (and therefore no big deal to engage in) and others as abnormal (and therefore something that would require an unusually strong individual motivation to engage in)

author: Alyssa Mae Clarin
title: Women, youth groups slam Sara Duterte over sexual advice to women OFWs
content:
One of the places where OFWs spend their rest day in Hong Kong. (Photo by Carlo Manalansan/Bulatlat)

“Instead of holding men accountable for their cheating and abuse, the advice places the burden on women to keep their partners through sexual performance.”

Women’s group Gabriela condemned Vice President Sara Duterte for telling female Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in Hong Kong to be good at sex to prevent their partners from cheating or leaving them, calling the remarks “misogynistic” and an example of “victim-blaming.”

In a video posted online by Filipino singer Jimmy Bondoc, Duterte told the Filipino women in the audience that they should be good at “esmeringhoy,” a Bisaya term used as a euphemism for sexual intercourse, to keep their partners from going astray.

Although the remark drew cheers and laughter from the audience, national women alliance group Gabriela said it should not be dismissed as merely tasteless banter, particularly because it came from the country’s second-highest official.

“Instead of holding men accountable for their cheating and abuse, the advice places the burden on women to keep their partners through sexual performance,” Gabriela said in a statement.

The national women’s alliance said Duterte’s remark reflects the same victim-blaming logic that women face daily, wherein they are made to question what they did or failed to do to supposedly warrant the violence, abuse, or betrayal committed against them.

Gabriela also stressed that the remark is profoundly detached from the realities faced by Filipino women, whose struggles are rooted in the lack of protection, decent livelihood, and respect for their rights—not in any supposed failure to please men.

Read: Citing women’s conditions, Gabriela Women’s Party questions Marcos’ UN statement

“A woman is never to blame for a man’s infidelity,” the alliance further added.

Bayan Muna Youth also criticized Duterte, saying that even when delivered as a joke, her advice to Filipino women migrants contributes to broader public discourse on women’s rights and gender relations.

“Humor does not remove the responsibility to challenge harmful gender stereotypes, particularly in a country where violence against women, sexual exploitation, economic abuse, and unequal domestic responsibilities remain pressing concerns,” the youth group said.

Gabriela urged women to reject the notion that their worth is measured by how well they serve and satisfy men. The alliance also called on public officials to stop dressing up patriarchal beliefs as concern for women.

Similarly, Bayan Muna Youth also urged public officials to move beyond jokes that reinforce misogynistic attitudes and instead push for concrete policies that uphold and protect the rights and welfare of Filipino women.

“Remarks that reduce women to instruments of men’s satisfaction have no place in a government that claims to protect them,” Gabriela concluded. (AMU, RVO)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Harassment won’t stop a son’s search for his missing father
content:
Marklen Lariosa, son of missing Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) labor organizer William Lariosa, speaks during a rally in Davao City on the first anniversary of his father’s disappearance on April 10, 2025. Photo by Kath Cortez/Davao Today

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through.”

Is it a mistake for a son to demand justice and accountability?

Marklen, son of disappeared labor organizer William Lariosa, raised this question following the recent incident of harassment and surveillance he experienced. Members of his family were alarmed after two unidentified individuals were looking for his residence on the night of October 25.

He told Bulatlat that this was the first time such an event had happened since his father, a labor organizer under Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao, was abducted in Quezon, Bukidnon, on April 10, 2024.

Marklen could not think of other possible reasons, suspecting that the incident may have something to do with his continuing involvement in campaigns and mobilizations that demand the surfacing of Lariosa. “Is it a mistake for a son to search for his missing father?” he further asked.

Read: After 2 years, son laments continuing disappearance of Mindanao labor organizer

Neighbors of the Lariosa family in their hometown in Davao de Oro province were the ones who encountered the two individuals. They reportedly wore helmets and were on board a black motorcycle, introducing themselves as “collectors” when they were asked.

For Marklen, the response and presence of the two raised suspicions. Aside from the fact that they visited the community around 7 p.m., which is outside the regular working hours, Marklen said that he did not apply for any financial loan.

After the incident, he was concerned for the safety of his family, prompting them to lodge a blotter report with the barangay. However, he stood firm that it won’t stop him from continuing his cause.

Desaparecidos, an organization of families and friends of enforced disappearance victims, denounced the incident, urging the government to put an end to this kind of harassment.

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through,” JL Burgos, Desaparecidos chairperson, said in a statement.

Rights groups Karapatan and the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR) also expressed strong condemnations about what happened.

Marklen, a member of the National Board of Desaparecidos, has raised a possibility that the two individuals who recently visited their neighborhood might be connected to those who visited their house several times prior to the disappearance of his father.

He said they were visited by individuals who allegedly introduced themselves as state agents once in 2022 and three times in 2023, accusing Lariosa of being involved in communist insurgency. There were warnings, he added, that they would get dragged into it if they would not cooperate.

The series of visits was reportedly the primary reason why Lariosa was forced to take refuge in Bukidnon. Marklen affirmed that his father, who remains missing, had been a labor organizer.

On July 8, the Supreme Court required certain commanders and elements of Philippine Army units to comment on the petition for review on certiorari filed by the family.

Read: Military ordered to reply to missing Mindanao labor organizer’s case

Since 2024, KMU Southern Mindanao has documented 57 cases of human rights violations against its members and organizers.

The labor group released a statement on October 24, presenting the faces of some individuals, including former high-ranking New People’s Army (NPA) member Roberto Rosete Jr., who allegedly harassed KMU’s leaders and members.

Read: Groups decry surveillance of KMU office in Southern Mindanao

Marklen called for an end to any form of harassment and intimidation against families of the disappeared, pointing out that achieving justice is their only goal. (RVO)

author: Coral Wynter
title: Standing with the women and girls of Afghanistan
content:
About 110 people from Australia and Britain joined Amnesty International (AI) in an on-line forum, on September 23, to hear about the human rights group's strategy to support women in Afghanistan. Kathy Allan from AI introduced the forum by saying that when Kabul fell on August 15, 2021, the United States handed over power to the Taliban, after the US Coalition, including Australian forces, had carried out a military intervention into Afghanistan for two decades.

The Taliban has 164 decrees targeting women and girls. Women have been barred from most jobs, and from working with non-government organisations (NGOs). Girls are banned from secondary school and university, parks, gyms and beauty salons. Women cannot speak publicly. LGBTIQ+ Afghans have been forced into hiding.

The Taliban is also attacking ethnic and religious minorities, as well as journalists and human rights defenders.

This institutionalised pattern of systemic domination and oppression based on gender has been labelled “gender apartheid”. Afghanistan is the only country in the world to impose this extreme form of gender discrimination.

Right now, international law has no statute that fully captures this situation. AI is calling for gender apartheid to be recognised as a crime under international law.

Muslima, an Afghan educator and writer, told the forum, “Almost overnight, the door to our classroom was closed. Just because you were a girl, you lost your classroom.

“I never imagined that my future would just mean I stay home ... simply because I was born a girl. Being at home every day felt like a prison, like being in jail. Where do I go? My human rights were wiped out.

“But now I have a computer, my classroom to the outside world. All that I have is a small screen in my room. If they find out, I can face charges.

“Thousands of girls have no access to a computer and internet, but I am lucky. Afghan women can’t talk about their stories, nor can they speak about these issues. Girls of 12 years of age are denied the simple right to education, to learn, to develop their skills, to make friends.

“The Taliban can’t build a strong future by excluding half of the population. Afghanistan is losing enormous [human] potential.

“I want the world to see something beyond our suffering. Women are still writing, working, advocating, creating, contributing and building. If you want to support Afghan women, you must listen to them.

“When the headlines disappear, Afghan women do not disappear.

“So my message is clear: make a space for us to speak. Share our voices.

“Sometimes solidarity begins with something as simple as a refusal to forget. Listen to the voices of Afghan women, who are denied their human rights,” Muslima concluded.

The next speaker was Shaharzad Akbar, a human rights activist from Afghanistan, currently living in exile. She talked about the Peoples Tribunal on Women of Afghanistan, which was held in Madrid, Spain, in October last year and hosted by four Afghan women’s organisations.

They are worried that the actions of the Taliban, as the de facto regime, are being normalised in the region. The Taliban currently have consulates in Germany, China, India and Turkiye, although only Russia officially recognises the Taliban government. Europe is now holding conversations with the Taliban regarding potentially deporting Afghan men and women.

Akbar said, “Women are not able to train as midwives or doctors ... Women will die from preventable diseases because there are not enough female health-care providers.”

Women are suffering from domestic abuse, but it is not considered a crime inside Afghanistan. Emotional, economic and physical abuses are not criminalised. Husbands are allowed by law to punish their wives for any offence.

Women can only go to a judge to make a complaint if they have obvious bruises or broken bones — and face many hurdles to do so. They are not allowed to leave the house alone and a male family member has to accompany them to the court. So a brother or father has to be convinced to support them.

The woman has to relay her message to the judge through a man. If she is believed and she has broken bones caused by her husband, he will be imprisoned for 15 days. He usually returns home only to repeat the abuse.

“We have had increased killing of women, increased suicides of women and a mental health crisis for women and girls in Afghanistan. They don’t see a future for themselves. They are imprisoned in their homes …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Dignity walks in the heart
content:
Mexico’s search collectives make alliances with Zapatista army to confront the systematic violence of enforced disappearances and femicides

It is dawn again and 12-year-old Ariana is getting ready to leave her home with her grandmother. Together they walk in the mountains of Chiapas to a nearby ranch to care for their family animals. After that? We cannot say, as they both stepped out of this world and disappeared. We only know for sure that they were never seen alive again.

The family and neighbours began the search until two days later, the body of 55-year-old Miriam Cruz Alpuche was discovered on the bank of a local stream. She was wrapped in black bin bags and community rescue units discovered multiple signs of violence. By the end of the week, Ariana Scarlet Velázquez Cruz was found close by.

“The demand for truth and justice for disappearances,” said Captain Marcos of the EZLN (Zapatista Army of National Liberation) “enforced disappearances and disappearances by individuals – must be assumed a national responsibility.” Marcos was speaking in San Cristóbal de las Casas (Jovel) in Chiapas after meeting with “mother seekers” in el caracol Jacinto Canel.

In the Zapatista territories, EZLN and colectivos de búsqueda (search collectives) have pledged to form alliances in confronting the Mexican government for it’s role in facilitating disappearances, murders, gender-based violence and wars. They will meet in Ajusco in December, an area that is a high risk for disappearances, as well as a delegation to Mexico City to both expose and find community-based resistance to this crime against humanity.

With more than 130,000 people missing in Mexico, decades of activism and legal battles against systematic violence and enforced disappearances, the United Nations has finally got involved in offering the state of Mexico assistance. Predictably as the families of the disappeared arrived to give their own testimony, the Mexican government denied this pain with their own historical fiction.

In Chiapas there have been 30 documented cases of femicide and 440 across Mexico in the first half of 2026. These numbers are reflections of the activities of local groups, not the true scale of the problem. Government corruption has hidden the mass killings of women and children, as well as a clear complicity in the enforced disappearances of it’s own citizens. If the body is never recovered, it cannot be known how the person died.

Investigations into femicides in Mexico are impacted by a loss of evidence, an inadequate investigation or when the gender perspective is not applied correctly. Families of the missing are re-victimised by the process of seeking justice while authorities fail to examine crime scenes, secure evidence or carry out acid phosphatase tests. All of this impacts the possibility of justice for the affected and their families.

Femicidal violence “leaves indelible consequences, deep traumas and an irreparable void in their families… in their communities and in the entire social fabric of the state,” said the Observatorio Ciudadano Nacional del Feminicidio (National Citizen Observatory of Femicide) following the murder of Miriam and Ariana. They demand an immediate gender – child perspective investigation.

The inaction of the authorities when a woman or child has gone missing is deadly, with some regional police asking families to wait 72 hours before reporting a missing person. This would have been too late for Miriam, as it would likely be for 12-year-old Ariana. The logic should be to investigate when a person is noticed missing.

In the absence of executing justice, various instruments of the law such as the Attorney General’s Office (FGE) work as a mechanism to prevent the opening of investigations, with “omission… a lack of commitment and responsibility,” observed Guadalupe Isabel Mondoza Pérez, who has been looking for her husband Alfonso since July 30, 2024 after he disappeared in Yajalón.

Authorities limit complaints by creating an administrative hole called “registros de attención” (care records) as a way of killing formal investigations. With legal advice from Colectiva Cereza (Cherry Collective), families can see what missing persons reports have been shelved in care records and which are open investigations.

If the aim is to tear the social fabric of our shared relations – it would make sense to weave these communities with shared struggles and resources to resist the stranglehold of the law as …

-71% of transmascs have a degree vs. 29% of transfemmes.

-46% of trans people make below $10k/y, with 57% of TWOC making below that.

If you want to actually help trans people, employ us so we can fucking survive. Hire us and train us. Fucking help us live.

https://dctranscoalition.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/dctc-access-denied-final.pdf

However, it’s undeniable from the data that there is a disparity.

It’s probably because transfems feel less safe on campus than transmascs, because they’re often more visibly transgender to transphobes (mostly due to societal focus on them), but I have no data to back this up.

author: Deaglan Godwin
title: Businessmen, not battlers, lead the charge for One Nation in NSW
content:
Pauline Hanson’s One Nation pretends to be a party of battlers, standing up for the little guy against the major parties. This narrative has been parroted by the mainstream media and even taken up by Hanson’s opponents. The party’s lead candidates for the March 2027 New South Wales state election paint a very different picture of who the party represents.

Take Mike Newman, newly-appointed NSW leader and candidate for Cessnock, the Hunter Valley seat One Nation considers winnable. Newman’s riches-to-riches story involves growing up in well-heeled Mosman on Sydney’s lower North Shore and attending the elite private school Cranbrook, along with billionaire James Packer. His father, Maurice Newman, was the chair of the Australian Securities Exchange and then of the ABC. 

Son followed father into the world of investment banking. After a long career as a banker in Tokyo, Newman landed a gig in the public service as NSW Senior Trade and Investment Commissioner in Japan. The wasteful inefficiency of the bureaucracy supposedly radicalised Newman and convinced him to go into politics. Curiously, during his three-year stint as commissioner, Newman racked up hundreds of thousands of dollars in expenses (funded by the taxpayer) for flights, five-star hotels and restaurant and bar bills, as was recently revealed by the

Sydney Morning Herald

. This spending included more than $20,000 for an extended stay in a Meriton Suite in Sydney.

Next up is Jeff Bacon, who will be second on One Nation’s ticket for the upper house. Bacon is the managing director of Oceana Precision, a weapons manufacturer based in Tamworth, his north-eastern NSW hometown. He ran as the lower house candidate for Tamworth with the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers party in 2019, then joined the Nationals in 2023 before defecting to One Nation in October 2025. 

In an interview with Tamworth’s local newspaper, the 

Northern Daily Leader,

 in January, Bacon alleged that every single one of Oceania Precision’s rifles was banned in NSW following firearms legislation passed by the state Labor government in the wake of the Bondi Massacre. Bacon would, apparently, be broke in six months if the laws weren’t repealed. Hanson has described him as her “go-to man on the firearms industry”.

Sure, you might struggle to pay grocery or electricity bills, or cover your mortgage or rent. But spare a thought for the owner of a medium-sized weapons manufacturer whose human rights have been trampled on by the Labor government. 

Stuart Bonds, the party’s lead upper house candidate, is more regularly held up as emblematic of the party’s battler credentials.

Bonds, a former Hunter Valley coal miner, won 21 percent of the vote for One Nation in the 2019 federal election. Bonds is critical of both renewable energy and the behaviour of multinational mining companies. He left One Nation in 2021 over its support for the Morrison government's industrial relations legislation that undermined casual workers’ rights.

Bonds, however, is more representative of your average bigot than battler. At an anti-immigration rally in early November, he espoused the far-right Great Replacement conspiracy theory. He told the protesters that, “we are being demographically replaced inside our own nation”, and warned them that this was part of a “socialist plan” to “tear down the fabric of your civilisation”. 

Bonds is also a bigot on other social issues. Many have rightly pointed out the irony of his misogynistic comments when he boasted: “I don’t have a woman boss, and I don’t have a gay boss, and there’s a reason for that”. The only problem for Mr Bonds is that he does indeed have both a woman boss in Hanson and a gay boss in James Ashby, the party director. Irony aside, the comments indicate the rank misogyny and homophobia that aren’t simply personal opinions, but party policy. One Nation boasts about being “pro-life” and is currently campaigning to restrict abortion rights in NSW. 

One Nation’s NSW state election candidates give you a glimpse into the actual character of the party. Rather than being the authentic expression of working-class grievances, the party is a Frankenstein-like combination of bankers, bigots and small business owners. What unites them is not their genuine struggles under the system, but their hostility to the gains made by oppressed groups and minorities, hatred of the left and commitment to a pro-business economic agenda.

author: S. Baum
title: Justice Department Official Who Led Attacks on Gender-Affirming Care Resigns
content:
Brett Shumate is the fourth DOJ official to resign since the midterms after leading investigations that pressured hospitals to end care for trans minors.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Brett Shumate has become the fourth Department of Justice official to join the post-election exodus from the agency following Republicans’ crushing midterm defeat — marking the end of the tenure of a man who helped grease the wheels of the anti-trans machine.

“The rats are fleeing the sinking ship,” Alejandra Caraballo, a lawyer and trans rights scholar, posted on Bluesky, alongside news that Shumate, the Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Division, was resigning.

Under Shumate’s leadership, the DOJ aggressively targeted providers of gender-affirming care, subpoenaing patient records and waging False Claims Act investigations to intimidate hospitals. This caused some major hospitals to end care for trans minors and pay millions in settlements to the government. He was also instrumental in defending these actions in court against claims they were unlawful government overreach.

No hospital or clinic has been successfully sued because it provides evidence-based medicine, but some of them signed agreements with the DOJ to stave off the worst of federal threats: the demand that providers hand over identifiable patient data about thousands of transgender children and their families. Not all of these investigations or deals have been public.

Still, hospitals shut down their gender-affirming care programs for trans youth, leaving care deserts across the country. Lower courts condemned the government’s ploy, with one Boston judge calling it “a fishing expedition.” In a similar Rhode Island case, another judge said the DOJ — under Shumate’s leadership at the time — “has proven unworthy of this trust at every point in this case.”

In June 2025, Shumate issued a memo directing Civil Division employees to prioritize attacks on gender-affirming care, courtesy of the whims of President Donald Trump and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, who was ousted in April. Shumate’s memo announced the Civil Division will “prioritize investigations of doctors, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, and other appropriate entities” that ostensibly violate Trump’s declarations about transgender youth care. “In addition, the Civil Division will aggressively pursue claims under the False Claims Act against health care providers that bill the federal government for impermissible services.”

This largely included providers of wholly legal gender-affirming care, even in blue states — such as Children’s Hospital Los Angeles in California and Mount Sinai Hospital in New York. There is no federal ban on gender-affirming care.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, in announcing Shumate’s departure on X, praised him for “shutter[ing] dozens of clinics” for gender-affirming care.

The DOJ also saw the departure of Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division, and whose firm previously represented “ex-trans” activist Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against Kaiser Permanente for providing gender-affirming care.

Jason Reding Quiñones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, and John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for the National Security Division, also resigned. The department is also reeling from general attrition of staff throughout. The DOJ is not likely to stop pursuing political targets, including trans people and their caretakers and doctors, but if nothing else, the turmoil at the DOJ is liable to make it less effective. Under Trump, “a drastically diminished Justice Department workforce is struggling to keep up with its civil side caseloads,” The Hill found.

“A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.” This may slow down some of the destructive efforts by the DOJ — going after lawful gender-affirming care providers, defending the government from lawsuits over human rights violations. But others question how this might shape the department politically as new hires grow increasingly conservative and less qualified or willing to defy unlawful orders. Other important targets of the DOJ, such as those guilty of terrorism or white-collar crime, may also benefit from less competence in oversight.

A replacement for Shumate has not yet been announced.
