author: ACG
title: Resistance to Data Centres in Ireland
content:
From a correspondent  in the Republic of Ireland.


On November 7

th

over 2,000 participated in a protest march in Dublin. The action was against data centres. There was a range of ages and organisations represented, from children to grandparents, environmental and community groups as well as political parties.  It was part of a co-ordinated Europe-wide response to a growing problem.


There are a number of reasons to oppose data centres and those at the protest voiced a variety of objections. One of the most commonly expressed complaints is their massive consumption of energy, often 24 hours a day. They compete with houses, schools and hospitals in this regard and the figures for the past decade show the increase they have made in consumption.


In the case of Ireland the Central Statistics Office (CSO) shows that data centres accounted for just 5% of consumption in 2015, but this had skyrocketed to 23% in 2025 (CSO.ie). This resulted in Irish households paying an estimated 715 Euros more in electricity bills from 2015 to 2023. This trend is likely to continue under current conditions. Campaign group Friends of the Earth predicts in a report that if that is the case, costs on households could mean an additional 1.43 billion Euros in electricity bills by 2034 (friendsoftheearth.ie).


oplus_32


Environmental concern can be found in their use of water. Data centres use huge amounts for their cooling systems. This puts pressure on local water supplies, especially during periods of drought or water restrictions. This is not a purely theoretical point in the case of Ireland. An indication of the general governmental attitude towards water usage can been seen in this year’s 2 and a half month ban on the use of hosepipes during summer. This was applied in Dublin and a number of other areas. However, an exemption was made for business during the ban (RTE, 22nd July 2026).


To put water use in perspective, total data centre water usage in Ireland was around 1 billion litres in 2025. Academics from universities in Ireland and Catalonia estimated in a recent joint report that this was equivalent to 18.5% of the consumption of occupied households in the Republic during that period (Irish Times 24/9/26). Over 95% of this water was consumed by the Mark Zuckerberg controlled Meta (Facebook, Whatsapp) alone.


Another reason sometimes forwarded in favour of data centres is the job creation that supposedly results. Its true they may employ workers during the construction phase of a project, but once up and running, data centres don’t need many people on an ongoing basis. Even those who remain once a data centre is established, don’t stay in the jobs very long. Data centre operations in Europe and Ireland show a low employee retention rate paired with a relatively short median tenure of 1.8 years. Linkedin data shows a high job turnover, with a minimum of 1,100 professionals changing jobs in a year (Savillis.ie). There is also the increase in AI services, which data centres’ enable. This deskills labour and puts human jobs at risk.


oplus_32


A further concern is the way the data centres are tied-in to the military-industrial complex. The ones in Ireland operated by Google, Microsoft and Amazon host cloud and AI infrastructure that support digital economies and military-connected cloud systems (KPMG.com). Human rights organisations such as the Irish Council for Civil Liberties have raised complaints about this, including the fact that Irish-based storage of data is tied to military and surveillance operations linked to foreign occupations and wars (ICCL.ie). Officially the Irish state claims to be neutral, but ever since World War 2, this has been more a form of neutrality that leans towards certain powers rather than others. The updating of technology is therefore really a continuation of a long-standing approach to intelligence gathering and geopolitics.


Data centres are clearly problematic. Those who have joined the opposition to them hold a combination of motivations, as can be seen in the broad demographics and organisational diversity of those who took part in the recent demonstrations. Along with this multiplicity of people, there is a variety of tactics that can be applied to the issue. At one end of the spectrum, there is the signing of a petition or marches like the ones held in Dublin. A march has its place. It at least raises greater awareness that a problem exists. The difficulty is often that petitions and …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Waves of protests to welcome Trump, Bayan announces
content:
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is so desperate to welcome Donald Trump to the Philippines that he will roll out the red carpet even if his US counterpart arrives so late for the ASEAN Summit and other ASEAN leaders have already left, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) said.


Bayan president Renato Reyes Jr. condemned possibilities of work and school suspension extensions following Department of Foreign Affairs’ announcement that the US leader is set to arrive on the 17

th

 just as the summit he was supposed to attend would be ending. Presidential spokesperson Claire Castro, meanwhile, said Trump’s late arrival is not within Malacanang’s lookout.


“Is Marcos now telling the people that their suffering, and the work and school suspensions, will have to be extended because Trump decided to arrive late for his Philippine visit?” Reyes asked.


Government has declared November 16 to 18 as non-working days to clear Metro Manila of its notorious traffic for its hosting of the biennial event it is hosting this year.


Reyes, however, foisted the possibility of Marcos Jr. extending the work and school holidays as Trump is only set to leave after his dialogue with the Philippine leader on the 18

th

.


“Marcos Jr.’s mendicancy and subservience are on full display now. He is desperate to get a nod from Trump, desperate to get Pax Silica signed, and desperate to get US backing for his isolated regime,” Reyes said.


The activist leader also criticized Trump who he said treats the Philippines “like a doormat, oblivious to the disruption and gross inconvenience his visit makes, on top of the neocolonial policies he wishes to impose.”


Meanwhile, Bayan announced its major rallies will start on Monday with a march to Liwasang Bonifacio where a protest camp will be erected before a rally near the US Embassy.


Tens of thousands of protesters will then march to the venue of the ASEAN Summit on Tuesday, participated in by delegations from all over the country, reminiscent of Trump’s first official visit to the Philippines in 2017.


A similar protest event will be held near Mendiola Bridge in time for the Marcos-Trump meeting in Malacanang on Wednesday.


“The Filipino people will make sure that both Trump and Marcos Jr will emerge as the biggest losers at the end of this week. We reject US imperialism and we oppose government subservience to it,” Reyes said. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Jian Sanz
title: Cops arrest 3 University of Makati students after anti-Pax Silica protest
content:
Police headlocking a UMak studen. (Photo from Anakbayan-UMaK)

Three students of the University of Makati (UMak) who participated in a protest against Pax Silica were arrested earlier today, November 13, in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City.

According to Panday Sining UMak, uniformed police officers and intelligence personnel in plainclothes surrounded the demonstrators, confronting them over an alleged unauthorized assembly and confiscating their placards.

In a statement, Anakbayan UMak condemned the violent, arbitrary arrest. “This is how the rotten government of Marcos Jr. treats students who are peacefully expressing their sentiments,” the group said.

During the dispersal, police officers blocked the students from both sides and forcibly apprehended one participant. Video footage from Karapatan National Capital Region showed that a police officer punched a female student who attempted to free another arrested student. A police officer was captured headlocking one of the arrested students. who can be seen to be put in a headlock by a police officer in another video report.

Karapatan NCR also reported that a paralegal who responded to the forceful arrest was threatened with charges by police officers.

The three students are currently detained at BGC Police Station 1 and face initial charges of alarms and scandal. The arrests unfolded amid youth-led protests across the country, as students rallied against the expected arrival of U.S. President Donald Trump, the chief architect behind the widely opposed Pax Silica initiative, for the ASEAN Summit. (RVO)

author: labor4pal
title: Labor for Palestine at NYC Break the Chain Protest
content:
A post shared by Labor4Palestine (@labor4palestine)

#Labor4Palestine standing with @breakthechain4pal and other orgs today in NYC to tell the Port Authority that we demand an #ArmsEmbargo at @jfkairport and everywhere else! #StopArmingIsrael #BDS #FreeFreePalestine #FromTheRiver2TheSea

A post shared by Luigi Morris (@luigiwmorris)

Stop Weapons Shipments to Israel! Our City Cannot Be a Pipeline for Genocide!

Today, Thursday, November 12, New Yorkers rallied to demand transparency from the Port Authority and an end to weapons shipments to Israel through JFK Airport. JFK is a major hub for military equipment being shipped to Israel. As denounced by the @breakthechain4pal campaign, cargo planes transporting explosives share the same taxiways as passenger aircraft, raising serious public safety concerns. These shipments must end!

The genocide in Gaza continues, and so does the bombing. Just today, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza reportedly killed at least six Palestinians. Despite the supposed ceasefire, Israel continues its attacks on Palestinians, with ongoing military support from the United States. We cannot allow our city’s airport to serve as a pipeline for weapons used to kill Palestinians.

The movement to stop weapons shipments is growing internationally. On October 30, dockworkers organized strikes and protests at more than 100 ports worldwide against militarism, rearmament, and weapons shipments to Israel. In Italy, workers and students have been at the forefront of this struggle, organizing multiple strikes in solidarity with the Palestinian people. They are setting the example!

From the ports of Italy to JFK Airport, workers and communities have the power to stop the machinery of war. New York City cannot claim to be progressive while its infrastructure is used to arm Israel. We need to follow the example of workers internationally, organize from below, and demand an immediate end to weapons shipments, military complicity, and the genocide in Palestine.

Not in our name! Not through our airports!

author: anred
title: Como el 2×1, pero con otro título: la AEDD alerta por una nueva avanzada judicial en favor de los genocidas
content:
La Asociación de Ex Detenidos Desaparecidos (AEDD) denunció una nueva avanzada judicial que podría favorecer a los represores condenados por delitos de lesa humanidad. La advertencia apunta a la Resolución 2867/2026, mediante la cual la Corte Suprema de Justicia aprobó un protocolo médico para unificar los criterios utilizados al evaluar pedidos de prisión domiciliaria por razones de salud. La medida fue firmada por Horacio Rosatti y Carlos Rosenkrantz y podría abrir nuevas oportunidades para que genocidas emblemáticos de la última dictadura, como Alfredo Astiz, Jorge Eduardo Acosta y Christian von Wernich, soliciten cumplir sus condenas fuera de las cárceles. «Los cortesanos que ayer intentaron vender nuestra tierra, hoy quieren regalar nuestro futuro a la impunidad», sentenció la AEDD.

Por ANRed.


«Como el 2×1… pero con otro título», sintetizó la

Asociación de Ex Detenidos Desaparecidos (AEDD)

 en un comunicado difundido a través de sus redes sociales, donde cuestionó que

los mismos jueces que en 2017 intentaron habilitar la aplicación del beneficio del 2×1 a los condenados por crímenes de lesa humanidad vuelvan a impulsar una medida que, aunque no concede automáticamente prisiones domiciliarias, puede incidir en las decisiones judiciales sobre los pedidos de los represores

. La resolución fue firmada el pasado jueves 12 de noviembre y publicada en el Boletín Oficial este lunes 16.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por aedd (@aedd1984)


El protocolo se denomina «Protocolo médico sobre el estado de salud de los internos penitenciarios y las posibilidades de su tratamiento en el establecimiento en el que se encuentran alojados» y, según el texto oficial, su objetivo es establecer criterios científicos para evaluar el estado de salud de las personas detenidas y verificar si las condiciones concretas de los establecimientos penitenciarios permiten garantizar los tratamientos médicos indicados. Dicho protocolo se instala como una herramienta que deberá orientar a los tribunales al momento de resolver la procedencia de una detención domiciliaria.


Si bien no modifica las causales legales ni determina por sí misma la concesión del beneficio, y la decisión continúa en manos de los jueces, l

a preocupación de los organismos de derechos humanos se explica por sus posibles consecuencias sobre los condenados por el terrorismo de Estado

. Entre quienes todavía permanecen alojados en establecimientos penitenciarios se encuentran

Alfredo Astiz

, Jorge Eduardo Acosta y Christian von Wernich

. La AEDD advirtió que la nueva disposición p

uede convertirse en una vía para que algunos de los responsables de los crímenes más graves de la dictadura abandonen las cárceles y continúen cumpliendo sus condenas bajo arresto domiciliario

.


La resolución también reavivó los cuestionamientos por el funcionamiento del máximo tribunal. Aunque la Acordada 21/2026, que había encomendado la elaboración del protocolo en agosto, había sido firmada por Rosatti, Rosenkrantz y Ricardo Lorenzetti, la resolución que finalmente lo aprobó lleva únicamente las firmas de los dos primeros. Según el propio texto, la decisión se adoptó en función de la cantidad de ministros habilitados para participar. La publicación se ordenó para su difusión entre los tribunales penales y las autoridades correspondientes del Poder Ejecutivo.


El antecedente que recupera la AEDD remite al 3 de mayo de 2017, cuando la Corte Suprema declaró aplicable el beneficio del 2×1 al represor Luis Muiña, condenado por delitos de lesa humanidad cometidos en el Hospital Posadas

. La decisión habilitaba computar de manera privilegiada el tiempo que había permanecido detenido preventivamente, mediante una ley que había estado vigente entre 1994 y 2001. La respuesta social fue inmediata:

el 10 de mayo, una movilización multitudinaria en Plaza de Mayo y en distintos puntos del país expresó el rechazo al fallo y a cualquier intento de reducir las condenas de los genocidas

. Días después, el Congreso sancionó la Ley 27.362, que estableció que el 2×1 no es aplicable a delitos de lesa humanidad, genocidio o crímenes de guerra.


La preocupación se inscribe, además, en

un escenario en el que la mayoría de las personas detenidas por estos crímenes ya cumple arresto domiciliario

: según el último informe de la Procuraduría de Crímenes contra la Humanidad, publicado en septiembre de 2026,

author: Bulatlat Staff
title: Int’l groups condemn police brutality
content:
Police officers forcibly grab human rights activists and multisectoral leaders during a protest in Cebu City on November 16, 2026. Screengrab from Bulatlat's video

By Dominic Gutoman and Anne Marxze Umil

International groups denounced the police brutality on November 15, the first day of the 49th ASEAN Summit.

In a statement, the International Association of Democratic Lawyers (IADL) expressed strong condemnation over the violent dispersal and mass arrests of the activists.

They said that instead of arresting international offenders like Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa who has an outstanding International Criminal Court warrant, “the Philippine police and military are using their superior force to harass and arrest peaceful demonstrators and protestors and to stifle dissent and lawful redress of grievances.”

The group stressed that the police brutality and mass arrests are overkill, violating the Philippine Constitution and the country’s laws in the presence of ASEAN member-states, other heads of state, and the United Nations Secretary General.

“The IADL in particular is holding the police Chief PGen Jose Melencio Nartatez, Jr., Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. himself as well as identified individual members of security forces responsible,” the group said in a statement.

The events of the 49th ASEAN Summit happen at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City until November 18, bringing leaders from 11 member-states and representatives of nine dialogue partner-countries.

The Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development (APWLD) stressed that police brutality and state-sanctioned harassment are blatant attacks on fundamental rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly which violates Articles 19 and 21 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR).

“The Philippine government’s actions also violate their international obligations under the UN Declaration on Human Rights Defenders and the UN General Assembly resolution which calls upon all States to take concrete measures to protect human rights defenders and recognise the vital work they do,” APWLD said in a statement. “We call on the international community, civil society organisations and feminist movements across Asia and the Pacific to amplify their demands, release statements of solidarity and support ongoing legal and humanitarian aid for those detained.”

In a press conference on November 16, Jheri Lising, representative of International League of Peoples’ Struggles (ILPS)-US, said that these arrests are part of a broader pattern of repression against people who stand up to US imperialism and its wars of aggression. “The Philippine government is once again demonstrating its willingness to trample on people’s democratic rights to protect US interests. We stand with the Filipino people in opposing Pax Silica, Trump’s visit, and the continuing US intervention in the Philippines.”

June Colcol of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan-US said that “the Filipino people, including our diaspora, have every reason to oppose Trump’s visit and the US economic and military agenda behind it.”

Colcol said that Pax Silica serves US strategic interests, deepens the Philippines’ dependence on foreign capital and technology, and offers no real path to national development. “The Marcos government will not silence us for exposing this agenda. We will not allow these mass arrests to set the tone for the international week of action. We remain indignant and determined to push through with our planned actions and mobilizations, in the Philippines and around the world.”

Arnold Padilla, secretary general of ILPS-Philippines said that the Marcos government will not succeed in silencing them.

“We will not allow yesterday’s arrests to dictate the course of this international week of action. We remain indignant, and we will push through with our plans to expose and oppose the agenda of Trump and Marcos. The demand for accountability will continue to be heard in the streets of the Philippines and across the world,” Padilla said. (DAA)

title: Animal Rising Disrupts National Pig Awards in Central London Following Campaigner Arrests
content:
Animal Rising campaigners disrupted the National Pig Awards at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in central London this evening (16 November), while protesters outside blocked the main entrance. Police were called to the venue.

Despite enhanced security, six campaigners reached the event and were subsequently apprehended before being ejected from the hotel at approximately 7 pm. Around 70 protesters gathered outside as attendees arrived, holding placards reading “Free Luna” and “End Factory Farming”.

The group publicly declared its intention to shut down the awards last week, calling for Red Court, a pig factory farm in Suffolk, to release Luna, a mother pig whose life of confinement was filmed continuously for over a month by Animal Rising earlier this year. [1]

The investigation documented squalid conditions and illegal piglet thumping on the Red Tractor Assured farm. [2] Over 40,000 people have since signed a petition calling for Luna’s release to a sanctuary. [3]

The group filmed Luna confined in a narrow farrowing crate for five weeks, unable to turn around or take more than a step forward. A sanctuary has since offered her a home for the rest of her life. [4]

Red Court confirmed last week that Luna is once again in a farrowing crate. If the farm refuses to release her, she will remain there for approximately another month, confined with her newborn piglets, before she is removed and re-inseminated.

The farm has also rejected a proposed £5,000 donation to You Are Not Alone, an East Anglian charity supporting farmers’ mental health, in exchange for Luna’s release. [5]

Earlier today, Animal Rising announced that a third campaigner, Michelle Farnham, had been arrested on suspicion of burglary following the open rescue of three piglets (Leila, Nova and Maia) from Red Court.

Before the rescue, Animal Rising reported serious welfare concerns at the farm to the police, RSPCA and Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).

APHA, the body responsible for enforcing farmed animal welfare, informed Animal Rising that the farm’s conditions, including the illegal thumping of a piglet, were normal.

Farnham attended Stoke Newington Police Station at 10 am this morning. Her fellow rescuers, Thomas Cusick and Liam Shaughnessy, had previously reported themselves to the police and been arrested. [6]

Farnham, 26, Animal Rising’s Campaign Lead, attracted national attention in September when she spent 21 days and nights locked in a farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square, highlighting Luna’s story and the suffering of animals in factory farms. High-profile visitors included Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [7]

Animal Rising is campaigning for a government commitment to end UK factory farming by 2040.

title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης για τη σύλληψη στις 30/10/24, Πέμπτη 19/11 στις 9:00 στα δικαστήρια Θεσσαλονίκης
content:
Την Πέμπτη 19/11 συνεχίζεται η δίκη της σύλληψης στις 30/10/2024, που ξεκίνησε την Τετάρτη 11/11. Δύο ημέρες μετά τους ξυλοδαρμούς και τις συλλήψεις από την ομάδα ΔΡΑΣΗ στο πάρκο εργατικού κέντρου στις 28/10/2024, πραγματοποιείται πορεία αλληλεγγύης στην περιοχή. Με το τέλος της πορείας πραγματοποιούνται μικρής έκτασης συμπλοκές με την αστυνομία. Μετά από λίγη ώρα δυνάμεις της αστυνομίας κατεβαίνουν στην Γκαρμπολά και πραγματοποιούν επιθέσεις σε κόσμο που βρίσκεται στην περιοχή. Έπειτα από αντεγκλήσεις με κόσμο που βρίσκεται σε κατάστημα στον πεζόδρομο, η αστυνομία επιτίθεται ρίχνοντας δακρυγόνο μέσα στο μαγαζί, χτυπώντας συγκεντρωμένους και σπάζοντας τραπέζια. Ταυτόχρονα εξαπολύει κυνηγητό σε κόσμο που προσπαθούσε να ξεφύγει από τα δακρυγόνα και πραγματοποιείται μία σύλληψη ατόμου που δεν πρόλαβε να μπει σε κατάστημα στην Τοσίτσα για να προστατευτεί.


Ολόκληρο το ρεπορτάζ για τα δύο περιστατικά εδώ: 

https://www.facebook.com/infolibregr/posts/pfbid02q9HH4eLyWUv4aFkEBFGiPMJJepUmTK75Uma39mvGUB8dtq3tiYQXno8hd7Rw1nTwl


Το κάλεσμα για την Πέμπτη 19/11:


ΕΝΗΜΕΡΩΣΗ ΑΠΟ ΤΗΝ ΠΡΩΤΗ ΔΙΚΑΣΙΜΟ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΗ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗΣ ΣΤΑ ΔΙΚΑΣΤΗΡΙΑ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΣΤΙΣ 19/11/26


Στις 11/11/26 εκδικάζονταν δύο υποθέσεις, η μία από τις 28/10/24 και η άλλη από 30/10/24. Η πρώτη αφορούσε τον ξυλοδαρμό και τις συλλήψεις κόσμου σε τυχαίο έλεγχο της ομάδας ΔΡΑΣΗ στο πάρκο του ΕΚΘ και η δεύτερη το πογκρόμ των δυνάμεων καταστολής μετά τη λήξη της πορείας που ακολούθησε δύο μέρες αργότερα (Περισσσότερα για το ιστορικό εδω:

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1643142/

). Η πρώτη υπόθεση πήρε αναβολή επειδή έλειπαν οι μάρτυρες κατηγορίας, ενώ η δεύτερη ξεκίνησε. Βασική επιδίωξη της Αστυνομικής διέυθυνσης Θεσ/νίκης ήταν να μην εκδικαστούν οι δύο υποθέσεις μαζί, μη τυχόν και αναδειχθεί σε σερί ακροαματικών διαδικασιών το επίπεδο αυθαιρεσίας στο οποίο επιχειρεί το σώμα γενικότερα και συγκεκριμένα η ομάδα ΔΡΑΣΗ (που πραγματοποίησε όλες τις συλλήψεις του διημέρου). Η ΕΛ.ΑΣ λοιπόν κατάφερε να απομπλέξει τις δύο υποθέσεις, όσον αφορά την έδρα και την μέρα εκδίκασης. Σχετικά με το δικαστήριο που αφορά τις συλλήψεις μετά την πορεία, κατέθεσε ο μάρτυρας κατηγορίας ενώ η έδρα διέκοψε για την Πέμπτη

(19/11/26 στις 9:00)

 όπου και θα συνεχιστεί με τις καταθέσεις των μαρτύρων υπεράσπισης, των κατηγορούμενων και την ολοκλήρωση της διαδικασίας.


Η συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης πλαισιώθηκε από 50 συντρόφια, παρέμεινε μέχρι το τέλος μπροστά από την είσοδο και εξέθεσε εκ νέου το παράλογο του ιδεολογικού face-control που εφαρμόζει η ΕΛ.ΑΣ τους τελευταίους μήνες στα δικαστήρια της Θεσ/νίκης. Δικαστική αστυνομία, ΜΑΤ, ασφαλίτες και αξιωματικοί υπηρεσίας καθόντουσαν μπροστά στην είσοδο των δικαστηρίων επί ώρες αφήνοντας να περνάνε εκατοντάδες άνθρωποι και απαγορεύοντας επί της ουσίας την είσοδο στο κτήριο σε αλληλέγγυο κόσμο. Στα πλαίσια αυτής της ευφάνταστης κατασταλτικής παράνοιας, απαγόρευαν την είσοδο μέχρι και λίγο πριν την έναρξη της δίκης στους μάρτυρες υπεράσπισης, ενώ κοντοστάθηκαν ακόμα και σε συγγενείς. Οι επικεφαλείς τους ανέφεραν για ακόμη μια φορά μια προφορική εντολή της προισταμένης εισαγγελέως των δικαστηρίων. Έγινε μια απόπειρα επικοινωνίας δικηγόρων μαζί της για να αποσαφηνιστεί περί τίνος πρόκειται, ωστόσο αυτό δε κατέστη εφικτό από πλευράς της. Όποια και αν είναι αυτή η προφορική εντολή

(αποκλείεται όντως αυτό το πράγμα να έχει τη μορφή γραπτής αποτύπωσης), από όποια διαχρονική λίστα επιθυμιών του απρόσωπου κρατικού αυταρχισμού και αν έχει προκύψει και ασχέτως του πως εξειδικεύεται, το μόνο σίγουρο είναι ότι στοχεύει στην αποσυσπείρωση του κόσμου, την απονοηματοδότηση της πολιτικής δίκης και την τραμπούκα. Η ξεφτίλα του να μπαίνουν εκατοντάδες άνθρωποι μέσα στα δικαστήρια ενώ ο αλληλέγγυος κόσμος όχι, έληξε μόνο όταν ξεκίνησε η δίκη, με τα συντρόφια να γεμίζουν την αίθουσα μετά από πολλές ώρες επίμονης διεκδίκησης του αυτονόητου. Την Πέμπτη στις 19/11/26 θα συνεχιστεί η δίκη που αφορά τις συλλήψεις στην Τοσίτσα και καλούμε τον κόσμο του αγώνα να στηρίξει με την παρουσία του σε αυτό όπως και σε όσα δικαστήρια έπονται το επόμενο χρονικό διάστημα απλώνοντας μια ασπίδα προστασίας γύρω από τα όποια διωκόμενα συντρόφια, τα κεκτημένα και τα επίδικα του αγώνα. Απέναντι στις ανεξάντλητες κατασταλτικές εφεδρείες του κρατικού μηχανισμού και τις διάφορες θεσμικές εκδοχές θέσπισης ιδιώνυμων, το μόνο που έχουμε είναι ο ένας την άλλη. Κόντρα σε λογικές ιδιώτευσης και ανάθεσης, αντιπροτάσουμε τη δέσμευση και τη συντροφικότητα.

Όσα είπαμε παλιότερα ισχύουν …

author: Kodao Productions
title: ‘Savage Sunday’ arrests biggest in Philippine history
content:
With at least 276 protesters currently detained at Camp Bagong Diwa (CBD) in Taguig City and eight others arrested in Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government on Sunday has committed the biggest mass arrest in the country’s history on Sunday.


Surpassing the record 244 mass arrested in the anti-corruption and anti-martial law protests in September 21, 2025, yesterday’s savage apprehensions reportedly also came with beatings of protesters under police custody.


“[S]everal other delegates remain unaccounted for, with reports that they were taken to other locations. Their exact number and whereabouts are still being verified,” the group Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan reported on Sunday night.


The hundreds apprehended at Sucat People’s Park in Muntinlupa City on Saturday afternoon were taken to CBD, headquarters of the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) while those arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio were taken to undisclosed precincts around Manila.


The savagery included the spraying of human feces and urine before the statue of national hero Andres Bonifacio, a sacred spot for the Filipino working class, by suspected government agents to prevent protesters from erecting a protest camp.


The arrests came as Marcos Jr. opened the 49th Association of South East Asian Nations Summit and anticipating the arrival of US President Donald Trump on Tuesday.


CHR, lawyers, doctors denied access


Volunteer lawyers, paralegals, and medical professionals, as well as the Commission on Human Rights were denied access to the detainees for hours, until finally allowed access before midnight last night.


It was the first time the injured were given medical attention and food since their arrest at about 2:30 PM.


Atty. Abigail Joy Aman, one of the volunteer lawyers at the scene, said they have been requesting access to the detainees at CBD since 5PM but were refused by the police who insisted government lawyers were already “processing” the arrestees.


“We kept telling them that the detainees have the right to be represented by lawyers of their choice. [And when we were finally allowed inside], they were those who told us they were punched in the gut,” Aman told reporters.


Aman added the detainees were not committing any crime at the time of the arrest.


Lakbayan confirmed their delegates were manhandled by the police, several sustaining injuries, bruises, and complain of difficulty in walking.


“Their detention conditions are equally alarming. They are being held in an extremely hot, poorly ventilated facility with inadequate water supply, endangering their health and well-being,” the group said in a statement.


The Lakbayan originally planned to march to Liwasang Bonifacio but were delayed by blockades in Binan, Laguna on Friday and were forced to spend the night at Sucat. While resting for the night, the Southern Police District cordoned the area and subsequently mass arrested the anti-Donald Trump protesters.


Scores of journalists arrested


Two Southern Tagalog Exposure reporters, one Altermidya Network correspondent, three College Editors Guild of the Philippines coordinators, and 12 student journalists were likewise arrested in Muntinlupa on Sunday. Several suffered injuries from the brutal arrests.


The University of the Philippines-Los Banos (UPLB) Office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs (OVCSA) condemned the mass arrest of their students and other participants. Nine of the arrestees from staff members of UPLB Perspective, the school’s official student publication.


“The right to peaceful assembly, freedom of expression, and collective action is guaranteed under the Philippine Constitution. Students and citizens must be able to express dissent, raise legitimate grievances, and participate in democratic processes without fear of intimidation, arbitrary arrest, or repression,” OVCSA said.


A lawyer from the Presidential Task Force on Media Security tried to negotiate their release from police custody but had been unsuccessful so far.


At Liwasang Bonifacio, two Tinig ng Plaridel (TNP, student publication of the UP College of Media and Communication) reporters narrowly escaped arrest by the police, an incident condemned by Dean Diosa Labiste.


The two student journalists were documenting manhandling of a protester when verbally abused by Manila Police District officers who attempted to arrest them. Once of the staffers suffered minor abrasions, the publication said …

title: Genel müdür ve yardımcısı tutuklanmıştı: Türkiye Sigorta fondan 1.6 milyar lira kazanç sağlamış
content:
Eski Genel Müdürü Taha Çakmak ve Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Gürol Sami Özer’in tutuklandığı Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat Emeklilik fon kazancının enflasyon etkisi düşüldükten sonra hesaplanan 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin liralık bölümünü TMSF’ye iade etti.

Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformuna (KAP) yaptığı açıklamada, tasfiye sürecine alınan yatırım fonlarından geçmişte elde ettiği kazancın yaklaşık 1.6 milyar liralık bölümünü Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’na (TMSF) iade ettiğini belirten Türkiye sigorta, bu tutarın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 lira olduğunu açıkladı.

Türkiye Sigorta tasfiye kapsamındaki fonların bir bölümüne geçmişte yatırım yaptığını, söz konusu yatırımların yapıldıkları tarihlerde yürürlükte bulunan mevzuata ve şirketin yatırım politikasına uygun olduğunu ileri sürmüştü. Türkiye sigorta TMSF ve Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) ile yapılan görüşmelerin ardından kazancın “gönüllü iade” kapsamında iade edildiğini açıkladı.

Şirketin açıklamasına göre iade tutarı, fonlardan elde edilen alım-satım kazancından yatırım süresine karşılık gelen enflasyon etkisinin çıkarılmasıyla hesaplandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Victoria Python
title: EFF’s AI Cybersecurity Policy Framework
content:
The news has been filled with stories recently of AI breaching the security of websites. And while it may feel like a new problem because of AI’s involvement, it turns out that there are longstanding existing cybersecurity safety best practices that these companies—some of the largest tech companies in the world—could and should have taken to prevent these breaches.


Recent cybersecurity incidents have shown that some of the world’s largest tech companies have failed to take basic security precautions when testing frontier AI systems on internet-connected systems. Unfortunately, these failures resulted in breaches of numerous third-party websites, including an AI research-sharing platform called Hugging Face and the Australian healthcare system’s website. Even worse, AI developers failed to detect most of the incidents until long after they occurred due to inadequate monitoring of the AI systems during testing. Had the companies abided by basic, common sense security protocols, these incidents likely would not have occurred.


While the White House and leaders of major AI companies have claimed that no action is necessary, understandably, lawmakers at all levels and of both parties are proposing legislation to create new, additional safety protocols. These incidents may warrant legislative action. However, the good news is that post-incident reports indicate

new

 protocols are largely unnecessary. Following

existing

 best practices would have been enough to prevent the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident and others like it. In other words, responsible AI developers can take immediate action to protect the public by implementing well-established security precautions as they develop and test their systems.


Lawmakers should start by referencing existing legal protections, including claims like negligence, gross negligence, trespass to chattels, Section 1201 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), and computer trespass statutes like the Consumer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) and analogous state law provisions, such as Section 502 of the California Penal Code.


Policymakers can help protect the public by requiring AI developers to follow established security protocols—and creating legal liability for failing to do so. These policies would protect the public from irresponsible actions by AI developers without impeding innovation. To the extent that gaps in existing laws warrant new legislation, EFF recommends the following policy framework:


STATUTORY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:

Lawmakers should enact legislation that requires AI developers to adhere to well-established cybersecurity best practices when testing AI systems, such as strong sandboxing and network isolation, least-privilege access, effective logging and monitoring, and clear incident-response procedures


REGULATORY STANDARDS:

Congress should require an existing federal agency, such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

1

, to adopt safety standards for pre-deployment development and testing of generative AI systems, based on the established best practices referenced above. The agency should be required to update the standards every 2 years, or earlier as needed due to reported security incidents and/or major technological advancements. These standards should be developed in consultation with academic and nonprofit AI researchers, civil liberties organizations, and commercial AI developers, and adopted through formal agency rulemaking following a notice and comment process. That consultation should include an assessment of potential adverse impacts on competition, with the goal of ensuring that regulatory standards do not effectively lock out potential competitors.


LIABILITY:

The law should provide for civil liability for AI development and testing that results in unauthorized access to a third party system, if performed under conditions that do not satisfy cybersecurity standards adopted by NIST, or another federal agency responsible for adopting these regulations, unless the company proves it acted reasonably under the circumstances to prevent unauthorized access to third party system 


ENFORCEMENT:

Both federal and state authorities should be able to hold AI developers accountable where they have failed to meet the minimum standards adopted by the designated federal agency, such as NIST. Providing for state—in addition to federal—enforcement power reduces the risk of regulatory capture. Regulators should require …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: The death of the word?
content:
Michelangelo,

Cumaean Sibyl

 (c. 1511), Sistine Chapel, Vatican City


This short article was originally published under the title “Morte della parola?” in the Italian newspaper

Paese Sera

 on 8 February 1968. It has been republished in the latest issue of the French magazine

Entétement

, although the original version can be found on the

La Voce di Fiore

 archive website. A Spanish translation of the same can be found at th magazine

Ficción de la razón

.


A book has recently been published in Paris,

Of Grammatology

 (1967), a work destined to cause a stir not only in the field of linguistic studies. Jacques Derrida, one of the most original figures in the new wave of French philosophical criticism, begins with the observation that, today, “through a movement whose necessity we can barely glimpse, everything that, for at least twenty centuries, has tended to be defined under the name of language, is beginning to be summarised under the name of writing”. It does indeed seem that writing—which, according to Rousseau, was nothing more than a complement to speech—is gradually freeing itself from its subordination to the phonetic medium, to the point of reversing its traditional relationship with language: writing would therefore not be a technique in the service of language, but rather, on the contrary, it is language that can be considered a specific case, an aspect, of writing.


To better understand the phenomenon to which Derrida refers when he speaks of writing dissociated from the phonetic element, one need only consider the example of mathematics, whose symbolic notation does not refer to any spoken language. If we consider that today we are witnessing a process of mathematisation across all the sciences, the “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon (readers who have followed recent news regarding the

in vitro

 synthesis of living matter, carried out by certain American scientists, will recall having heard talk of writing and “programmes” even in relation to the most elementary processes of the living cell). The “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon.


On the basis of these premises, Derrida deduces the need for a pure science of writing, which considers writing prior to speech and independently of it: this science is, precisely, “grammatology”; and, to define its aims, it suffices to substitute this term for “semiology”, the term Saussure uses to outline the programme of his famous

Course in General Linguistics

: “We shall call it grammatology… and, as it does not yet exist, we cannot say what it will be; but it has a right to exist, and its place is determined in advance”. The age of speech, which began under the creative power of the verb, is drawing to a close before our very eyes; the character of this new age might be summed up in the following formula: “In the beginning was the written word’’.


Whilst it is true that, from this perspective, linguistics must become a mere branch of grammatology, Derrida seems, however, to overlook the fact that a science already exists which considers language not as speech, but as code and writing; consequently, grammatology itself should necessarily be understood as a sub-branch or a section of that science. This is cybernetics, which, from its beginnings in Wiener’s theories, defined its world as a universe of writing and coding. The very idea of grammatology is already fully contained within the notion of “programme”, one of the key concepts of cybernetics. Etymologically, “programme” —pro-grammer— means “to put the letter (that is,

writing

) first”, whilst “prophecy” means, by contrast, “to put the word first”. Indeed, in the programme assigned to an electronic brain, everything that constitutes the living, phonetic element of language is erased to make way for a system of absolute writing that can be deciphered but not pronounced. It is fair to say that, up to now, our civilisation has known two types of language that have gradually diverged: the language of science is, essentially, written language —code, writing—, whilst the language of poetry and philosophical thought is spoken language —breath, word—. Nevertheless, these two domains—which, for convenience’s sake, we might call the “sphere of the programme” and the “sphere of prophecy”—are drawing ever closer together today thanks to cybernetics; through the mathematisation of human phenomena, cybernetics …

author: By Sophia Potsi, Contributor
title: Europe’s Broken Promise: From Open Camps to High-Tech Prisons
content:
Greek Islands – In 2015, the Greek island of Lesvos was the epicenter of the so-called migration crisis. With arrivals reaching 2,000 people per day, images from the island reflected the solidarity of the locals. Fishermen were seen pulling people out of the water and elderly women took care of newborns in village squares. The islanders’ response of solidarity with people fleeing war was so remarkable that they were nominated for a Nobel Peace Prize.


For a while, Lesvos was a place that functioned as an in-between, an island that people stayed for a little bit and then left to continue their journey to Europe. But after the EU-Turkey deal in 2016, the islands were turned from places that people passed to places that people were held. From passageways they became waiting rooms in closed camps on the edge of Europe. 


And this is how Moria was built, the camp that in the following years would become a symbol of Europe’s brutal containment and inhumane policies and treatment against refugees, migrants, and people on the move.


Moria: Suffering and Resilience


Moria camp, formally known as the Moria Reception and Identification Center, was the largest refugee camp in Europe. It was originally built to hold 3,000 people, and had help up to 20,000 people at peak times before it burned down in 2020. 


The conditions in the camp were horrible. There was no running water, no sewage system and almost no healthcare. People were living in limbo in makeshift shelters waiting years for their asylum decision. 


It was a place of suffering and a

mental health crisis

 unfolded with reported suicide attempts, self-harm, panic attacks and anxiety. 


Yet, the camp allowed the residents to have some agency. Showing resilience, the residents built a mosque, a barber shop, and a makeshift oven. 


Residents showed solidarity with each other and

organized themselves

 to push for better living conditions, cleaned up the camp, and ran schools.


“Welcome to Europe” graffiti on the outside walls of Moria camp. Photo contributed by Sophia Potsi.


The Fire


In September 2020 Moria camp burned to the ground. 


Six people, five of them minors, were arrested and charged with arson and were dubbed the Moria Six. Greek authorities claimed the fire was deliberately lit by camp residents. The Greek Minister of Migration and Asylum at the time, Notis Mitarachi,

posted to social media

 that “the arsonists of Moria have been detained [and] the safety of everyone is guaranteed.” 


However,

Forensic Architecture

 later reconstructed the events on the night of the fire from hundreds of videos and testimonies and found the fire most likely came from improvised electrical connections among flammable tent-like shelters in hot, dry, windy conditions. This conclusion was supported by Lesvos fire department’s own report. Prior to the September 2020 fire, there had been 247 fire outbreaks in the camp.


Of the six people charged, two were tried as minors and released after four years. The other four were initially found guilty but then released after three and a half years in prison after they were acquitted of the charges and cleared in

2025

.


As the chapter closed on Moria, the European Union

made promises

 that there would be “no more Morias.”


A wall at one of the entrances in Moria has writing on it that reads, “You cannot repaır the hell. Let’s people to be free! One Day.” Photo contributed by Sophia Potsi.


The Replacement Camp


What replaced Moria in Lesvos, supposedly as a temporary solution, was the Mavrovouni camp, often called Kara Tepe. Facing the sea just outside of Mytilene are rows and rows of the same white containers. It looks like every other camp in Greece with no sign that anyone has made the place their own. 


It exists to keep people in containers, fed and counted, and almost nothing else. Compared with the chaos and terror of Moria it is an improvement but there are still issues with sanitation, water and electricity.  


The biggest additions are the restricted movement of residents and the intensified surveillance. Security guards stand at the gate. No journalists or NGO workers can enter freely. 


Residents have their

life controlled

 by police, private security and various procedures with set times to come and go mediated by ID checks and bag searches at checkpoints.


While this model is far more restrictive than the one seen in Moria, the country has unveiled even more strict systems for future …

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Peasant organizer persists despite surveillance
content:
Jesus Monasterial. (Photo from Photo from Tanggol Magsasaka-TK)

Repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety.

When he was a university student, he questioned the purpose of agricultural education. Now he is organizing landless farmers and fisherfolk.

Jesus Monasterial has spent more than two years working with rural communities in Southern Tagalog. However, his work resulted in repeated surveillance by state forces, peasant groups said.

On October 31, Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan reported that a police intelligence operative identified as “Bruno” had been asking about Monasterial’s whereabouts in Lian, Batangas. The operative was reportedly previously assigned in Nasugbu.

At the time, Monasterial was assisting a protest camp in Barangay San Diego, where farmers, fisherfolk, and residents opposed the possible demolition of several houses.

“I was on my way back to the people’s protest camp in San Diego when news reached us that someone had been asking about my personal information,” he said.

The camp was established by Samahang Mangangawil 1979 and the San Diego Homeowners’ Association, with support from the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK) and Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas–Timog Katagalugan (PAMALAKAYA-TK).

The incident prompted fellow organizers to discuss security measures. They also plan to file a complaint before the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).

Monasterial’s involvement in peasant organizing began at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) where he was enrolled in BS Agricultural Biotechnology.

Coming from a family of farmers in Bicol, where his grandparents worked as agricultural tenants, he became increasingly critical of an agricultural education system that he said served the interests of transnational corporations rather than addressing farmers’ lack of land and government support.

Through the League of Filipino Students–UPLB, he became involved in social issues action and joined community immersions with farmers in Tartaria, Silang, Cavite, as well as Mangyan communities in Mindoro and Dumagat communities in Rizal.

These experiences led him to leave his studies and become a full-time organizer. He now serves as deputy secretary-general of KASAMA-TK.

His work involves staying in communities, conducting consultations and political education, and helping establish local farmers and fisherfolk associations.

“Being a full-time organizer means devoting my entire time to the communities and being far from my loved ones,” he said, adding that he had to set aside his plan to finish college.

The October 31 incident was not the first reported surveillance involving Monasterial.

On July 19, 2026, soldiers from the 16th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army reportedly sought to identify the organizers of KASAMA-TK’s Regional Peasant Consultation in Barangay Malinis, Lemery, Batangas.

On September 21, a man introducing himself as “Del” Dela Cruz reportedly approached a member of Sugarfolks’ Unity for Genuine Agricultural Reform (SUGAR-Batangas), attempting to persuade the member to leave the organization and provide information about its activities.

According to Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan, the man showed footage of a protest outside the Department of Agriculture regional office led by the Alyansa ng Magsasaka para sa Kumpensasyon (AMK), SUGAR-Batangas, KAISAHAN, and KASAMA-TK. He allegedly warned the member against working with Monasterial, claiming that the organizer was “already drawing attention.”

The protest resulted in a dialogue with government representatives to demand agricultural inputs and implements for farmers and farmworkers affected by successive calamities.

The groups also cited previous incidents in Barangay Casile, Laguna; Lupang Ramos and Tartaria, Cavite; and Coron, Palawan.

Monasterial said that the repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety. “Repeated surveillance limits my movements as an organizer and makes me fear returning home to my family because they might also be targeted by the state due to my advocacy.”

Despite the threats, Monasterial said that his work remains rooted in the struggles of farmers and farmworkers.

In Batangas, he witnessed sugarcane cutters and loaders receiving only P350 to P400 for every ton of cane harvested and loaded onto trucks. Their wages are paid at the …

author: dev
title: Habiter au corps d'un âne mort ou le chemin de Nietzsche
content:
Dans la continuité des très nombreux articles que nous avons publiés afin de déchiffrer l'Intelligence artificielle, le monde qu'elle avale, celui qu'elle charrie et celui qu'elle produit, nous partageons cette semaine l'épatante découverte d'Olivier Chiran et Pierre Muzin. La première occurrence de l'expression IA reviendrait au célèbre philosophe Friedrich Nietzsche dans le tout aussi célèbre

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

, un tiret séparait néanmoins les deux voyelles :

« Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit. »


« Donnez-moi du travail, de la fatigue,


de la douleur et de l'enthousiasme. »


George Sand


1.


Pour savoir précisément où nous en sommes, mais aussi faire face à ce qui nous arrive, alors que l'intelligence artificielle étend son emprise sur le monde et les vies, nous avons besoin d'un sémaphore.


2.


On dit que l'expression « intelligence artificielle » a été lancée par John McCarthy, en 1956, lors de la conférence de Dartmouth, coup d'envoi du programme de recherche consacré à la reproduction algorithmique de la pensée humaine. Soixante-douze ans plus tôt, en 1884, Friedrich Nietzsche, le célèbre philosophe allemand, rédige son grand poème philosophique :

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

. Dans la troisième partie de cet ouvrage (trouvée « sous le ciel alcyonien de Nice », dira-t-il), il écrit : « Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit

 [

1

]

. » Première apparition de ces deux lettres, longtemps avant Dartmouth. Évidence de leur rapprochement – en même temps que, d'un simple tiret, de leur mise à distance. On pourrait s'étonner que les traducteurs français (Henri Albert en 1903, Geneviève Bianquis en 1969) aient fait le choix, au lieu du « hi-han » conventionnel, de les conserver telles quelles. Mais le texte allemand dit bien : «

Immer I-A sagen – das lernte allein der Esel, und wer seines Geistes ist

 ! » – Nietzche ayant délibérément fait tomber le

h

 de «

iah

 », braiment de l'âne dans la langue de Goethe. Nous dirons donc, quant à nous, que l'histoire de l'I-A commence à la fin du xixe siècle, lorsqu'un philosophe visionnaire, cheminant à flanc de montagne, a compris qu'on pouvait arracher au cri de l'âne sa puissance d'exclamation intempestive – et qu'il y avait là, pour nous, un grand danger

 [

2

]

.


3.


C'est qu'il y a deux ânes. Gilles Deleuze, commentant les propos de Nietzsche : « On aurait pu croire que l'âne, l'animal qui dit I-A, était l'animal dionysiaque par excellence. En fait, il n'en est rien ; son apparence est dionysiaque, mais toute sa réalité est chrétienne

 [

3

]

. » Le braiment sans son ou ses

h

, c'est cette manière qu'a l'âne de dire toujours oui – mais un faux oui, une fausse affirmation qui ne sait pas dire non, qui ne sait qu'acquiescer face à ce qui est. Bêtise. Démission de la pensée. Obscurantisme. Post-vérité. Positivisme logique. (Margaret Thatcher : «

There is no alternative

 » → TINA : « I-A ! I-A ! ») Toutes choses contre lesquelles, justement, la philosophie s'évertue à lutter. « Le réel tel qu'il est, conclut Deleuze, c'est une idée d'âne. »


4.


Il arrive aussi, on le sait, que l'âne se cabre. L'I-A approbatif que dénoncent les philosophes est la forme mutilée de ce « hi-han ! » qui est à la fois refus catégorique et cri pour l'autonomie et la liberté. Entre les deux, il y a toute la différence entre l'âne vivant (dionysiaque) et l'âne mort (chrétien) – entre l'appel à la révolte et le bourdon béat de la fanfare. (« Si l'âne contribue peu à l'harmonie durant sa vie, écrivait-on au milieu du xixe siècle, il la sert généreusement après sa mort, lui fournissant les meilleures peaux qui existent pour les grosses caisses et les meilleurs tibias pour fabriquer des clarinettes

 [

4

]

. »)


5.


Dans

L'Âne

, de Lucius de Patras, le narrateur voit une magicienne se transformer en oiseau après s'être frotté le corps avec un onguent

 [

5

]

. Ayant voulu l'imiter, il se retrouve, quant à lui, métamorphosé en âne. Séquestré par une bande de brigands, il tente de leur échapper en emportant avec lui, dans sa fuite, une jeune prisonnière. Par malchance, les brigands retrouvent les fuyard

·

title: Lieblingsstreberin: Paula Saunders
content:
In der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ gerät Tatiana Maslany als geschiedene Mutter in einen Scam aus Cybersex, Erpressung und Verschwörung.

Geschiedene Soccer Mom, gewissenhafte Fact-Checkerin, falsch Verdächtigte? Paula Saunders (Tatiana Maslany), Protagonistin der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“, lässt sich auf kein Label festlegen. Sie jongliert mit einem Sorgerechtsstreit und einem schlecht bezahlten Medien-Vollzeitjob – worüber sie sich beim Online-Sexarbeiter Trevor ausheult, der ihr empathisch zuhört, solange sie ihn bezahlt. Bis Trevor plötzlich bei ihrer Camsex-Session entführt wird. Kurze Zeit später kriegt sie einen Anruf, dass sie 15.000 Dollar zahlen soll, um ihn freizukaufen. Von der Polizei wird sie mit dem Hinweis, dass das sicher Betrug ist, abgewimmelt. Als sie nicht zahlt, wird sie mit Cybersex-Aufnahmen erpresst. Da das Sorgerecht für ihre Tochter auf dem Spiel steht, nimmt sie die Sache selbst in die Hand und spürt anhand von ein paar wackeligen Screenshots und einer Überweisung die Erpresser*innen auf. Sie beherrscht alle Techniken der Open-Source-Recherche, ist kreativ und fokussiert, wenn es darum geht, die Fakten herauszufinden. Bis die Frage aufkommt: Wer sind eigentlich die Scammer hinter Trevor? Während die Darstellung von Online-Sexarbeiter*innen als „Scammer“ klischeehaft ausfällt, finden sich alle menschlichen Ambivalenzen in Paulas Charakter wieder, was sicher auch Tatiana Maslanys schauspielerischem Können zu verdanken ist. Paula wird von einer Mischung aus Erpressung, Gewalt und Tatendrang weiter in den Scam hineingezogen, bis sie der ziemlich nutzlosen Polizei immer verdächtiger erscheint. Dabei will Paula nach eigenen Angaben nur eine gute Mutter sein und legt sich dafür regelmäßig mit ihrem Ex-Mann Karl (Jake Johnson) an. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Wenn sie nur ihre Unschuld beweisen und die große Verschwörung aufdecken könnte, die sie in die Situation gebracht hat … Die Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ ist auf Apple TV verfügbar, eine zweite Staffel ist geplant. author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: Scott Timcke
title: The Stories Shaping Africa’s AI Future
content:
In the boardrooms of Addis Ababa and the tech hubs of Nairobi, a new worldmaking project is underway. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the central arenas where African states negotiate their position in an unequal global order. To speak of “AI in Africa” is not simply to describe the arrival of a technology, but to encounter a set of competing discursive frames through which political desires, developmental ambitions, ethical claims, and governance priorities are translated into technical agendas. As national strategies and regional protocols are rolled out, what comes into view is a struggle over how Africa is imagined within this machine age, and what kinds of futures that imagination makes thinkable.


These frames are not simply different ways of describing a new technology. They are competing scripts for what Africa is, what AI is for, and who ought to shape its future. Some cast the continent as a site of leapfrogging and renewal; others as a zone of exposure, extraction, sovereignty, moral repair, or improvised adaptation. Each brings some actors and possibilities into focus while pushing others to the margins. That is why the issue is not only what AI means for Africa, but what pictures of Africa are being called into view through AI discourse.


The first terrain is shaped by promise and protection. One of the most pervasive registers is promissory. In the African renaissance 2.0 frame, visible in the

AU Continental AI Strategy

, AI appears as a

leapfrogging

 device through which Africa can bypass the chokepoint of traditional industrialization and enter prosperity through technical modernization. Here, the ethical subject is the developmental state or planner charged with delivering growth, inclusion, and renewal. What comes into view is capacity, competitiveness, and beneficial transformation. What recedes from view are the historical and political-economic conditions that make acceleration so attractive in the first place: debt, infrastructural dependence, uneven ownership, and the possibility that AI may deepen rather than overcome inherited asymmetries.


Running alongside this is a protective register. In this vulnerability frame, Africa is not late but exposed to surveillance, bias, exclusion, and systems introduced into settings where safeguards are weak and redress is limited. As the

CIVICUS report on AI surveillance in Africa

 suggests, the issue is not only future risk but already existing forms of technologically mediated harm. The ethical subject here is the harm-bearing population—the data subject, precarious worker, surveilled citizen, and linguistically marginal user most likely to absorb the costs of badly governed AI. This frame is ethically indispensable because it foregrounds rights, harm, and institutional fragility, including the uneven but growing architecture of data protection on the continent. Its limit, however, is that it can cast Africa chiefly as a site to be protected rather than one from which technological futures are actively contested and shaped.


A second terrain is shaped by structure and sovereignty. Alongside these promissory and protective registers sits a more structural critique. In the

anti-colonial frame

, AI appears as a socio-technical order built through unequal material relations: not only data extraction, but also mineral supply chains, outsourced labor, environmental degradation, foreign-owned infrastructures, and asymmetrical control over the institutions that govern digital life. From this perspective, Africa is not outside the AI order looking in; it is already deeply inserted into it, though often on subordinated terms. The ethical subject is the dispossessed worker, community, or polity whose labor, resources, and data are drawn into AI systems while ownership and value are captured elsewhere. What becomes visible is the political economy of AI—an approach that makes it harder to sustain the comforting idea that Africa’s main problem is simply one of readiness or delayed entry. But the frame has limits. In foregrounding dispossession, it can flatten internal differentiation, externalize agency too completely, and become so totalizing that the uneven realities of negotiation and strategic inhabitation recede from view.


The sovereignty frame shifts the question from extraction to control: AI is cast as a problem of authority over infrastructure, procurement, standards, and rulemaking, a concern visible in South Africa’s

National …

title: Avrupa | Yüzbinlerce genç 20 Kasım'a hazırlanıyor: “Geleceğimiz için, onların savaşlarına karşı”
content:
Gençlik ve öğrenci örgütleri tüm Avrupa ülkelerinde 20 Kasım Cuma günü, “Fight for Our Future, Not Their Wars” (Geleceğimiz için, onların savaşlarına karşı) sloganıyla ortak eylem gününe hazırlanıyor. Uluslararası Gençlik Grevi Koalisyonu'nun 11 Kasım'daki açıklamasına göre 25'i aşkın ülkede kıtadaki yüzlerce kentte okul boykotları, üniversite eylemleri ve gösteriler planlanıyor.


Koalisyon etkinliğe yüz binlerce gencin katılmasını bekliyor. Ancak henüz ülkeler özgülünde doğrulanmış bir katılım tahmini bulunmuyor. 


Savaş değil sosyal haklar için bütçe


Haziranda Köln'deki uluslararası buluşmanın ardından gelişen koalisyon, 10 Ağustos'ta ortak grev çağrısını duyurmuştu. Hareketin manifestosu, askerî harcamaların artırılması ve eğitim, sağlık ve sosyal hizmetlerdeki kesintiler arasındaki dolaysız bağdan yola çıkıyor. Manifesto'nun temel yönelimleri kendi ifadeleriyle şöyle özetleniyor: 


Savaş ve sosyal haklar:


“Askerî harcamalar tarihsel rekor düzeylere ulaşırken eğitim, sağlık, konut ve kamu hizmetleri yeniden silahlanmayı finanse etmek için feda ediliyor.”


Gençliğin geleceği:


“Bu geleceği reddediyoruz.”


Uluslararası örgütlenme:


“Geleceğimizi tehdit eden, bizi sömüren ve baskı altında tutan sistem uluslararası olduğu için mücadelemiz de uluslararasıdır.”


Hareketin siyasal yönelimi:


“Otoriterliğe ve baskıya karşı, demokratik haklarımızı savunmak için köklü bir sistem değişikliği. Irkçılığın ve patriyarkanın sona ermesi, bütün ülkelerde aşırı sağın yenilgiye uğratılması için.”


Manifestonun imzacıları arasında Türkiye'den Özgür Üniversite Hareketi, Almanya'dan YUNA – Demokratische Jugend ve Internationaler Jugend Verband, Avusturya'dan Ronahî – Youth Building Bridges bulunuyor. 


Manifesto, zorunlu askerliğin kaldırılmasını, kamu hizmetlerine yatırım yapılmasını, erişilebilir konutu, iklim adaletini ve demokratik hakların korunmasını talep ediyor. NATO'nun ve Avrupa Birliği'nin yeniden silahlanma politikalarını eleştirirken işgal, sömürgecilik, ırkçılık, patriyarka ve aşırı sağa karşı mücadeleyi de ortak programına dahil ediyor.


Gençlik koalisyonu yalnızca bir günlük protestoyu değil, ülkeler arasında kalıcı bir öğrenci ve gençlik hareketi oluşturmayı hedefliyor. Okul ve üniversite boykotlarının yanı sıra genel toplantılar, yürüyüşler ve işgal eylemleri de tartışılan mücadele biçimleri arasında.


Fransa'dan Almanya'ya: Farklı mücadeleler buluşuyor


Fransa'da liselilerin eğitim koşullarına ve sosyal eşitsizliklere karşı sürdürdükleri protestolar, Avrupa'daki seferberliğinin önemli dayanakları arasında. İtalya'da Rete della Conoscenza ve öğrenci örgütleri, eğitim hakkını ve militarizm karşıtlığını ortak gündeme taşıyor. Birleşik Krallık'ta Socialist Students, 200'ü aşkın okul, kolej ve üniversitede ders bırakma hazırlığı bulunduğunu açıklıyor.


Almanya'da Gen Z regelt girişimi 39 kentte gösteri çağrısı yapıyor. Eğitim ve sağlık hizmetlerinde kesintilere, hayat pahalılığına, iklim politikalarına ve zorunlu askerliğe karşı çıkan hareket, 20 Kasım'ı yeni bir seferberlik aşaması olarak görüyor.


Ancak gençlik hareketinin bütün bileşenleri aynı örgütsel çatı altında değil. Almanya Federal Öğrenci Konferansı, Gen Z regelt'in örgütsel şeffaflığına ilişkin çekinceler ileri sürerek eylemini ayrı düzenliyor.


Uluslararası Barış Bürosu ve Stop ReArm Europe ise 20–22 Kasım arasında “Welfare, not Warfare” (Savaş değil, sosyal refah) sloganıyla sendikaları, barış hareketlerini ve sivil toplum örgütlerini eyleme çağırıyor. Bu etkinlikler gençlik greviyle bağlantılı, ancak ondan ayrı örgütleniyor.


Göçmen gençler hareketin neresinde?


Uluslararası grev manifestosu, ırkçılığa ve aşırı sağa karşı mücadeleyi açıkça ortak talepler arasına alıyor. Ancak göçmen gençlik örgütlerinin koalisyonun yönetiminde ve karar mekanizmalarında nasıl temsil edildiği belirginleşmiş değil. 


Almanya'da ise göçmenler tartışmanın doğrudan konusu haline geldi. 31 Ekim gösterilerinin ardından Federal İçişleri Bakanı Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), bazı kentlerdeki şiddet olaylarından sol gruplarla birlikte “göçmen çevrelerden” gelen kişileri sorumlu tutmuş, Federal Eğitim Bakanı Karin Prien (CDU) de benzer ifadeler kullanmıştı. 


Berlin'deki Gen Z regelt örgütleyicilerinden Veronika Dinter, 3 Kasım'da Evangelischer Pressedienst'e yaptığı açıklamada hükümete seslendi:  


“ Taleplerimizle alay etmek ve tartışmayı ırkçı açıklamalarla saptırmak yerine ciddiye alın."
