author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Remembering “remembrance day” with Randolph Bourne
content:
It cannot be too firmly realized that war is a function of States and not of nations, indeed that it is the chief function of States. War is a very artificial thing. It is not the naive spontaneous outburst of herd pugnacity; it is no more primary than is formal religion. War cannot exist without a military establishment, and a military establishment cannot exist without a State organization. War has an immemorial tradition and heredity only because the State has a long tradition and heredity. But they are inseparably and functionally joined. We cannot crusade against war without crusading implicitly against the State. And we cannot expect, or take measures to ensure, that this war is a war to end war, unless at the same time we take measures to end the State in its traditional form. The State is not the nation, and the State can be modified and even abolished in its present form, without harming the nation. On the contrary, with the passing of the dominance of the State, the genuine life-enhancing forces of the nation will be liberated. If the State’s chief function is war, then the State must suck out of the nation a large part of its energy for purely sterile purposes of defense and aggression. It devotes to waste or to actual destruction as much as it can of the vitality of the nation. No one will deny that war is a vast complex of life-destroying and life-crippling forces. If the State’s chief function is war, then it is chiefly concerned with coordinating and developing the powers and techniques which make for destruction. And this means not only the actual and potential destruction of the enemy, but of the nation at home as well. For the very existence of a State in a system of States means that the nation lies always under a risk of war and invasion, and the calling away of energy into military pursuits means a crippling of the productive and life-enhancing process of the national life.


The State

 (1919)


Randolph Bourne


from

The Anarchist Library

: “Randolph Bourne left an unfinished, unpaginated draft of

The State

 when he died during the flu pandemic of 1918. The draft was published posthumously, with some material incorrectly ordered, in

Untimely Papers

 (1919). This edition follows the corrected ordering used in most printed editions of Bourne’s work.”


I.


To most Americans of the classes which consider themselves significant the war brought a sense of the sanctity of the State which, if they had had time to think about it, would have seemed a sudden and surprising alteration in their habits of thought. In times of peace, we usually ignore the State in favour of partisan political controversies, or personal struggles for office, or the pursuit of party policies. It is the Government rather than the State with which the politically minded are concerned. The State is reduced to a shadowy emblem which comes to consciousness only on occasions of patriotic holiday.


Government is obviously composed of common and unsanctified men, and is thus a legitimate object of criticism and even contempt. If your own party is in power, things may be assumed to be moving safely enough; but if the opposition is in, then clearly all safety and honor have fled the State. Yet you do not put it to yourself in quite that way. What you think is only that there are rascals to be turned out of a very practical machinery of offices and functions which you take for granted. When we say that Americans are lawless, we usually mean that they are less conscious than other peoples of the august majesty of the institution of the State as it stands behind the objective government of men and laws which we see. In a republic the men who hold office are indistinguishable from the mass. Very few of them possess the slightest personal dignity with which they could endow their political role; even if they ever thought of such a thing. And they have no class distinction to give them glamour. In a republic the Government is obeyed grumblingly, because it has no bedazzlements or sanctities to gild it. If you are a good old-fashioned democrat, you rejoice at this fact, you glory in the plainness of a system where every citizen has become a king. If you are more sophisticated you bemoan the passing of dignity and honor from affairs of State. But in practice, the democrat does not in the least treat his elected citizen with the respect due to a king, nor does the sophisticated citizen pay tribute to the dignity even when he finds it …

title: HABAŞ Katliamı’nda yaşamını yitiren Kadir Kaan Özçelik’in kardeşi Şevval Özçelik:'Savaşalım ki bizden sonrakiler ölmesin
content:
İzmir – Aliağa’daki HABAŞ Demir Çelik Fabrikasında 9 Kasım’da meydana gelen patlamada yaşamını yitiren 19 işçiden biri olan Kadir Kaan Özçelik’in kardeşi Şevval Özçelik, katliam günü fabrika önündeki bilgi karartmasını, Fabrikada rutin haline gelen ihmal zincirini ve adalet mücadelesini anlattı. Ağabeyinin sabah saatlerinde hayatını kaybetmesine karşın kendilerine akşam 8’e kadar hiçbir bilgi verilmediğini söyleyen Özçelik, sorumluların ev hapsinde tutulmasına ve Türk Metalin sessizliğine tepki göstererek diğer işçi ailelerine birlikte mücadele çağrısı yaptı.

Üniversite sınavına hazırlanan mezun bir öğrenci olduğunu belirten Şevval Özçelik, patlamanın yaşandığı pazartesi günü saat 10.15-13.00 arasındaki dershane denemesinin ardından arkadaşlarıyla vakit geçirip saat 15.00 sularında eve dönerken teyzesinin telefonuyla fabrikada patlama olduğunu ve ağabeyine ulaşılamadığını öğrendi. Ağabeyinin telefonunun kapalı olması üzerine aradığı annesinden, ilk andan itibaren fabrikada olmalarına rağmen hiçbir açıklama yapılmadığını, hastanelerde de izine rastlayamadıklarını öğrenen Özçelik, bir aile dostuyla tesise gitti. Fabrika önünde sonuç alamayıp yeniden hastanelere bakmak için araçlara yöneldikleri sırada babasının “Şevval, geri dönün” telefonuyla geri döndüklerini ve babasının bir arkadaşının içeri girip vefat listesinde ağabeyinin adını gördüğünü aktaran Özçelik, saatlerce süren belirsizliğe “Abim sabah vefat etmesine rağmen akşam saat 8’e kadar bizimle dalga geçer gibi hiçbir şey söylememişler; biz de belki yaşıyordur umuduyla saatlerce abimi aramışız” dedi.

Katliama giden sürecin göz göre göre yaşandığını vurgulayan Özçelik, normal şartlarda çok uzun testlerden geçen makinelerin arızalanma ya da yıkılma ihtimalinin bulunmaması gerektiğini belirterek, “Ancak bundan sorumlu kişilerin araba koleksiyonları olmasına rağmen, anladığım kadarıyla bu testleri tüm doğruluğuyla yaptıracak bütçeleri yokmuş” dedi. Ağabeyinin ölümünden sorumlu olanların daha önce gerekli önlemleri alması halinde bu kayıpların yaşanmayacağını dile getiren Özçelik, “Zaten abimin vefat etmesinden sorumlu olduğunu düşündüğüm insanlar daha önce bu ‘iş güvenliğini’ sağlasaydı ne abim ne yanındaki 18 can ne de bundan önceki hayatlar kaybolacaktı” ifadelerini kullandı.

Yürütülen soruşturmada ortada gerçek bir kovuşturma olmadığını belirten Özçelik, “Kamuoyunun da sorumluluğuna işaret ettiği kişi şu an konforlu evinde, ev hapsinde tutuluyor. Bu durumun böyle sürmeyeceğini ve çok yakında hiçbir şey olmamış gibi sokaklarda gezeceğini de öngörebiliyorum” diyerek HABAŞ’ın sahibi Mehmet Rüştü Başaran’ın ev hapsiyle bırakılmasına dikkat çekti. Bugüne kadar ihmal ve patlamalar yüzünden sevdikleri hayattan koparılan tüm insanlar adına olayın unutulmaması, sorumluların hukuken hesap vermesi için sesini her platformda duyurmaya devam edeceğini vurgulayan Özçelik, mağdur aileleri ve işçileri savunması gereken Türk Metal yönetiminin tek bir tweet dahi atmamasını da eleştirerek bu tutumun “Taraflarının mağdur taraf değil, belki de bizim suçlu ve sorumlu olduğunu düşündüğümüz şahıslardan yana olduğunu düşündürüyor” dedirttiğini kaydetti.

Aynı acıyı yaşayan diğer ailelere de seslenen Özçelik, yakınlarının bedenine dahi ulaşamayan, bir parçasıyla ya da kendisi gibi yalnızca ağabeyinin yanmış saçıyla yetinmek zorunda kalan ailelerin acısını anladığını belirtti. Susulması halinde olayın unutulacağını, suçluların ya hiç ceza almayacağını ya da hak ettiklerinden daha az ceza alacaklarını ve kaybettikleri yakınlarının da kanlarının yerde kalmasını istemeyeceğini dile getiren Özçelik, diğer ailelere “Bana istediğiniz her an ulaşabilirsiniz. Biz birbirimize destek olursak daha güçlü oluruz. Eğer biz bir duvar olursak bizi kimse yıkamaz. Lütfen savaşın; savaşın ki bizden sonrakiler ölmesin” sözleriyle seslendi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: The Third World War, the Middle East and the Kurds
content:
Following the collapse of the Soviet Union in the early 1990s, Britain, the United States and Israel developed a strategy under the concept of the “New World Order,” aimed at restructuring the international system in the interests of global capital. The conflict that began with the war against Iraq in the 1990s continues to this day and has grown increasingly intense, widespread and complex through successive phases. One of the central objectives of this Third World War was to dismantle the Kurdish freedom movement, resolve the Palestinian question in line with hegemonic interests, and reorganize the Middle East under Israeli dominance and the control of the principal hegemonic power.


To prevent the expansion and further development of the Kurdish freedom movement and ultimately bring about its destruction, a federal Kurdish entity was established in Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq). In doing so, the powers involved relied on both local collaborationist forces and the states among which Kurdistan has been divided. However, despite all the plots directed against the freedom movement and Abdullah Öcalan, they failed to achieve the objectives pursued through this war.


The geopolitical pressures behind Turkey’s strategic reorientation


The failure of the strategy aimed at dismantling the Kurdish freedom movement was not the only factor that prompted the Turkish state to seek new political options. Other developments following Hamas’s attack on Israel on October 7 also played a role: Israeli military operations in the Gaza Strip and Lebanon, the resulting weakening of Hamas and Hezbollah, the escalation of tensions with Iran into open warfare, and the restructuring of international energy and trade routes, which saw Cyprus included in relevant agreements while Turkey was left out. These developments forced the Turkish state to reconsider its previous strategic orientation.


Another significant factor was the resistance developed by the Kurdish freedom movement under Abdullah Öcalan’s leadership, characterized by a far-reaching willingness to make sacrifices. Without this resistance, the changing regional balance of power alone would not have prompted the Turkish state to undertake such a strategic shift. It was only the combination of geopolitical developments and the struggle waged in Kurdistan that compelled the Turkish leadership to respond to Abdullah Öcalan’s approach to initiating a new political process and to issue a corresponding appeal to him.


The nation-state order in the Middle East is being shaken


The military and political upheavals in the region also caused considerable concern within the Turkish leadership. These include the war waged by the United States and Israel against Iran, the change of power in Syria that saw Baathist rule replaced by a Sunni-dominated government, and the resulting weakening of the so-called Shia Crescent. At the same time, the nation-state order in the Middle East, rooted in the Sykes-Picot Agreement, became increasingly unstable and was called into question even by the dominant powers themselves. These uncertainties were further heightened by the perception that the hegemonic actors were considering partly divergent approaches to resolving the Kurdish question.


With Israel’s growing hegemonic influence, its increasing capacity for military intervention across the region and the extensive support it receives from the United States, these developments came to be perceived by Turkey as an existential threat to the survival of the state. Against this backdrop, the fact that the political resolution process continues to this day and that Abdullah Öcalan remains recognized as a negotiating partner can largely be attributed to the Turkish leadership’s security concerns and fears for the state’s very existence.


The Third World War, which began in the Middle East and particularly in Kurdistan, has gradually spread to other regions of the world. The collapse of the Soviet Union brought an end to the bipolar world order, prompting the United States to develop a strategy aimed at controlling the Middle East and establishing its unchallenged global hegemony. Despite various crises, the US largely succeeded in securing its dominant position through the support and involvement of cooperating governments. In recent years, however, the People’s Republic of China and Russia have steadily expanded their international influence. Their rise as major economic and military hegemonic …

title: Just Released: Video Taken by ALF As They Liberate 9 Mice from University of New Orleans Vivisector Christopher Harshaw
content:
On September 19, 2026, nine female mice (including four so-called “breeding females”) were loaded up and spirited away from a miserable, windowless cinderblock room on the 2nd floor of UNO’s Psychology Building to begin a new life in safety and comfort. Today for the first time, video taken by the Animal Liberation Front(ALF) during the raid is being released, after it was received anonymously and exclusively by the North American Animal Liberation Press Office.

The ALF communique received after the raid can be viewed here. The raw video footage can be viewed in its entirety here. Images in this press release are stills from the footage, are anti-copyrighted and can be used without permission.

The lab was that of Christopher Harshaw, who subjects mice and rats to experiments that purportedly aim to study autism, body temperature regulation and social behavior. This involves injecting them with drugs (such as acetaminophen to induce neurodevelopmental disorders), shutting them into small lighted cabinets overnight, and putting poisonous chemicals into their water like aniline (known to cause blood disorders and spleen tumors in rodents).

Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harwshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.

Per the communique: “To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on sight it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.”

author: Tobias Schalyo
title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt? 


Lea und Josias engagieren sich seit Jahren im Tierschutz und haben selbst zwei Katzen adoptiert.


PETA: Von Snacks über Pflege bis zu Alltagsprodukten: Wo findet ihr die Überraschungen, die es in euren Kalender schaffen?

  


Adventsome

: Die wichtigste Frage ist immer: Würden wir uns selbst darüber freuen, wenn wir morgens das Türchen öffnen? Das Produkt muss zudem vegan, unisex und alkoholfrei sein und auch darüber hinaus mit unseren Werten matchen!

title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Sharepic downloaden


Der Beitrag

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

 erschien zuerst auf

ARIWA

title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.


Show some support to

South Suffolk Hunt Sabs.

SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!

 appeared first on

Hunt Saboteurs Association

.

Symbolbild

Update vom 7. November 2026


Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden stellt Verfahren ein


Nachdem im Januar 2026 ein Video für einen medialen Aufschrei sorgte, das zeigt, wie ein sogenannter

Polizeihund

 bei einer Demonstration gewaltsam gegen einen Demonstranten eingesetzt wurde, erstatteten wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen die Verantwortlichen.


Im August 2026 wurde bekannt, dass die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden in dem Fall nicht weiter ermittelt – angesichts des traurigen Videos mit absurden Begründungen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft erklärt diese Entscheidung in dem Einstellungsbescheid damit, dass ein „Verstoß gegen das Tierschutzgesetz […] nur vorliegen [würde], wenn man einem Tier ohne vernünftigen Grund aus Rohheit erhebliche Schmerzen zufügen würde.“ Der im Video dokumentierte Umgang des Beamten mit dem Hund sei keine „Rohheit“ im Sinne des Tierschutzgesetzes, da die ergriffene „Maßnahme […] zum Aufrechterhalten der öffentlichen Sicherheit und Ordnung erforderlich war […]“ und der Hund „nur kurz eingesetzt“ worden sei.


Die Staatsanwaltschaft begründet die Entscheidung darüber hinaus damit, dass „Diensthunde […] legal bei der Polizei als Hilfsmittel auch in Stresssituationen eingesetzt […]“ werden. Die Tiere würden dabei automatisch Belastungssituationen ausgesetzt. Die Interessen und das Wohl der Hunde rückten jedoch im Verhältnis zu den polizeilichen Interessen der Gefahrenabwehr in den Hintergrund, da die „Diensthunde“ zu diesem Zwecke ausgebildet würden. Der den Hunden zugeschriebene „Nutzen“ rechtfertigt laut Ansicht der Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden, dass die Tiere bewusst in Gefahrensituationen gezwungen werden.


PETA kritisiert Entscheidung der Staatsanwaltschaft: Gesetz erlaubt Gewalt gegen Diensthunde


Die Einstellung unserer Anzeige ist ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass das Gesetz die „Diensthunde“ nicht vor einem gewaltsamen Umgang und Missbrauch schützt. First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023

title: Peoples’ Climate Summit calls for a democratic energy transition
content:
The Peoples’ Climate Summit in Antalya continued its discussions on the second day with a fundamental critique of global energy policy. During a three-part event titled “Phasing Out Fossil Fuels and Energy Democracy,” representatives of international climate movements, trade unions and environmental initiatives discussed alternatives to an energy system dominated by fossil fuels and the interests of major corporations.


The summit is being held as an alternative event to the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31). While the official negotiations focus on international climate policy, participants at the alternative summit emphasized the social consequences of the climate crisis, the historical responsibility of industrialized countries and the right of affected communities to participate in decision-making.


“It is not about charity, but justice”


Opening the session, Leon Sealey-Huggins of the British organization War on Want criticized the growing concentration of economic and political power. He argued that the current environmental and social crises were not accidental developments, but consequences of an economic system that prioritized the interests of a privileged few over the needs of the majority. Those particularly affected, he said, included low-income communities, small-scale farmers and people whose livelihoods were threatened by environmental destruction and rising energy prices.


Sealey-Huggins warned against reducing the energy transition to the electrification of consumption in the Global North. “While increasing amounts of energy are being supplied to electric cars, air conditioning systems and data centers, around 700 million people worldwide still lack access to basic electricity. A just transition must therefore prioritize the needs of the people.”


Sealey-Huggins also highlighted the colonial history of economic inequality. He noted that the Global North had benefited for centuries from the extraction of raw materials and labor from colonized societies, arguing that these historical relationships must also be taken into account when financing the energy transition.


“It is not about charity, but justice. It is about redistributing wealth and power,” Sealey-Huggins stated. He called for a global Green New Deal that would have to be achieved through the collective struggle of trade unions, feminist movements, Indigenous communities and environmental initiatives.


Climate justice and the rights of Indigenous communities


Rukia Khamis of the international climate organization 350.org emphasized that economic development models from the Global North could not simply be transferred to other societies without taking local conditions into account. She argued that economic growth did not automatically translate into environmentally sustainable development. The historical responsibility of industrialized countries toward the Global South must therefore be a central component of international climate policy, she underlined.


Her colleague João Cerqueira addressed disputes over Indigenous territories in Brazil. Citing the example of the Guarani-Kaiowá people, he described a ruling by a Brazilian federal court prohibiting the issuance of new project permits in the area concerned without prior consultation with Indigenous communities. “A territory does not have to be officially recognized by the state in order to be protected,” Cerqueira explained.


He stressed that Indigenous communities should not merely be consulted on energy projects that had already been approved. Instead, he added, they must have the right to decide for themselves what kinds of economic and environmental development take place on their land. This includes the right to reject new fossil fuel extraction projects.


“In Brazil, in Turkey and everywhere around the world, communities are at the forefront of resistance. Along rivers, in courtrooms and on the streets, they are deciding their own future,” Cerqueira said.


Women bear the social consequences of energy policies


Süheyla Doğan, chair of the Association for the Protection of the Natural and Cultural Heritage of Mount Ida, addressed the gender-specific impacts of the energy crisis. She noted that the coal and energy industries remained heavily male-dominated. Women, she said, were underrepresented both in the workforce and in leadership positions, yet bore a significant share of the social consequences of job losses and workplace accidents.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Two Conferences, Two Distant Venues, One Unilateralist US Policy
content:
Nearly nine years ago, in November 2017, I faced criminal charges for joining a protest against the visit of then US President Donald Trump to the Philippines. He was in Manila for the 31st ASEAN Summit hosted by then President Rodrigo Duterte. What should have been an exercise of our constitutional right to protest ended in a violent police dispersal.


Water cannons, truncheons and even a sonic weapon were used against protesters trying to march toward the summit venues. I was among the progressive lawmakers and protest leaders charged with violating the Public Assembly Act, direct assault and disobedience to persons in authority. The police accused us of inciting protesters to breach barricades.


I considered the charges politically motivated, particularly since I was a sitting member of Congress exercising my right to dissent against a visiting foreign leader. The assault and disobedience charges were eventually dropped for lack of evidence that we had personally attacked police officers.


That experience exposed a familiar contradiction: government readily invokes democracy and national sovereignty in dealing with foreign powers but becomes intolerant when Filipinos exercise those same rights to question our relationship with a powerful ally.


Trump is back in Manila, nearly nine years later. His return brings into focus issues far bigger than the visit itself: military access, economic dependence, geopolitical rivalry, climate responsibility and Philippine sovereignty.


Two international conferences in distant venues provide a useful lens through which to examine these issues: COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, and the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila.


Their agendas differ, but both reveal the unilateralist character of Trump’s foreign policy — one that puts American strategic and economic interests ahead of multilateral commitments and the concerns of less powerful nations.


America’s retreat from climate responsibility


While Trump is welcomed in Manila, the United States is drawing criticism in Türkiye for its absence from international climate negotiations. For the second consecutive year, his administration has declined to send an official government delegation to the UN climate conference.


Trump has dismissed climate change as a hoax while his government retreats from international commitments and rolls back domestic environmental protections.


This is no minor diplomatic snub. The United States is among the world’s largest historical contributors to greenhouse gas emissions and possesses enormous economic and technological resources.


Its withdrawal weakens efforts to secure climate finance, adaptation support and compensation for loss and damage — commitments particularly vital to developing countries that have contributed little to the crisis but suffer its worst consequences.


Washington’s retreat also creates space for China and other powers to present themselves as defenders of multilateral cooperation. But for countries like the Philippines, the issue is not which superpower fills the diplomatic vacuum. It is whether the international community will deliver the resources and concrete commitments needed to confront a crisis already devastating vulnerable communities.


Trump’s return: Military dependence and strategic alignment


The concerns raised in Türkiye are not disconnected from what is happening in Manila. Opposition to Trump’s visit has brought together progressive lawmakers, church groups, people’s organizations, farmers, workers, Indigenous communities, professionals and student activists.


Their protest is directed not simply at Trump but at the policies and agreements associated with his administration and the Marcos government’s unquestioning alignment with Washington.


The Makabayan bloc has filed House Resolution No. 1593 opposing the administration’s reception of Trump. At the heart of the protest is the concern that the Philippines continues to grant Washington military and diplomatic concessions without adequately examining what the country gives up in return.


The expansion of American military access under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), additional military sites and increasingly frequent joint exercises risk drawing the Philippines deeper into the strategic confrontation between Washington and Beijing.

author: Carey Gillam
title: Environmental Groups Warn Nitrate Pollution Is “Urgent Threat to Public Health”
content:
A petition sent to the EPA calls for tighter restrictions on a contaminant increasingly associated with many cancers.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Sixteen environmental and public health groups filed a legal petition with U.S. regulators on Monday seeking new restrictions on nitrate contamination — a type of water pollution the groups say is driving a “public health crisis across the country.”

The petition calls for the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to slash the Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for nitrate in drinking water to 1 milligram per liter (mg/L), down from the current federal standard that allows for up to 10 mg/L. The groups are calling for the Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) to be set at 0 mg/L, which essentially would acknowledge that no amount of nitrate is considered safe for human health over lifetime exposure.

Such moves are warranted because scientific research shows that current levels of contamination pose “an urgent threat to public health,” including increasing the risk for certain cancers, the petition states.

The petitioners cite analysis showing that surface water levels of nitrate across the nation are increasing while nitrate monitoring is decreasing.

“One of the things we have sought to do here is to do the EPA’s job for it,” said Tyler Lobdell, an attorney with Food & Water Watch, one of the groups leading the petition effort. “One hundred and twenty million on people being serviced by public water systems are told the water is perfectly safe when the science says it is not.”

The petitioners include the Environmental Working Group, the Center for Biological Diversity, the Center for Food Safety, Food & Water Watch, Sierra Club, Natural Resources Defense Council, among others.

The petition blames not only the EPA but also federal, state, and local lawmakers and other public officials for failing to address nitrate pollution, which is linked to cancers and other health problems.

The groups cite excessive application of synthetic fertilizers, the “over-application” of animal waste from concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) onto farm fields, inadequately treated sewage and industrial discharges, and failed septic systems as culprits for the nitrate-laden water.

The legal petition for rule making requires a response by the EPA and could set in motion further legal actions, Lobdell noted.

When asked about the petition, the EPA said it would review it and said it is “committed to ensuring all Americans have access to clean drinking water.” However, the agency noted it completed its most recent review of drinking water regulations, including the regulations for nitrate, in July 2024, evaluating available studies and applicable data. And based on that information, there was no need for a revision of the MCL, the agency said. The agency said it will consider new studies for its next review.

The current standard of 10 mg/L for drinking water was initially set in the 1970s and finalized in 1991 at a level that was set to avoid causing methemoglobinemia, also known as blue baby syndrome. All public water systems are required to monitor for nitrate contamination to determine compliance with that MCL.

But research on nitrate health impacts has grown over the past 35 years and there is now a large and growing body of evidence that consuming even low levels of nitrate-contaminated water is associated with colon and rectal cancers, and ovarian cancer, bladder and kidney cancers, as well as other adverse health impacts such as neural tube defects and low birth weights in babies.

The petitioners said they identified 3,205 community water systems serving roughly 119.7 million people that recorded at least one nitrate sample at or above 1 mg/L between 2021 and 2023.

The petition comes as many U.S. states, including key farming states, wrestle with concerns about nitrates. Iowa, in particular, has drawn national scrutiny for its high levels of nitrate in prominent waterways and climbing rates of cancer.

Scientists point to farm operations as largely to blame for nitrate contamination, both because of the runoff of fertilizer applied to fields of corn and other crops, and the runoff of liquified manure generated by large livestock operations that is also often spread on farm fields. The runoff carries nitrates and phosphorus into surface and groundwaters, and …

content:
Fred Pedersen is minister of environment, energy, and minister responsible for Qulliq Energy Corp. following his selection to cabinet on Nov. 5.

The Cambridge Bay MLA was

chosen

stepped down

title: "Coffers Are Never Empty…For Bombs": Climate Activist Asad Rehman on Need for Climate Finance
content:
The United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is in its second and final week. To get an update on the state of negotiations among countries, we speak with longtime climate campaigner Asad Rehman, the chief executive of Friends of the Earth England, Wales and Northern Ireland. He says rich, developed countries are still dragging their feet on a rapid transition away from fossil fuels while withholding the money that poorer, Global South countries need.


“Whether you’re cutting emissions, whether you’re adapting to the impacts of climate change or dealing with incredible losses which are totalling over a trillion right now, you need public finance,” says Rehman. “And the rich countries are saying, 'Our coffers are empty.' But, of course, the coffers are never empty when it comes to paying for bombs. It’s never empty when it comes to the fossil fuel subsidies to the corporate giants, and it’s never empty when it comes to the billionaires.”

author: Rebecca John
title: Big Oil, Climate Change, and a ‘Smoking Gun’
content:
Arnold Obguia did not leave the island. According to the forecast, it was no big deal, just another tropical storm. But a few hours later, the winds escalated rapidly, bringing waves so large they almost pulled him out to sea. Clinging to a piece of broken sea wall, Arnold survived to find his house completely destroyed. Others were not so lucky.


This story is published in partnership with

Rolling Stone.


Typhoon Rai, known locally as Typhoon Odette, battered the Philippines in December 2021. With winds of up to 167 miles per hour, extreme rainfall, violent storm surges, extensive flooding, and landslides across the central Philippine archipelago, Odette ripped rooftops from houses and devastated crops, engulfing people and property in torrents of fast-flowing floodwater. A Category 5 cyclone, Odette displaced nearly

3.2 million people

, killing 400, injuring over 1,000, and causing nearly a billion US dollars in damages.


Now, Arnold and other victims of the typhoon are demanding their day in court, filing a civil

lawsuit

 against

oil and gas giant Shell

. Their allegations: Shell helped to make the typhoon more destructive through the company’s contribution to historic greenhouse gas emissions and its funding of climate denial — despite knowing since at least 1965 that the burning of fossil fuels was the primary cause of man-made climate change.


“The forecast had initially said it was going to be a weak storm,” says Arnold from the house he rebuilt with storm debris on the tiny island of Bilangbilangan in the heart of the Philippines’ Cebu Strait. Forty-four years old, Arnold is a fisherman, born and raised on the island, who earns his living catching trevally and bigeye scad, silvery-blue-green fish that swim in large schools around the region’s coral reefs.


“But suddenly the winds were different, they were very strong,” he recalls. “When I looked outside the window it was frightening because the waves were very high.” While his wife and two young daughters had taken refuge on the mainland, Arnold and his 14-year-old son had stayed behind to guard his boat and fishing equipment — the source of the family’s livelihood. “The waves were swelling and I could see the storm surge coming,” he remembers. Calculating that he might have time to better secure his boat, he ran outside only to get caught by the 20-foot waves that nearly swept him away. Terrified, Arnold held tight to the broken sea wall until, bruised and wounded by the debris whirling in the water, he was able to rejoin his son. “Thinking about my family and how much I wanted to see them again gave me the strength to hold on,” he says. Arnold and his son rode out the rest of the storm sheltering in the house of a neighbor. Hours later, when it was over, Arnold discovered his boat was broken but his family was safe. Like everyone else on Bilangbilangan, they had lost almost all their possessions. “Everyone went back to zero,” he explains.


Arnold joined the lawsuit in early 2024 when a coalition of NGOs working with communities ravaged by the typhoon organized a

civil claim

 on behalf of the survivors. In 2025, British law firm Hausfeld agreed to take up the case in the UK — where Shell is headquartered —submitting full details of the claim against the oil company in July of this year.


Typhoon Rai — known as Odette in the Philippines — had sustained winds of 121 miles (195 kilometers) and gusts of up to 167 miles (270 kilometers) per hour when it made landfall in the archipelago on December 16, 2021. Credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using VIIRS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE , GIBS/Worldview , and the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership. Public Domain.


Representing more than 100 of the typhoon’s victims, Hausfeld describes the suit as a “landmark case” that could have “major repercussions for the

fossil fuel industry,

” potentially paving the way for other hard-hit communities around the world to sue oil Big Oil on its home turf. The firm argues its clients suffered severe losses including serious property damage, personal injury, bereavement, psychological trauma, and loss of earnings. An announcement of the date for the first hearing to be held at London’s High Court is expected sometime early next year, says Greg Lascelles, the Hausfeld partner leading the legal team.


Shell has dismissed

the lawsuit

 as “baseless,” asserting the company had no “unique knowledge about climate change” in an

official …

author: winter oak
title: Chinese communism and the usual suspects
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


The seizure of power by the communists in 1949 led to a brutal and murderous assault on Chinese life that was even worse than that experienced by Russians under the Bolsheviks.


In January 1958 Mao Zedong, the chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), launched the regime’s second five-year plan, known as the Great Leap Forward.


Says


Wikipedia

: “The purpose of the plan was to use heavy industry to expedite the production of raw materials such as steel as a supplement to economic growth, similar to the Soviet model and the defining factor behind Mao’s Chinese Marxist policies.


“Mao spent ten months touring the country in 1958 to gain support for the Great Leap Forward and inspect the progress that had already been made. What this entailed was the humiliation, public castigation and torture of all who questioned the leap”. [1]


This rapid industrial “growth” and “development”, with people being sucked from the countryside into the cities, was a disaster – millions died from the resulting famine.


Author Frank Dikötter puts the death toll from 1958 to 1962 at more than 45 million Chinese – of these, around 7% were tortured and killed by the government, 2% committed suicide and 5% died in Mao’s labour camps built to hold dissidents. [2]


He describes severe punishments for slight infractions, such as being buried alive for stealing a handful of grain or losing an ear and being branded for digging up a potato.


The so-called

Cultural Revolution

, which began in 1966, was an insanely cruel effort to impose “modernisation” and destroy all that was traditional.


Mao’s Red Guards sought to wipe out the “Four Olds” (old ideas, old culture, old customs, and old habits), often by desecrating historical artifacts and cultural and religious sites. Tens of millions of people were persecuted and sometimes massacred – up to 2 million died. [3]


I have previously explained how the

Bolshevik

,

Fascist

 and

Nazi

 regimes – which likewise combined rabid industrialism with authoritarian terror – were all controlled by the entity I call ZIM, the zio-imperialist mafia. [4] But who could have been behind the nightmarish communist tyranny that subsequently took hold of China?


Yitzhak Shichor of the University of Haifa and Hebrew University of Jerusalem sheds some light on the matter in a fascinating

paper

 published in the

International Journal of China Studies

 in 2020.


He writes: “Jews were deeply involved in Communist revolutions in Europe, and primarily in Russia, often in leading positions. This is understandable given their demographic location, extensive education and suffering over the years.


“However, how could we account for the fact that they also played a role in Communist revolutions in Asia, and especially in China? There were practically no Jewish communities to speak of and those few who lived there had been almost totally assimilated, and had no interest whatsoever in Chinese culture, history and politics.


“Still, Jews (who arrived out of China) not only took part in the revolution but had also helped igniting it and then stayed on or joined later”. [5]


Shichor (

pictured

) says of these Jewish participants: “Their main value to the revolution was mainly writing, translation, communication and publication. Although they were all deeply committed to the Chinese Communist revolution, some of them were jailed – for years – and occasionally more than once. Nonetheless, they continued to believe in, and even to justify, the Chinese Communist Party”. [6]


Shichor explains that the Marxist brand of socialism, which reached China via Japan, was initially

the least attractive

 to Chinese intellectuals.


“Considered too violent, the notions of ‘class struggle’ contradicted traditional Confucian values of harmonious and integrative society, and the thought that ‘workers’ represented the ‘universal’ and ‘revolutionary’ class, did not conform to pre-modern Chinese beliefs…


“Whatever socio-political opposition and ideological radicalism existed, they were articulated not by Marxist communism, but by anarchism. Mao Zedong, one of the founders and later leader of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), regarded himself as anarchist up to the early 1920s”. [7]


But Marxism-Leninism soon came to the fore, thanks to the influence of the Bolsheviks, and Schichor reveals that “many of the chief Soviet and Comintern missionaries in China were Jewish”. [8] …

title: Will the new FPIC guidelines fast-track the Pax Silica hub in ancestral lands?
content:
Indigenous Aytas from different villages in Capas, Tarlac, listen to an environmental advocate during a community gathering on August 16, 2026, to discuss the impacts of the proposed Pax Silica hub on their land. Photo by Chantal Eco / Bulatlat

“It was really built to cater to corporations. Any semblance that it protects IP rights and allows Indigenous peoples to say no is gone.”

Mandor Matias, 45, has lived all his life on his family’s land in Sitio Binyayan in Capas, Tarlac. He and his relatives plant rice and vegetables on about three hectares of land. But on July 15, employees from the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) came to his house. They pointed to the planted land in front of it, handed him a paper to sign and offered P30 (USD 0.47) per square meter, or about P900,000 (US$ 14,100) for all three hectares.

“They gave me a paper and asked me to sign it. I said I didn’t need to sign it. If I signed it, it would be as if I had accepted payment,” Matias told Bulatlat in Filipino.

He was not told why they were being pushed to sell their land. He later learned through social media and then confirmed by their village head, that the Pax Silica hub, a U.S.-backed hub for artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing, will be built on their land.

Matias is an indigenous Ayta. His home and farm now lie within the area of the proposed Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park, a 1,620-hectare hub in New Clark City that the BCDA is developing with the United States under the Pax Silica framework. Their fate may now be decided under new consent rules. In May, the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) approved the contentious amendments to the guidelines on free, prior and informed consent (FPIC), and a copy was only released publicly in September. The 2026 guidelines shorten deadlines, approve permits automatically when officials fail to act on time, and let some government projects pass with a document review instead of a full community vote. Indigenous groups warn the rules could clear the way for Pax Silica and other “development projects” on ancestral lands.

The FPIC process could take months to years, especially when a project could greatly affect the ancestral land and the community is divided. The new FPIC guidelines run on tight deadlines: seven working days for the NCIP’s field investigation, 10 days for community assemblies on large projects and up to 60 days for the community to decide. If NCIP officials fail to act on time on a completed consent report, the certificate is issued automatically.

Government-funded projects need only a document review if they are “non-commercial.” Those with private partners or long-term impacts go to Category A or B, as the regional director decides. Projects that displace residents fall under Category A, the strictest track. But a project can get its certificate even before it is clear which households will be affected. Protections for those families can be settled later. Meanwhile, even after a community says no, the applicant keeps the right to refile.

Funa-ay Claver, an Indigenous youth leader and spokesperson of Katribu, said the BCDA may avoid FPIC altogether by insisting that no Indigenous people live on the site.

“It was really built to cater to corporations. Any semblance that it protects IP rights and allows Indigenous peoples to say no is gone,” Claver explained in Filipino.

She said the categories depend on a project’s scale, not on how many people it affects, and that manufacturing hubs are not mentioned anywhere. She added that the NCIP never released a draft for public comment.

Katribu said it is wary of even calling on the BCDA to “uphold FPIC.” Under the new rules, Claver said, consent risks becoming a checklist that only clears the way for the project.

At a media forum of the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (FOCAP) in September, BCDA President Joshua Bingcang claimed that they have always consulted communities whenever there’s a project or development within New Clark City. While showing pictures of what he described as consultations, he did not specifically say that they have already consulted, much less secured the consent of the Aytas living in the area where the Pax Silica hub will be built.

He called the hub site “already BCDA property” and promised, “We will not just kick them out… there will be consultations.”

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: IMF, WB cause misery for marginalized communities
content:
The Counterdocket exposed the harms caused by the IMF-WB.


BANGKOK – For 80 years, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank (WB) brought suffering to many communities in the Global South.


On October 15, their stories were heard at the Counterdocket in Bangkok, Thailand where the two Breton Woods institutions also held their annual meeting from October 12 to 18.  


Dubbed as Our Voices Count! A Counterdocket, it brought together movements to challenge extractive systems and demand greater accountability from the IMF-WB. The Counterdocket exposed the harms caused by the IMF-WB. From the Support to Parcelization of Lands for Individual Titling (SPLIT) project of the WB Group in the Philippines to Lithium mining in Argentina, these testimonies became public records of the IMF-WB’s effects on communities. 


“This counterdocket is an act of historical and political reassertion,” said Joms Salvador, regional coordinator of the Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development (APWLD) during the opening on October 15. “The communities sitting in this room are not beneficiaries of course waiting for charity, nor are they subjects to be studied. You are the plaintiffs. You are the witnesses. And you are the judges of a system that has failed humanly. And through the voices of community leaders, feminist economists, legal scholars, and human rights defenders across all these sessions throughout the day, we are building an irrefutable record of systemic accountability.” 


“Its jurisdiction is not grounded in formal legal authority, but in the right of communities to document, testify, question and demand accountability for decisions that shape their lives,” said Zeph Repollo, Southeast Asia regional director at Just Associates (JASS), a feminist movement-building organization. 


(Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development)


She added, “It is an expression of communities’ self determination and their right to be heard, particularly in a context where existing accountability mechanisms have proven largely ineffective in addressing the consequences of IFI (international financing institutions) actions for economic, social, cultural, and environmental rights.” 


The Counterdocket focused on five connected themes examining how economic policies, development projects, and global power structures affected the communities in the Global South. The testimonies presented covered a range of projects and issues spanned across South Asia, South East Asia, Africa and Latin America. 


Some of the cases heard at the Counterdocket included the Sentani Airport and Transformation of Buyaka Ancestral Land case in West Papua 


IMF-WB effects on Filipinos lives 


At the Counterdocket, Ana Marie Mijares, 54, a farmer from Kabankalan, Negros Occidental narrated the militarization they experienced in the government’s implementation of SPLIT, a project of the Department of Agrarian Reform and the World Bank Group. 


According to the project proponent, the main objective of SPLIT is to improve the land tenure or the rights of the farmers to the land they cultivate and to provide individual titles to farmers under collective certificate of land ownership award (CLOA). 


Their community is composed mainly of farmer-beneficiaries and former sugar farmworkers organized through Kauswagan sang Bino para sa Buhi kag Hilway nga Palangabuhian (Kabuhi-an)  and Kauswagan sang Mamumugon, Mangunguma sa Bino (KASMMABI) in Barangay Orong, Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental.


The community manages around 198 hectares of land awarded through the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program in 1998 under a collective Certificate of Land Ownership Award (CLOA). The original beneficiaries were former hacienda sugarcane workers, with additional Agrarian Reform Beneficiaries (ARBs) later included through a petition for the inclusion of qualified ARBs in the landholding. The community now involves around 168 farming families.


Ana Marie Mijares (middle) with other delegates at the Counterdocket. (Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development)


After years of struggle for land, the farmers developed their own way of managing the property. Each family cultivates an individual portion of around 1.5 hectares, while at least 15 hectares are maintained as common or collective land for collective production.
