author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Police violently disperse, arrest hundreds in Muntinlupa protest
content:
More than a hundred protesters were arrested today, November 15 after police dispersed the contingent of progressive groups in the Southern Tagalog region who will be joining the protest next week in time for US President Donald Trumps’a arrival in the country.

After a long stand off between the police and the protesters, the Lakbayan Southern Tagalog was dispersed by the Southern Police District at Sucat People’s Park in Muntinlupa City at past 2:00 p.m., leading to the arrest of roughly 300 individuals, including more than 10 student journalists and alternative media reporters.

The protesters were headed to the Kampuhan protest at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila to protest against the Pax Silica initiative and the arrival of U.S. President Donald Trump for the ASEAN Summit in Pasay; however they were halted in Sucat, Muntinlupa.

Witnesses reported that initial negotiations with the police were conducted to allow the demonstrators to proceed with the protest.

Shortly after, police officers reportedly issued a final warning, stating, “Pasensyahan po, pinagbigyan namin kayo pero ayaw niyo sumunod,” before moving in to break up the assembly.

Witnesses reported that the dispersal quickly escalated and turned violent as police officers began dragging away participants.

One demonstrator recounted attempting to intervene after seeing a fellow protester being dragged by police. Alongside a T.U. and the Vice President of M.C., the witness attempted to assist the protester, only to be arrested afterwards.

Despite repeatedly stating that they were willing to submit to a voluntary arrest, the protesters claimed they continued to be subjected to physical force. One protester recounted how after managing to stand up, they were allegedly pushed toward the nearby police station, dragged once more, and brought to the station entrance.

Human rights group Karapatan said, “The PNP has turned a public space meant for the exercise of people’s democratic rights into a site of violence and repression. Karapatan condemns these acts of brutality and demands accountability from the police officers and commanders responsible,”

“These disturbing scenes, recorded in full public view, expose the brutality of the police and the extent to which state forces are willing to go to suppress dissent,” said Cristina Palabay, Karapatan secretary general in a statement.

Palabay said the Marcos regime’s relentless crackdown on protesters exposes its desperation to appease the US government and serve its interests at the expense of the Filipino people’s fundamental rights.

Palabay said the arrested protesters must be immediately released. She added that while in police custody, they must be guaranteed access to their legal counsel, paralegals, relatives, and representatives of their respective organizations, as well as immediate medical attention.

“We demand that the PNP stop all forms of physical and psychological abuse against them,” Palabay said.

In a statement, the College Editors Guild of the Philippines (CEGP) confirmed that more than 10 campus and alternative media journalists were arrested, including: three from their group, nine from the UP Los Baños Perspective, three from the Southern Tagalog Exposure, and one member each from The Stape, Philippine Collegian, and CCC The Sentinel, alongside campus journalists from Parañaque and UP Baguio.

The CEGP vehemently condemned the mass arrests and over 24 hours of harassment and intimidation, describing the operations as a deliberate crackdown on press freedom and peaceful dissent stemming from Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ‘s “overkill” police deployment.

“Not only are those who participate in the protests being targeted, but publications that highlight the grassroot struggle of those who are affected by Pax Silica,” the CEGP stated.

Altermidya Network also condemned the arrest saying, “The government cannot claim to uphold democratic freedoms before the international community while police forces suppress public demonstrations and interfere with journalists documenting events on the ground.” (With reports from Anne Marxze Umil) (AMU,RVO)

author: Unknown
title: Biçer: Kurdish cinema must build historical awareness in peace process
content:
Kurdish cinema in Turkey has faced censorship and repression throughout its history. Not only Kurdish cinema but also film and television projects dealing with Kurdistan have been forced to contend with censorship and pressure from successive governments.


Documentaries and films struggle to find venues for screenings, while cinemas refuse to show these productions. Most recently, the film Rojbash, which focuses on Teatra Jiyana Nû, has still not been released. Legal proceedings concerning the film are also ongoing. Another production unable to secure screening venues is a documentary about the Vartinis massacre.


Director Ömer Biçer, who documented the Vartinis massacre, spoke to ANF about the problems facing Kurdish cinema and the role of cinema in the struggle for peace.


‘I saw cinema as a responsibility’


Director Ömer Biçer, who began working in cinema in 2021, described how he became involved in filmmaking and his journey towards directing. Biçer said that he entered the world of cinema after meeting friends at Istasyon Akademi Mezopotamya Sinema.


Biçer said: “I was looking for an answer to the question, ‘Could I become a filmmaker?’ I believed that cinema was a collective art form and that we could become filmmakers by taking part in any aspect of it. However, looking at my earliest works, I found myself directing, which is one of the areas of cinema that carries the greatest responsibility in terms of production.


The reason was that, in 2021, Kurdistan and Turkey were experiencing difficult conditions of war, which affected every field of art. Making art was becoming increasingly difficult, particularly filmmaking. I saw this as a responsibility. It reminded me of something Ahmedê Xanî said when writing Mem û Zîn: ‘Hanî ji kemala bêkemalî / Meydana kemalê dît valî.’ In other words, Xanî saw a void in the field of artistic excellence. He wrote Mem û Zîn not because he considered himself exceptionally talented, but out of love for his people and a sense of national responsibility. I can say that I found myself in a similar situation and felt something similar.”


‘Kurdish society also guides its artists’


Biçer said that before making the Vartinis documentary, he had produced a short film addressing a public health problem that emerged during the resistance in Sur. 


Biçer continued: “Before Vartinis, I actually made a film called Sêhiya Gel in 2024. It dealt with a public health problem during the Sur resistance in 2015. During the post-production stage, after filming had been completed, this story and project came to me. It was actually a request from the people of Vartinis.


I think I felt ready for it, as though I had been preparing for years. A group of people came and said, ‘This is what happened to us, and this is how it ended. There was a massacre, followed by a second massacre through the legal system. We do not want this to be forgotten.’


At that point, regardless of whether someone is a filmmaker, whether new or experienced, any human being would try to become part of that story.


Anyone with a sense of moral responsibility would say, ‘Something like this has happened, I have been asked to take part, and I will accept that responsibility.’ That was the concern that motivated us to begin.


But both while making Vartinis and through the reactions we received afterwards, we were reminded of something: Kurdish society is genuinely dynamic and political. What I saw was that Kurdish society can also guide its artists. What was Kurdish cinema dealing with? What kind of narrative was it pursuing? When the issue of Vartinis emerged, we could see that everything else it had been dealing with suddenly lost much of its significance. That is how the process of telling the story of Vartinis began.”


‘There was also a public health crisis during the Sur resistance’


Biçer also discussed his short film Sêhiya Gel, which addresses events during the Sur resistance: “I was in Amed (Diyarbakır), about 100 metres from Diyarbakır Square, close to Sur. I was dealing with some paperwork at a notary's office when we learned that a woman had been killed by the police. The woman, Mızgın Kılıç, whose code name was Ruken Amed, was killed by police officers while trying to enter Sur to support the resistance fighters there.


That was when I felt that the war was continuing and that its psychological effects were affecting public health. How healthy were those who remained healthy? What was the ethical cost of …

title: Social siege in Yüksekova: Children, women and youth targeted - Part One
content:
Allegations of child sexual abuse, harassment and sexual assault against women in Hakkari (Colemêrg), particularly in Yüksekova (Gever), have brought long-standing social problems in the district back into focus. A case involving allegations of sexual abuse of a 13-year-old child, in which school bus driver Eren Oğuz and local musician and security guard Necat Koparan are named, has been brought before the judiciary. Separately, several women have filed complaints alleging harassment and sexual assault by Nevzat Çiftçi, a local musician who performs at weddings. The fact that both men are well known in the district, perform at weddings and maintain connections with different sections of society raises the need to examine these incidents in a broader context. Are these merely isolated cases, or are they part of a wider social siege targeting young people, women and children through special warfare policies?


Yüksekova is a Kurdish town known for its strong neighborhood culture, close relations among neighbors and tradition of social solidarity. Over the years, this social structure has become a target of the state's repression and security policies. The curfews and clashes that began with the declaration of self-rule in Yüksekova on 13 August 2015 resulted in widespread destruction. Neighborhoods were demolished and thousands of families were displaced. The destruction targeted not only physical spaces but also relations of neighborliness and solidarity. The subsequent reconstruction of the town accelerated the replacement of neighborhood culture with a consumption-oriented way of life.


Today, discussions about Yüksekova point to a multidimensional social siege, ranging from abuse targeting children and women to drugs, loan sharking and money laundering networks, and from the criminalization of young people to divisions deepened through tribalism. The erosion of social values, from wedding culture and everyday life to economic relations and local power networks, is also part of this picture. The latest case involving the alleged sexual assault of a 13-year-old child has once again highlighted the extent of the problems surrounding children's safety and protection. This report examines how social life in Yüksekova has been targeted through special warfare policies and the transformations these policies have brought about.


Child sexual abuse and threats involving images


The sexual abuse case involving a 13-year-old child in Yüksekova has once again raised concerns about children's safety and protection in the district. The case, which has been referred to the judiciary, names school bus driver Eren Oğuz and Necat Koparan, a local musician, wedding performer and security guard. The child reportedly described the abuse in a statement given at the Child Monitoring Center, saying that images of the child had been used to make threats and that attempts had been made to obstruct the child's education. The threats and pressure the child reportedly faced after the abuse indicate that the incident was not limited to the alleged sexual abuse itself. Threats involving images and interference with the child's right to education are also significant aspects of the case. The suspects' release after giving their statements has raised questions about how the investigation is being conducted, how the child is being protected and what support mechanisms will be put in place.


Eren Oğuz's position as a school bus driver is particularly significant because families entrust their children to drivers during their journeys to and from school. Children's safety and the protection of this relationship of trust are therefore central concerns. Necat Koparan's status as a security guard and his position in society as a local musician are other notable aspects of the case. Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Hakkari, Öznur Bartın, also brought the issue before parliament, submitting a parliamentary question to the Ministry of Family and Social Services.


Years of abuse and harassment cases in Yüksekova and Hakkari


The latest case involving the alleged sexual assault of a 13-year-old child is not the first such incident reported in Yüksekova or other districts of Hakkari. Over the years, allegations of child sexual abuse, harassment and sexual assault against women, as well as cases involving threats and blackmail, have emerged at different times. author: dialogocomospovos
title: Reforma agrária é transformação
content:
No intercâmbio com lideranças indígenas do Mato Grosso do Sul, os participantes puderam conhecer o trabalho de Mestre Isaac com a horta orgânica no Assentamento Terra Vista e compreender um pouco mais da história e da filosofia que sustentam essa prática.


Isaac explicou que o coletivo não cabe em quadrado: a horta é dele, mas é coletiva ao mesmo tempo, porque serve à comunidade e aos encontros realizados no assentamento. Foi feita para incentivar o coletivo e também quem estava desanimado e não acreditava.


Segundo ele, o objetivo da terra não é enriquecer; vieram para ensinar e aprender. A reforma agrária, afirmou, diz respeito à transformação e à diversidade, e o assentamento já formou médico, advogado, engenheiro, agrônomo e enfermeiro.


A natureza pediu esse cuidado: poder alimentar-se bem e viver sossegado, tranquilo. Na cidade, disse, a pessoa vegeta, acorda, levanta e trabalha assustada; no assentamento há porta aberta, água pura sem cloro nem veneno e fruta natural.


Ele contou que viveu 18 anos no Espírito Santo com a cabeça impregnada pela ganância, tinha café e tratava tudo de forma brutal, até perceber que estava errado e matando a si mesmo ao bater herbicida e jogar veneno na cara do outro. Ao chegar, começou a pensar e enfrentou desafios sem correr, acreditando na força da natureza.


Além da horta, tem roça de cacau e já teve 14 mil pés de café, mas precisou parar por causa de hérnias de disco. Às margens do rio Aliança, os participantes conversaram sobre essa trajetória, sobre o que vieram fazer na terra e sobre a importância de trabalhar tranquilo, sossegado e em coletivo.

author: Unknown
title: The memory of a cartoon: From Qırıx to Bajar
content:
Doğan Güzel's cartoons carry a collective memory stretching from the streets of Diyarbakır (Amed) in the 1990s to the present day. Born out of everyday life, political conflicts and social contradictions, Qırıx gradually became more than a cartoon character, emerging as a figure representing the youth of the period and the transformation experienced by Kurdish society. Güzel's work, which continued through humor publications such as Gırgır, TEW-LO, Pîne and Zrîng, has now taken a new form with Bajar magazine. This long-running journey seeks not only to preserve the collective memory of the past but also to create space for the written use of Kurdish through cartoons and comics.


Güzel's journey as a cartoonist began with a character he created by observing the people around him and the political atmosphere of the time. Doğan Güzel, who spoke to ANF, said that he began drawing cartoons for Gırgır magazine and described his need to create a character he could draw every day.


Güzel said: "Since I was among patriotic young people, I wanted to create a character I could draw every day without too much difficulty whenever I needed to produce something in response to newspaper headlines. I looked around and observed my fellow students. I tried to create a character by combining Kurdish culture with something familiar to me. I think the character resonated with people because I drew him sincerely, without forcing myself too much.


Although my drawings were amateurish, I was naturally reflecting the period as I tried to portray the people around me. I was depicting the world of young people who were just becoming involved in politics, taking part in protests and experiencing uncertainty. I combined the experiences of students in Istanbul with the social reality of Kurdish people. Perhaps that is why the character became popular. When you draw by observing your surroundings, you also reflect the pulse of the country you live in."


Qırıx first appears in Özgür Gündem


Qırıx appeared in the pages of Özgür Gündem between 1992 and 1995. Politics in the character's world was not limited to developments reported in newspaper headlines. Young people's friendships, everyday decisions, uncertainties about joining the struggle and questions about how to lead their lives were also part of that world.


Güzel described the political atmosphere in which the character emerged and the uncertainties experienced by young people. 


Güzel said: "There was intense political activity in Istanbul in 1991, 1992 and 1993. It was a period when Kurdish young people were discovering their identities and becoming involved in politics, with demonstrations taking place every day. Young people felt they had to make major decisions. They were asking themselves, 'What should I do? How should I act? Where do I stand in this struggle?' This atmosphere was reflected in my cartoons. Keko's incomplete understanding of politics, his uncertainty about whether to join the struggle, his constant changes of mind and the ambiguity over whether these feelings were sincere or driven by other reasons reflected the experiences of young people at the time. There were strong similarities between what was happening in Kurdistan and the experiences of young people in Istanbul. The problems were shared, and young people were confronting similar questions."


Qırıx's significance lay not in being a character who observed the political struggle from the outside, but in embodying the contradictions experienced by young people in his own everyday life. The character reflected a generation struggling to make decisions, changing alongside social conditions and sometimes confronting its own contradictions.


T

he politics of everyday life


The years in which Qırıx emerged were marked by armed clashes, detentions, village evacuations and state violence that shaped everyday life in Kurdish cities. Güzel's cartoons, however, portrayed this harsh reality not simply through political messages but also through the seemingly ordinary lives of people.


Güzel said that he had not initially expected his drawings to attract so much attention. He described his style as different from conventional newspaper humor and reflected on both the character's popularity and the discomfort it caused.

author: Unknown
title: Zidane'dan Mbappe açıklaması: Türkiye maçında oynayabilecek mi?
content:
Fotoğraf: Кирилл Венедиктов/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 3.0

Fransa A Milli Futbol Takımı Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane ve futbolcu Lucas Da Cunha, yarın Türkiye ile oynanacak kritik karşılaşma öncesinde Bordeaux şehrindeki Matmut Atlantique Stadı'nda basın toplantısı düzenledi. İtalya deplasmanında mağlup olduklarını hatırlatan Zidane, yarın sahadan galibiyetle ayrılmaktan başka düşünceleri olmadığını vurguladı.

Üst tura yükselmek için kazanmak zorunda olduklarının altını çizen Fransız teknik direktör, "Türkiye yarın bize zorluk çıkaracak. Buna çok dikkat etmeliyiz. Fransa olarak iyi bir maç ortaya koymalıyız" dedi. İtalya maçında yedikleri 3 golün savunmanın zayıflığından kaynaklanmadığını ifade eden Zidane, milli takımlarda antrenman yapmaya vakit bulamadıklarını, belirli bir oyun felsefeleri olduğunu ve tek amaçlarının üst tura çıkmak olduğunu belirtti.

Basın toplantısında en çok merak edilen konuların başında gelen Kylian Mbappe'nin sakatlık durumuna da değinen Zidane, yıldız oyuncunun herhangi bir problemi bulunmadığını ve yarın Türkiye karşısında forma giyebilecek durumda olduğunu açıkladı.

Toplantıya katılan futbolcu Lucas Da Cunha ise teknik direktörünün kendisine duyduğu güvenden duyduğu memnuniyeti dile getirerek, tek hedeflerinin sahadan galibiyetle ayrılmak olduğunu söyledi.

author: Natália Perez
title: Bolsonarismo além da presidência: “Extrema direita não sai derrotada”, avalia especialista
content:
Desde o dia seguinte à derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nas eleições presidenciais de 2026, o senador da República segue morando nos Estados Unidos, para onde fugiu após o ministro Alexandre de Moraes determinar a entrega de seus passaportes – o mesmo caminho do irmão e ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, no ano anterior, também para evitar os inquéritos dos quais são alvo na Justiça.


Nos EUA, os Bolsonaros buscam a proximidade com Donald Trump e seu entorno político. Mas a recente derrota dos republicanos nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato pode representar um enfraquecimento da extrema direita defendida por essas figuras políticas?

 Este é o tema do

Pauta Pública

 desta semana que recebe Odilon Caldeira Neto, historiador, professor da Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora (UFJF) e coordenador do Observatório da Extrema Direita. Para ele, “a despeito da imensa vitória que foi a reeleição do presidente Lula, o campo da extrema direita brasileira não sai derrotado”.


Na conversa com Andrea Dip, ele também analisa os desafios do campo progressista para os próximos anos. “O processo que culminou nas mobilizações para a eleição de Lula não é o ponto final, na verdade são pontos de partida […] assim como a direita criou uma nova geração a partir das mobilizações das ruas, a partir das formas de pulverização e de atuação na sociedade, as esquerdas também precisam pensar a partir dessa realidade ou, se não, essas conquistas muito importantes podem ser espécies de respiros, podem ser ganhos pontuais”, afirma.


Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.


EP 242


											O início do fim do bolsonarismo? — com Odilon Caldeira Neto


13 de novembro de 2026


					·


				Historiador reflete sobre os rumos da extrema direita e os desafios do campo progressista


0:00


-:–


15


15


Veja mais episódios desta série


Após a fuga e as cartas atrapalhadas de Flávio, as três versões delas, qual análise pode ser feita sobre as reconfigurações do bolsonarismo e como a figura do Tarcísio se encaixa nesse momento?


Existe um espólio em disputa no campo bolsonarista que se configura de diversas maneiras, inclusive intrafamiliar. O caso de Eduardo Bolsonaro e o caso de Flávio Bolsonaro trazem consigo alguma espécie de capital, mas distantes do cenário político brasileiro.

 É interessante focar a análise nas figuras que vão, em certa medida, buscar articular atores e atrizes – atrizes, justamente, pela presença da Michele Bolsonaro –, e talvez um ator do campo bolsonarista familiar, o Carlos Bolsonaro. Agora, Carlos assumiu posição de um certo protagonismo, tendo visitado o pai na prisão domiciliar, em sua residência, ele tem sido uma espécie de interlocutor.


Porém, a figura de Michelle Bolsonaro não pode ser menosprezada de maneira alguma, por várias razões: da capacidade política à forma como ela liderou até recentemente o PL Mulher, a forma como ela integra setores eleitoralmente muito interessantes, com relação aos setores do conservadorismo evangélico, de um voto feminino que é sempre um gargalo para a extrema direita brasileira. Então, sem dúvida alguma, a Michelle é uma atriz de fundamental importância.


Inclusive, o campo bolsonarista tem manifestado, de maneira crescente, espécies de reações à figura de Michelle. Tem sido muito comum a referência à utilização de outros sobrenomes atribuídos à Michelle, que não o Bolsonaro, ou seja, existe uma tensão familiar, que pode ser resolvida dependendo da capacidade política de Michelle Bolsonaro.


Um campo que ainda há de se configurar, mas tem um elemento importante de situar que é o desejo de reflexões e de mudanças no caráter da prisão de Jair Bolsonaro, ou seja, mais uma vez a questão da anistia.

 O quadro de Jair Bolsonaro lida ainda um pouco com a questão, não somente da tensão entre o STF e o campo bolsonarista, mas também pela configuração da Câmara e do Senado.


Por outro lado, existe um campo de disputa da juventude de extrema direita que tem sido mobilizado nas últimas semanas pelo partido Missão. Renan Santos conseguiu articular bem um certo domínio do cenário das redes nas últimas semanas, inclusive, da forma um tanto ambivalente ou paradoxal que ele se colocou ao longo do segundo turno.


Outro cenário é o campo dos mais jovens eleitos nesse dado momento. A figura do Pavanato parece uma figura importante e, claro, a Eduarda Campopiano. É claro que tanto Pavanato quanto Eduarda Campopiano saem um pouco machucados deste …

author: Unknown
title: Fransa-Türkiye maçı ne zaman, saat kaçta, hangi kanalda?
content:
A Milli Futbol Takımı, UEFA Uluslar A Ligi 1. Grup'taki altıncı ve son maçında Fransa'ya konuk olacak. Bordeaux kentindeki Matmut Atlantique Stadı'nda oynanacak karşılaşma saat 22.45'te başlayacak. Mücadeleyi İngiltere Futbol Federasyonundan hakem Chris Kavanagh yönetecek.

A Ligi'nde oynadığı ilk 5 maçta puan alamayan Türkiye, grupta son sırada bulunuyor. Türkiye İtalya'ya Bursa'da 4-1, deplasmanda Belçika'ya 3-0, Bologna'da İtalya'ya 3-1 ve İzmir'de Belçika'ya 2-1 mağlup oldu.

İki takım grubun ilk maçında Kocaeli Stadı'nda karşı karşıya gelmiş, Fransa mücadeleyi Kylian Mbappe'nin golüyle 1-0 kazanmıştı. Türkiye ile Fransa bugüne kadar 7 kez karşılaştı. Bu maçların 5'ini Fransa kazanırken Türkiye 1 galibiyet elde etti, 1 karşılaşma ise beraberlikle sonuçlandı. Söz konusu maçlarda Fransa 14, Türkiye 5 gol kaydetti.

Türkiye, gruptaki 5 maçını da kaybetmesine rağmen A Ligi'nde kalma ihtimalini koruyor. A Ligi'ndeki dört grubun son sırasında yer alan takımlardan puan ve averaj bakımından en kötü durumda olan ikisi doğrudan B Ligi'ne düşecek. Diğer iki takım ise B Ligi'nden gelecek takımlarla play-off oynayacak.

Kart cezası sona eren Abdülkerim Bardakcı, Fransa karşısında forma giyebilecek. Belçika maçında gördüğü kart nedeniyle cezalı duruma düşen Ozan Kabak ise karşılaşmada görev alamayacak.

title: Rusya'dan açıklama: 'Ukrayna'nın enerji, liman ve demir yolu altyapı tesislerini vurduk'
content:
Görseller: Pixabay | Kolaj: Evrensel

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, Ukrayna'daki eylemlerine ilişkin açıklama yaparak ülkedeki kritik altyapı tesislerinin hedef aldıklarını duyurdu.

Bakanlıktan yapılan açıklamada, Rus ordusunun gece saatlerinde askeri amaçla kullanılan enerji, liman ve demir yolu altyapı tesislerine saldırı düzenlediği belirtilerek şu ifadelere yer verildi:

"Rivne bölgesinde Ukrayna ordusu için kullanılan lojistik tesislerinin çalışmalarını sağlayan trafo merkezi, Odessa bölgesindeki Çornomorsk Limanı'nda feribot terminali ve trafo merkezi ile Dnipropetrovsk kentindeki bir tren istasyonu yakınlarında iki lokomotif vuruldu."

Saldırıların insansız hava araçları (İHA) kullanılarak gerçekleştirildiği aktarılan açıklamada, Karadeniz'de askeri yükler taşıyan bir geminin de hedef alındığı kaydedildi. Öte yandan açıklamada, gece boyunca Ukrayna'ya ait 533 İHA'nın çeşitli bölgeler üzerinde hava savunma sistemleri tarafından düşürüldüğü de belirtildi.

author: Administrador
title: Preparativos Zapatistas para el Encuentro Abrazo con familias Buscadoras. Parte 6: REGALOS
content:
Música: «Es que yo te quiero a ti», Kevin Kaarl Imágenes, edición y producción: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Creo fue en el mes de julio, cuando el Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés anunció la salida e inicio de la primera etapa de la “Gira por la Vida- Capítulo México”. Entonces creo que dijo, palabras más, palabras menos, que las madres buscadoras eran como nuestras mamaces. Ahí fue cuando empezó, como quien dice, la problema.

Porque todas y todos de la tropa pensamos: “Ah caray, son nuestras mamaces y las vamos a ir a ver. Ni modos que llegamos y sólo decimos “Ya vine jefa, ¿qué hay de comer?”. No, si se llega así pos sólo un chanclazo, un zape o un pellizco malo (porque los hay buenos), vamos a conseguir. Porque el novio, la novia o loa novioa, vaya y pase, repones y ya. Pero si se enojan las mamaces, ay diositillo, ni dónde esconderse.

“Llevemos regalo”, dijo uno. “Sí”, dijo una insurgenta, “así como a la madre tierra se le regala el trabajo honrado”. El capitán dijo: “sí, es un regalo preventivo. O sea antes del regaño, ya tienes el regalo y cuando empieza la tormenta, sacas el regalo y sonríes y pones cara de “mamá, soy marquitos, no haré travesuras”.

“Ni quien te crea”, interviene el SubMoy y agrega, “además, todas las redes dicen que no tienes madre”.

Siguió la discusión y se llegó al consenso de que un regalo. Pero luego se hizo la bulla de que cuál regalo. Que si flores. “No compita, en lo que subes al autobús ya valieron”. “Una puema”, dice otra insurgenta. El SubMoy: “los pueblos ya van a mandar cartas, poesías, canciones. Aunque no sé si a las madres buscadoras les guste el hip hop y el rap y esas cosas”.

Siguió la discusión. Tardamos. Y entonces se puso peor, porque un insurgente dijo “regalémosles un recuerdo”.

Empezó la bulla. Todas y todos hablando al mismo tiempo: que cuál recuerdo, que dónde lo va a poner, que no es buena idea, que sí es, porque la memoria es lo que importa porque por eso son buscadoras. Viera que no tienen memoria, pues se rinden, se desmayan.

Entonces las mujeres, con esa mala costumbre que tienen las mujeres de acabar las discusiones cuando apenas se está poniendo buena la cosa, dijeron: bordados y muñecas. “Que lo sepan y lo recuerden que tienen familias acá”.

Los insurgentes, encabezados por el capitán, dijeron que no, que eso de muñecas y bordados es para niñas, que ya tienen juicio las madres buscadoras, que no están para andar jugando y con bordados otra vez, que de una vez no se puede creer. Las insurgentas se embravecieron, que eso no sirve pensar así, que porque son recuerdos, no juguetes ni adornos.

Y que sigue la discusión, pero ya revuelto todo, porque el insurgente que le tocaba la intendencia quemó los frijoles, y todo por andar en el chisme del regalo. Y, por un momento, hay una unión del común de mujeres y hombres, porque una cosa es, como quien dice, la chinga, y otra es el frijol quemado. Pero todos se consolaron comiendo tostadas y arroz estilo vietnamita. Pero era apenas una tregua, inestable como el temperamento del Trump. Así que, después de lavar los platos y darles de comer a los chuchos y a los gatitos, siguieron.

En eso apareció el SubMoy: “¿Qué tanto alegan?” Todos empezaron como quien dice a exponer el problema. “Ya párenle”, gritó el SubMoy. Todo quedó en silencio. Los varones esperando que el Sub hiciera honor a la solidaridad de género. Las mujeres esperando que tuviera bueno el juicio.

El SubMoy encendió un cigarrillo, quedó pensando. Después de un rato dijo: “hagan la lista de lo que hay que conseguir”.

Las insurgentas aplaudieron. Los insurgentes hicieron caras, pero no dijeron nada porque el arresto era comerse el frijol quemado.

Entonces, en todas las posiciones insurgentes, empezaron a darle a confeccionar regalos. A las carreras, porque ya estaba cerca la salida.

Y empezaron tarde por su culpa del capitán, que empezó con la bulla de que muñecas y bordados no, que eso es de niñas. Y además hizo una trinchera con las mesas y las sillas, y ahí estaban todos los insurgentes parapetados. Porque resulta que las insurgentas los atacaban con bolitas de lodo que, dicen, les enseñaron a hacer las del Comando Palomitas. Entonces tardaron reacomodando y limpiando.

Así que, si no se acompletan los regalos, va en su cuenta del capitán.

A mí ni me culpen. Yo sólo soy un escarabajo y caballero andante, el muy grande y memorioso “Don Durito de la Lacandona. A.C. de C.V. de I.I”. Y yo no tuve nada que ver. Pero yo lo miré todo. Y no les vengo a …

content:
Este jueves, integrantes de la Coordinadora por la Libertad de los Presos Políticos realizaron una acción de protesta frente a la Catedral Metropolitana de Buenos Aires. Se encadenaron a una de las columnas de la Catedral para exigir la libertad inmediata de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo, detenidos por participar de la movilización contra la reforma laboral del 11 de febrero.

La intervención buscó visibilizar también el agravamiento de las condiciones de detención de ambos trabajadores en el Complejo Penitenciario de Marcos Paz. Denunciaron la falta de atención médica, la suspensión de actividades educativas y recreativas y las restricciones a las visitas de organismos de derechos humanos.


Milton Tolomeo inició una huelga de hambre el pasado 8 de noviembre

 para reclamar respuestas frente a las condiciones de alojamiento y las vulneraciones de derechos que sufren en el penal.


El encarcelamiento de Milton y Eneas se inscribe en una política de criminalización de la protesta social que busca disciplinar a quienes salen a la calle y enfrentan las políticas del Gobierno. Frente a la Catedral, el encadenamiento convirtió el reclamo en una acción directa contra el silencio y la indiferencia. La exigencia sigue siendo clara: ¡Libertad inmediata a Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo! ¡Luchar no es delito!

title: HABAŞ ardından konuştuğumuz MESEM öğrencisi: Kalıbın altında kalabilirdim, patron kalıp için korktu
content:
Ekim Can Aslan [email protected]

HABAŞ Demir Çelik Fabrikasında meydana gelen ve 19 kişinin yaşamına neden olan katliamın ardından Ümraniye’de bir sanayi sitesinde MESEM öğrencileri ile bir araya geldik. Öğle arasında sohbet ettiğimiz MESEM öğrencileri, HABAŞ’ı duyduklarını ancak katliamın tam olarak nasıl meydana geldiğini anlamadıklarını söylüyor. Kendi çalıştıkları yerlerde her gün bir iş kazasıyla burun buruna geldiklerini anlatan MESEM öğrencileri, iş cinayetlerinin bir “sakatlık” veya “istisna” değil, bu düzenin kendisi olduğunu gözler önüne seriyor.

İlk önce üç kişilik bir arkadaş grubuyla sohbet ediyoruz. 11. sınıf motor mekanik ve elektik öğrencileri. HABAŞ’taki patlamayı duyup duymadıklarını sorduğumuzda Ahmet isimli genç kafa sallıyor: “Duyduk abi üzücü bayağı. Zor valla bu işler.” Kendi iş yerinde, iş güvenliği önlemlerinin alınıp alınmadığını sorduğumuz Ahmet, önlemlerin alındığını hiç sıkıntı yaşamadığını dile getiriyor. Ardından şu örneği veriyor: “Abi büyük araçlarla çalıştığımız için liftten düşme ihtimallerine karşı altlarına hep bir şey koyuyoruz.”

Ardından aynı arkadaş grubundan Hasan söze girip kendi ücretinden şikayet ediyor. Genellikle MESEM’de asgari ücretin yüzde 30’u olan devlet katkısına ek olarak iş yerinden haftalık cep harçlığı alan gençlerin aksine kendi iş yerinde sadece 8 bin 400 TL aldığını anlatıyor. Hasan’ın tepkisine karşın Ahmet, “Oğlum sen de biraz para biriktir, aldığın bütün parayı harcayıp söyleniyorsun sürekli” diye söze giriyor. Hasan bu cevaba sinirlenip herkesin aklına gelen o cevabı kendine has bir öz güvenle verince gülüşüyorlar: “Sekiz bin liranın ne kadarını biriktirip ne kadarını harcayayım?”

Hasan ve Ahmet’in yanından kalktıktan sonra beş kişilik bir MESEM’li grubuyla sohbet etmeye başlıyoruz. Onlara da HABAŞ’ı duyup duymadıklarını sorunca üçü birbirine bakıyor. İçlerinden biri söze girip duyduğunu ama ne olduğunu, neden olduğunu bilmediğini anlatıyor. HABAŞ’ta yaşanan katliamı anlattığımızda ise yüzleri düşüyor. Gruptan makine bölümü öğrencisi olduğunu öğrendiğimiz Burak söze girip kendi iş yerindeki bir olayı anlatıyor. Bir kalıp atölyesinde çalıştığını belirten Burak, geçtiğimiz günlerde atölyesinde vinçle bir kalıp taşınırken yaşadığı tedirginlikten bahsediyor:

“Geçtiğimiz günlerde atölyede vinçle kalıp taşınıyordu. Bu sırada ben de tam altında duruyordum. ‘Dedim şimdi düşer, şöyle kenara geçeyim.’ Geçtikten sonra kalıp düştü. Altında kalsam paramparça olurdum. Kalıp düştükten sonra iş yeri sahibi geldi. ‘Çabuk kaldırın kalıba bir şey olmuş mu bakalım’ dedi. Ustam araya girdi ‘Kalıbın Allah belasını versin benim burada elemanım var’ diye söylendi.”

İş cinayetlerinden ve iş kazalarından, gerekli önlemleri almayan iş yerlerinin sorumlu olduğunu söyleyen gençler, MESEM’in iş öğrenmek için en mantıklı yol olduğunu savunuyor. İş kazalarının ‘olabileceğini’ söyleyen gruba, dünyanın çeşitli yerlerinde, Avrupa’da meslek eğitimi görüp iş kazası geçirmeyen milyonlarca genç olduğunu söyleyince gençlerin cevabı “Aslında haklısın abi de…” oluyor. Kendi iş yerlerinde şu an 11-12 saat çalışan gençler “Okulda bölümünüzle ilgili yeterli atölyeler olsa bu sürenin yarısında da aynı işi öğrenmez misiniz?” sorusuna da “Öğreniriz” diye cevap veriyor. Sosyal medyada MESEM ve meslek liseleri üzerinden patronlara verilen teşviklere dair videolar gördüklerini, bu paraların öğrencilere verilebileceğini söylüyorlar.

Sohbet sırasında içlerinden birini, MESEM’li başka bir arkadaşları Ali görüntülü arıyor. O gün okula gelmeyen Ali’yle kısa bir muhabbet edip telefonu kapatıyorlar. Kapattıktan sonra Ali’nin kim olduğundan bahsediyor. Ali de makine bölümü 11. sınıf öğrencisiymiş ve bir CNC atölyesinde çalışıyormuş. Tezgahta çalışırken Ali’nin eldiveni makinenin matkabına dolanmış ve Ali sağ elinin üç parmağını bu şekilde kaybetmiş.

Milli Eğitim Bakanı Yusuf Tekin’in eylül 2026’da açıkladığı verilere göre sadece bir buçuk yılda iş kazası geçiren 9 bin 950 çocuktan birinin de Ali olduğunu anlıyoruz. Az önce kendi yaşadıklarını anlatan Burak, “Al sana iş güvenliği abi” diyor.

Bu örneğin ardından sohbet iş yerindeki iş güvenliği önlemlerine dair daha öfkeli devam ediyor. Bir MESEM’li ayda bir çalıştığı iş yerine giden İSG uzmanının göstermelik bir evrak doldurup gittiğini söylüyor. Diğeri ise kimsenin çalışma koşullarını denetlemediğini, İSG kurallarına dikkat edilmediğini.

title: Avrupa'da sendikalar ve genel grev tartışılıyor
content:
Fransa’da geçtiğimiz hafta milyonlarca emekçi ve genci bir araya getiren 5 Kasım grevinin ardından sendika yönetimlerinin tutumu tartışılıyor. Grev çağrısını geciktiren ve eylemleri rutin gösterilere indirgeyen sendika bürokrasileri, hükümetle sınırlı kazanımlar karşılığında uzlaşmakla eleştiriliyor. Buna karşı gençlik hareketi ile işçi sınıfını ortak meclislerde buluşturma, sermayeyi sarsacak radikal eylemler örgütleme ve mücadeleyi genel greve taşıma çağrısı öne çıkıyor.

Almanya’da 22 milyon insanın göç geçmişi bulunuyor; yeni bir rapor, entegrasyon sürecindeki başarıları gözler önüne seriyor. Ancak hükümetin tasarruf planları siyasi tartışmalara yol açıyor.

İngiltere’de ise gazetecileri hedef göstererek korku ve baskı yaratmakla suçlanan aşırı sağcı Tommy Robinson’ın iki ayrı taciz suçundan mahkum edilmesi, göçmen karşıtı hareketin geleceğine ilişkin tartışmaları yeniden alevlendirdi. Robinson’ın olası hapis cezası, yalnızca bir kişinin yargı süreci değil, sokaklarda ve sosyal medyada örgütlenen aşırı sağ hareketin geleceği açısından da önem taşıyor.

Sendika yönetimlerine yönelik meşru bir öfke var: Grev çağrısı yapmakta geciktikten sonra hareketin kontrolünü yeniden ele geçirmeye ve gençliğin sırtından hükümetle kırıntılar üzerinden pazarlık yapmaya çalıştılar. Ancak işçi hareketini ve onun örgütlerini devre dışı bırakmak da çıkmaz bir yol olacaktır. 17 Ekim’in ruhunu yeniden yakalamak ve ona çok daha büyük bir güç kazandırmak için yapılması gereken, tam tersine, işçileri ve örgütlerini mücadeleye katmak, bürokrasileri tabandan aşmak ve genel grevi örgütleyebilecek meslekler arası meclisler kurmak.

5 Kasım grev günü çelişkili bir nitelik taşıdı. Bir yandan, ekim ayının başında başlayan gençlik isyanıyla işçi hareketinin birleşmesi açısından önemli bir sıçramaya işaret ediyordu. Bugün, yalnızca 1 milyondan fazla insanı harekete geçirmekle kalmadı; aynı zamanda SNCF’nin (Fransız ulusal demir yolları) bazı birimlerinde ve ortaöğretimde yüksek grev oranlarına, enerji, petrokimya ve kamu hizmetleri gibi sektörlerde ise kitlesel seferberliklere sahne oldu.

Diğer yandan grev, “aktif” olmaktan çok uzaktı. Tam tersine, sendika yönetimleri bugünü sıradan, rutin bir grev gününe dönüştürmek için ellerinden geleni yaptılar. Daha da kötüsü, bu tarihi hareketi kendi bünyelerine katmak ve gençlerin sırtından pazarlık yapmak üzere kendilerini hükümetin muhatabı olarak konumlandırmak için kullanmaya çalıştılar. Üstelik bunu, lise öğrencilerinin isyanının başlamasından yaklaşık bir ay sonra, bu isyan acımasızca bastırılırken grev çağrısı yapmayı bekledikten sonra gerçekleştirdiler. Hatta 24 ve 31 Ekim tarihlerinde, şehirlerin dışına düzenlenen ve 17 Ekim’e kıyasla çok daha sıkı denetlenen ve kontrol altında tutulan yürüyüşlere meşruiyet kazandıran bir rol üstlendiler.

İhanet de gecikmedi: CFDT ve FO, hükümet kendilerine asgari ücrete (SMIC) 5 avroluk bir zam vermeyi kabul ettiği için artık grev çağrısı yapmama kararı aldı. Bu, seferberlik içindeki gençliğe ve ay sonunu artık getiremeyen bütün işçilere çekilmiş büyük bir el hareketinden başka bir şey değil. CGT ise hareketin tabanından gelen baskıya daha duyarlı davranarak mücadelenin içinde kalmayı sürdürüyor ve 17 Kasım’da kamu ve özel sektör çalışanlarını kapsayan yeni bir seferberlik günü çağrısı yapıyor. Ancak gerçekten genel ve devamlı bir grev inşa etmek için hiçbir ciddi imkanı seferber etmiyor.

Dolayısıyla sendikal örgütler, işçi hareketinin stratejik konumlarının tam merkezinde yer alıyor. Bu işçi taburlarının mücadeleye katılması olmaksızın iktidara karşı stratejik bir zafer kazanmayı düşünmek mümkün değildir. Öte yandan, son 10 yıldaki işçi mücadelelerinde tabandaki sendikacıların son derece ilerici tutumlarına ilişkin pek çok örnek bulunuyor. Yalnızca son birkaç haftaya bakacak olursak, Le Havre, Saint-Denis, Paris, Toulouse ve Saint-Avold’da polis karşısında lise öğrencilerini savunan sendikacıları ya da eğitim emekçilerini hatırlayabiliriz. Bunlar yalnızca birkaç örnek. Zafere ulaşmak için sendikacıların ve işçilerin büyük çoğunluğunu, kendi bürokratik yönetimlerini aşma mücadelesine katmayı başarmak gerekiyor. Buna CFDT ve FO’nun tabanındaki sendikacılar da dâhil. Onlara, yöneticilerinin kendi çıkarlarına ihanet ettiğini göstermek gerekiyor. (…)

Bu mücadeleyi yürütmenin aracı, farklı sektörlerin meclislerde bir araya gelmesi. Bunun amacı da henüz harekete geçmemiş işçilere ve tabandaki sendikacılara ulaşmak, sendika bürokrasilerinin kontrolü ele geçirmesine …

title: Uysal: Art's unifying and healing power can contribute to peace
content:
Theatre in Turkey is increasingly drifting away from its essence, influenced not only by longstanding structural problems but also by the political climate. Even plays that claim to be political remain under the influence of Turkish nationalist ideology.


The launch of the Peace and Democratic Society Process has sparked public debate about the role of art in the struggle for peace and the experiences of the past. For years, plays featuring racist rhetoric targeting the Kurdish people and other communities under the influence of war have been staged. The new process has also brought discussions about the need to transform the language of art.


Theatre director and dramaturg Abdullah Uysal spoke to ANF about the current state of theatre in Turkey and the role of art in the struggle for peace.


'Theatre is a technically and economically demanding profession'


Abdullah Uysal said that theatre has been affected by the cultural erosion experienced particularly under the rule of the Justice and Development Party (AKP), emphasizing that the problems facing theatre have economic, social and political dimensions.


Uysal said: "What is the state of theatre in Turkey? The situation is actually good, but at the same time, it isn't. It is difficult to fully grasp the cultural erosion that has taken place over the past 25 years, particularly under AKP rule, and its consequences. Theatre is already a technically and economically demanding profession. You create a work, an artistic aesthetic, and you need spaces in which to present it. You sell tickets to audiences who come to those spaces. This is directly connected to society's entire network of relationships and its economic and sociological structure. Theatre naturally finds its audience in places where people are comfortable, economic difficulties are not overwhelming and democracy is not under threat. People can create opportunities to relax and devote time to themselves. This directly affects theatre. Tickets are sold, and you can bring your work to audiences.


However, Turkey has struggled with economic problems since its establishment. Over the past 25 years, particularly under AKP rule, the economy has deteriorated dramatically and is now in a very poor state. As a result, theatre practitioners have either been forced to scale down their productions, performing in smaller venues with capacities of 30, 20 or even 15 people, or to reduce their expenses significantly.


For example, productions with large casts are no longer being staged. Look at what is being produced today: one-person plays, musical cabaret-style performances and stories that do not challenge audiences intellectually but instead distract them from everyday life. These are often what might be called 'cheesy' productions, built around cheap, stale narratives.


The popularity and celebrity culture that have emerged with the use of social media, along with people's reactions to momentary events, have changed the reasons audiences choose certain performances. There is a group in Turkey that claims to be producing theatre, and their tickets sell out. Let me give you an example. A simple story that has been adapted into films since the 1970s, staged perhaps 20 times and turned into television series is currently being performed in Turkey. They stage it in venues seating between 3,000 and 5,000 people, with tickets costing 5,000 Turkish lira, and every performance is sold out. Some viewers may even remember a theatre performance in Turkey where arguments broke out because people complained, 'I can't see my seat.' If you showed footage of that performance to someone abroad, they would conclude that Turkey has no audience problem and that theatre is thriving."


Uysal also said: "Yet at the same time, we hear that many theatre venues in cities across Kurdistan and in Turkey's major metropolitan areas are closing because of economic difficulties. As economic, political and class contradictions deepen in Turkey, and the cultural divide widens alongside them, it becomes increasingly difficult to speak of theatre's continued existence.


This raises a fundamental question: What is theatre, and what is not? Theatre, as we understand it, means producing works of art that touch society and have the power to transform it. It should enable people to look at communities, individuals, women, ecology, animals and the world with renewed hope, or give them the strength to change the world. Unfortunately, this kind of …

author: Unknown
title: New book documents unique plant diversity in the Hevsel Gardens in Amed
content:
A new scientific book exploring the plant life and ecological diversity of the historic Hevsel Gardens has been presented in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). Titled

“Species and Habitats – Flora of Hevsel”

(

Türler ve Habitatlar Florası: Hevsel

), the publication is based on years of field research and aims to help document and preserve the city’s natural heritage.


The book launch took place at the Çand Amed Culture and Congress Center. It was organized by the Amed Metropolitan Municipality and the local coordination board of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB). Attendees included Co-Mayor Emin Ay, City Council Co-Chair Dilan Aydın, scientists and representatives of TMMOB.


Years of research into the plant life of the Hevsel Gardens


The Hevsel Gardens stretch between Amed’s historic city walls and the Tigris River. As part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site “Diyarbakır Fortress and Hevsel Gardens Cultural Landscape,” they hold both cultural, historical and ecological significance.


The new book examines the vegetation and botanical diversity of this cultural landscape. Prof. Dr. A. Selçuk Ertekin and Dr. Zeki Kanay played particularly important roles in the scientific research. Their studies were supplemented by field observations from TMMOB members, local residents familiar with the area and people from the surrounding region. The publication thus combines scientific research with local knowledge of the plant life and habitats of the Hevsel Gardens.


Ay: Everyone must take responsibility for the Hevsel Gardens


At the book launch, Co-Mayor Emin Ay honored Ertekin’s scientific work by presenting him with a commemorative plaque. In his speech, he highlighted the historical significance of the Hevsel Gardens and the Tigris River. He said both have been closely linked to Amed’s development for thousands of years and have sustained the livelihoods of its people for generations.


At the same time, Ay criticized the ongoing destruction of the landscape, which he blamed on the policies of those in power. He stressed that protecting the Hevsel Gardens was therefore not solely the responsibility of public institutions but a shared responsibility of society as a whole. “Just as a mother protects and cares for her child, we must all protect and preserve the Hevsel Gardens,” Ay said.

title: Gülengül: The state protects capital and considers it its duty to do so
content:
The explosion that occurred on Monday at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory in İzmir’s Aliağa district, killing 19 workers and injuring 11 others, has once again brought workplace deaths in Turkey into the spotlight. According to the monthly report published by the Workers’ Health and Work Safety Assembly (İSİG), 193 workers lost their lives in work-related incidents in October alone.


İSİG’s periodic reports indicate that at least six workers die in workplace incidents every day in Turkey on average. Despite these deaths, the government continues to ignore warnings rather than ensure workers’ health and safe working conditions.


Seyfettin Gülengül, a member of the Labor Commission of the DEM Party’s Istanbul Provincial Organization, spoke to ANF about the underlying causes of workplace deaths, which have once again come to public attention following the deadly incident at the HABAŞ factory.


‘An average of six workers die every day’


Gülengül stated: “First of all, it must be pointed out that an average of six workers die in workplace incidents every day in Turkey. Let us look at the fatal workplace accidents that have occurred at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory and its port facilities in İzmir’s Aliağa district over the years.


November 16, 2007:

 İlyas Kırdı was killed and ten others were injured when an artillery shell exploded during scrap sorting operations.


August 24, 2008:

 Kutbettin Özkaya lost his life after being crushed beneath a 2.5-ton iron block that slipped from a crane.


2013:

 Two separate accidents occurred within a month, claiming the lives of Olgar Öner, who was killed when a cable snapped, and Engin Solmaz, who was electrocuted.


April 27, 2017 (Kocaeli):

 Nail Demirci was killed in an explosion involving an LPG tanker.


July 26, 2018:

 Evren Erik was seriously injured in an explosion at a steel furnace and died on August 3.


2018:

 Hasan Bostancı lost his life after falling from a dust collection chimney.


August 14, 2020:

 Subcontracted worker Şaban Karaca was killed after becoming trapped between steel blocks.


October 7, 2020:

 Kadir Özdemir fell to his death while working at height without a safety line.


November 6, 2020:

 Port worker Raif Çatan, who was not equipped with a life jacket, fell into the sea and drowned.


August 28, 2022:

 Oktay Eryılmaz died in hospital after falling from a crane.


January 11, 2024:

 Kemal Özdemir was killed when a metal coil fell on him.


October 21, 2026:

 Hakan Doğan fell to his death from a height of eight meters while working on a ladder.


November 5, 2026:

 Eyüp Eğinli lost his life when a tire on a piece of heavy machinery exploded.


November 9, 2026:

 Eighteen workers were killed and 15 others injured when an overhead crane broke loose, triggering an explosion.


So, are all these factories not inspected? They are. In fact, reports are prepared on many of them. However, there is a fundamental problem: Occupational health and safety specialists are paid by the employers receiving their services, meaning the companies or institutions themselves. That is how the law works.”


‘The state protects capital’


Gülengül stated that the government protects capital, saying, “The state protects capital and considers it its duty to do so. It sides with the powerful under the pretext that investors create employment.”


Referring to the Labor Minister’s remarks, Gülengül continued: “Why did the minister speak this way? Let us recall that statements such as ‘Death is inherent in the nature of this work’ or ‘Accidents are inherent in its nature’ were made by the then Prime Minister following the mining disaster on May 13, 2014, in the Soma district of Manisa, which claimed the lives of 301 miners. The same mentality and the same government are still in power today. That is how I interpret the minister’s remarks.”


‘We must have a greater say in the democratization of the country’


Seyfettin Gülengül stated that the DEM Party has been working on the issue of workplace deaths for years: “As the DEM Party, we have stood in solidarity with the families of workers who have lost their lives for years, just as we have in many other areas, and we have stood alongside them on the ground. Our parliamentary representatives also raise these problems, legal shortcomings and injustices in parliament. However, as I have said, correcting certain laws, regulations and similar issues requires the democratization of the country and greater …

title: Women demonstrate in Istanbul for the release of sick and elderly female prisoners
content:
Outside the Çağlayan Palace of Justice in Istanbul, MATUHAYDER (Association for Solidarity and Cooperation with Families of Prisoners and Convicts in the Marmara Region) called for the release of sick and elderly women prisoners. The demonstration, held under the slogan “Freedom for Women Prisoners,” was part of activities marking November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The protest focused on inadequate medical care in Turkish prisons and the repeated denial of release to prisoners who have completed their sentences.


Sultan Bozkurt, a relative of a political prisoner and a member of the Kurdish Peace Mothers Council in Istanbul, criticized the continued imprisonment of political prisoners despite the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. She stressed that seriously ill prisoners, in particular, must be released immediately.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b16b7a07_20261113141156_2026-11-13-istanbul-matuhayder-hasta-tutsaklar-icin-eylem-1.mp4


Life-threatening illnesses under prison conditions


MATUHAYDER board member Elif Taşdöğen drew attention to the situation in the women’s prisons in Sincan, Gebze, Kayseri-Bünyan and Bakırköy: “Many imprisoned women require increased medical care due to their age or serious illnesses but do not receive adequate treatment. Others remain in prison even after completing their sentences because their release is repeatedly postponed.” Taşdöğen described it as unacceptable to continue holding women with life-threatening illnesses in prison conditions that fail to ensure proper medical care.


Women must be able to shape peace


Referring to the ongoing peace process, Taşdöğen emphasized that women must not be regarded merely as those affected by political decisions but must actively participate in shaping a peaceful society. “Women must build peace not behind prison walls, but at the heart of society and in every sphere of life, through their own strength and free will,” she said.


Taşdöğen called for the release of Evin Zapsu, Pınar Tikit, Havva Ak, Hatice Yıldız, Fatma Tokmak and Çiğdem Özlü, along with all other sick women prisoners. “Where women are not free, peace remains incomplete. We insist on women’s freedom, peace and the collective building of a democratic society,” she stated.


The demonstration concluded with applause and slogans.

author: Unknown
title: Telling life stories, preserving names in Qandil - III
content:
Martyr Taylan left behind seven or eight notebooks and numerous poems. In one of his notebooks, he had also written a note addressed to whoever might one day edit his writings: “I just write. I write without any particular order. I hope the person who edits this later won't be upset with me. This was all I could do. I could have chosen not to write anything at all. But I felt it was my duty, and that is why I wrote.”


Munzur Diyar, a member of the Martyrs' Studies Committee whom we met in Qandil, said that he came across these lines when Taylan's diaries reached the committee. Diyar and his comrades collect notebooks, letters, photographs and testimonies left behind by guerrillas, preparing some of them for publication as books. However, not every completed work reaches readers.


“Tell our child’s story too”


Families have repeatedly criticized the committee’s television programs. Diyar recounts how relatives pointed out that while the programs featured the life stories of certain guerrilla fighters, their own family members, who had lost their lives many years earlier, were overlooked. They asked: “Our children also lost their lives years ago. Why aren’t there any programs about them?”


In response to this criticism, the committee changed its approach. Whereas individuals had previously been selected for the broadcasts, the committee decided to present the life stories of martyrs in chronological order from then on.


Documenting the lives of 700 martyrs


The idea for this program came from a young guerrilla who had never known his father. His father had joined the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party) six months before he was born. When the young man was around 21 or 22, he proposed preparing a program documenting the lives of martyrs individually. He continued this work for approximately ten years, producing programs about the lives of nearly 700 martyrs.


The program covered the lives of those who died in 2012, beginning with the first month of the year and proceeding chronologically. Diyar said that once they completed 2012, they moved on to 2013 and planned to continue with subsequent years. Rather than selecting particular individuals for programs, they aim to document as many lives as possible.


Diyar said that the committee also prepares radio broadcasts and written works alongside its television programs. However, the committee places particular importance on diaries written by guerrillas themselves and memoirs they wrote about one another. These account for a significant proportion of the texts the committee is working to publish as books.


Preparing biographies


Diyar said that the committee holds approximately 1,700 diaries that could be published as books. Some are only 20 or 30 pages long and are being prepared for publication alongside the diaries of other martyrs. Others are long enough to fill several volumes on their own. Taylan's notebooks are among these works.


The committee also began preparing biographies of guerrillas who fell after 2020. According to Diyar, their latest plans involve expanding this work to cover everyone, with the aim of documenting each person's life story as far as their research resources allow.


Building a digital archive


Publishing the diaries requires a considerable amount of work. Diyar explained that the writings cannot simply be printed as they are. They must first be edited and organized into a readable format. Yet even when the texts are ready for publication, their distribution is not guaranteed. The committee has been able to publish some of the works in Europe, while obstacles have prevented their publication in Turkey.


For this reason, committee members have begun building a digital archive intended to be accessible to anyone interested. They plan to publish both the books and other materials from their collection on a website that has not yet been launched. However, disagreements have arisen with publishers who insist that the books should be printed before being made available digitally.


“Publishers may want to print and sell books. But that is not what matters to us. Our primary goal is for the people to learn about the martyrs. Once the texts are published, anyone who wishes to print them is welcome to do so.”


Memorials for those without graves


The graves in the cemeteries of Qandil and other areas account for only a small proportion of those who have lost their lives in the course of the armed struggle. “We are talking about 27,000 martyrs …

author: Unknown
title: Three ISIS members killed in Pirde
content:
Iraqi security forces killed three suspected members of the Islamic State (ISIS) and arrested another suspect during a military operation in Pirde, in Kirkuk province, on Friday evening. The Iraqi Security Media Cell announced the operation, citing the Armed Forces High Command.


The operation took place at around 8 p.m. local time, based on intelligence gathered by military intelligence. After detecting the movements of a suspected ISIS group, Iraqi army aviation units carried out an airstrike on the group’s location. The operation was conducted within the area of responsibility of the 32nd Infantry Brigade of the 8th Division.


Before the airstrike, security forces had blocked access roads to Pirde and deployed additional military vehicles to the area. Gunfire and explosions were reported in the surrounding area. According to Iraqi authorities, a man suspected of transporting the three people who were killed was also arrested. Searches of the operation area initially continued.


The operation is part of a series of Iraqi military operations targeting remaining ISIS networks in Kirkuk province. As recently as November 9, Iraqi fighter jets struck suspected ISIS positions in the Zaytun Valley, destroying an underground hideout. Despite its military defeat in Iraq in 2017, ISIS remains active through sleeper cells, particularly in territories disputed between Baghdad and Hewlêr (Erbil).

author: Unknown
title: TJK-E: We will stop femicide and wars through organised struggle
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdish Women's Movement in Europe (TJK-E) released a statement on the occasion of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.


Calling for stronger organizing and collective political resistance, TJK-E warned of increasing violence against women, criticized the militarization of European societies and called for a determined confrontation with patriarchal power structures. It also urged women’s organizations and anti-war movements to actively support the peace and democratic society process. The full statement by TJK-E Coordination reads as follows:


Violence against women is increasing worldwide


“We are living through a historic moment marked by profound transformations and multiple crises. We stand at a crossroads where the old order is collapsing and the new has yet to emerge. At such historic turning points, politics and organized action take on far greater meaning and importance. With this awareness, as we mark November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, we must strengthen our organization and make our political power more effective.


Violence against women, which we regard as the longest war in history, is not decreasing but continues to intensify. Worldwide, 840 million women and girls are affected by male violence. According to official figures, at least 83,000 women and girls were killed by men in 2024. We know that the actual number is significantly higher. In countries such as Germany, France and Italy, a woman is killed by her partner or former partner every three days. In France, 61 percent of the women murdered last year had previously contacted the police and sought help. In Germany, a woman experiences violence at the hands of her partner every four minutes. Violence against women occurs predominantly not on the streets or in the workplace, but within their own homes.


Statistics on sexual and digital violence, as well as misogynistic attacks, also show a worrying increase. At the same time, there is a growing number of cases in which men drug their wives and hand them over to other men to be raped, as in the Pelicot case in France. These cases reveal the horrifying extent of rape culture. As TJK-E, we too declare: Shame must change sides! It is not the survivors who should feel ashamed, but the perpetrators. They must be held publicly accountable, their crimes exposed and punished. Every form of violence against women must have consequences!


Combating patriarchal violence within Kurdish society as well


Violence against women within Kurdish society in Europe has also reached a level that we must describe as femicide. In Germany alone, three Kurdish women have been deliberately murdered in the past two months by men from whom they had separated. This selfish, ruthless and murderous mentality, which regards women as property, refuses to recognize their independent will and does not even hesitate to deprive its own children of their mothers, poses a threat to society as a whole.


There can be no justification for violence against women, especially femicide. The fundamental problem is the culture of male domination. We will intensify our efforts to combat this life-destroying culture, which produces perpetrators and takes human lives, and to foster a culture of equal and free coexistence, as well as a democratic family culture.


Both in our homeland of Kurdistan and in Europe, where we live today, we feel the profound social upheavals arising from the multiple crises of capitalist modernity. The global hegemonic powers are once again attempting to dismantle the old order through war and destruction and establish a new one. At no point since the Second World War has so much been invested in wars or so much money spent on weapons. Never before have European governments so openly diverted public funds into the pockets of the arms industry and paved the way for militarism in order to prepare their societies for war.


Women must actively shape the peace process


As Kurdish people, we know very well what war means. For 200 years, we have been fighting for our existence and freedom against the genocidal regime of capitalist modernity. Today, we are striving to pave the way for a transition from armed conflict to democratic and legal struggle. At a time when sabers are rattling across the world, Abdullah Öcalan has initiated a historic process through his Call for Peace and Democratic Society, aimed …

author: Unknown
title: Women Defend Rojava launches new campaign phase in Germany
content:
At a meeting last weekend, the Women Defend Rojava campaign discussed its future activities in Germany and launched a new phase of its work. In light of political developments in Syria and the growing threats to the achievements of the women’s revolution in Rojava, the activists intend to expand their information and solidarity efforts. Their first major initiative will be a month of action dedicated to feminist self-defense, centered around the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25.


According to the campaign, the discussions were based on a comprehensive assessment of the political and social situation in northeastern Syria. The activists pointed to the increasing impoverishment of the population and the persistent threat posed by Islamist groups, including the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS). Under these circumstances, they stressed, international efforts to defend the women’s revolution are particularly important.


Bringing the experiences of Rojava to wider society


In the coming period, Women Defend Rojava plans to raise public awareness of the social achievements of the revolution and the current political situation in Syria. To this end, the campaign intends to use informational materials, digital media and local events. The activists particularly aim to reach people beyond existing solidarity networks and connect the experiences of Rojava with social struggles in Germany.


“Above all, our aim is to inspire people around us, in our neighborhoods and cities, with the ideas of the revolution in Rojava and to create hope,” the activists explained following the meeting. In light of political developments in Germany, they also see a growing need for social alternatives in the country. They believe that the experiences of Rojava could offer valuable insights into addressing social and political challenges.


“We want to show that the revolution in Rojava is relevant to us here as well, and that it can offer our society answers and perspectives for solving our own problems.” Planned activities include seminars, lectures and delegation visits for those interested in learning firsthand about the social structures and developments in Rojava.


Month of action for feminist self-defense around November 25


The month of action for feminist self-defense announced by Women Defend Rojava begins in November, coinciding with the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25. Through self-defense workshops, film screenings, neighborhood cafés and creative activities, the activists aim to highlight different forms of resistance to patriarchal violence. These activities will also explore the concept of self-defense and its connection to the autonomous women’s structures in Rojava.


As part of the initiative, the campaign has published a new brochure on autonomous women’s structures in Syria. The publication is intended to support political education efforts and make the experiences of women’s organizing accessible to a wider audience.


Joint cultural activities as part of organizing efforts


Alongside political discussions, the meeting also featured collective cultural activities. Participants watched

Jinwar

, a film by the Rojava Film Commune about the women’s village of the same name in Rojava. The program also included group singing and games. The campaign announced plans to continue its internationalist solidarity efforts in the coming months and encourage more people to support the women’s revolution in Rojava.

title: Hatimoğulları: Now is the time to expand the ecological struggle
content:
Tülay Hatimoğulları, co-chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), criticized the UN Climate Summit COP31 in Antalya as a platform serving the interests of governments and major corporations. At a press conference with representatives of the ecology movement, she accused those responsible of using climate protection as a pretext to legitimize an economic system based on limitless growth, exploitation and the destruction of the natural foundations of life.


Hatimoğulları spoke during protests against the official climate conference. Alongside COP31, ecological and civil society organizations in Antalya are organizing an alternative People’s Climate Summit. The DEM Party politician welcomed activists who had traveled from various regions and paid particular tribute to the resistance of women, farmers, young people and workers against the destruction of their living environments.


“COP31 is nothing but exploitation”


The DEM Party co-chair fundamentally questioned whether the very governments and corporations whose economic and energy policies have significantly contributed to worsening the climate crisis could be expected to develop solutions to it. “COP31, jointly organized by the state and capital, represents the domination of capital over life, the exercise of power over society and the plundering of nature. It is nothing but exploitation itself,” Hatimoğulları declared.


The climate crisis, she said, is not merely an ecological problem but a reflection of social power relations. “The climate crisis is a question of class exploitation and justice. Its root cause is the insatiable greed for profit.”


In this context, she also recalled the deaths of 19 workers at HABAŞ in Izmir. Hatimoğulları blamed the disregard for occupational safety regulations and the profit-driven interests of company management for the deadly working conditions. She noted that workers who sought to protest against these conditions had reportedly been attacked by the gendarmerie. She stressed that the DEM Party stands alongside the workers and supports their struggle for decent working conditions.


Ecological destruction in Kurdistan is increasing


A particular focus of Hatimoğulları’s speech was the expansion of mining and energy projects in Kurdistan. She warned that the economic exploitation of the Kurdish provinces was accelerating precisely at a time when peace and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question were being discussed. “Today, as we discuss the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the guns have fallen silent, we are witnessing capitalism and capital rapidly advancing into the Kurdish provinces,” she said.


The DEM Party co-chair noted that the government and major corporations have already carried out extensive interventions in nature in the Aegean, Black Sea and Mediterranean regions, and are now increasingly targeting the Kurdish provinces with similar projects.


“This is not merely about exploiting natural resources, but also about destroying long-established social environments and ways of life,” she underlined.


“The village where we were born, the summer pastures we migrate to, and the fields where we earn our livelihoods are living environments. For the people who live there, this land, these trees and natural resources are neither objects nor commodities.” Hatimoğulları pointed to protests against controversial energy and mining projects in Sur in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), Varto and Diyadin, as well as ecological resistance movements in Artvin, Gümüşhane, Uşak and the highlands of the Black Sea region.


She described these struggles as manifestations of a common conflict between the livelihoods and well-being of local communities and an economic policy that subordinates natural resources to corporate exploitation. She sharply criticized Law No. 7554, which ecological initiatives have described as the “Plunder Law.” Remarking that the legislation was passed despite resistance from social movements and the parliamentary opposition, she said: “We do not recognize Law No. 7554. As far as we are concerned, it is null and void.”


Oil discoveries in Gabar and contradictory climate policies
